docs.title: RIQS Business Documentation
docs.text:
Welcome! These docs explain what RIQS does, who can do what, and how to do it, in plain language.

They are written for everyone: new team members (developers, testers, analysts, product owners, support) and clients.

Technical architecture is documented separately (coming later).

docs.title: How to write and update these docs
docs.text: These docs explain what RIQS does, who can do what, and how to do it, in plain language. Anyone should be able to read a page and understand it: a new team member, a tester, a product owner, or a client.

docs.title: Writing rules
docs.text:
1. Plain English. Short sentences. One idea per sentence. Explain any special word the first time you use it, or link to the Glossary.
  2. Write for the user, not the code. Say "Click Save", not "the form calls the save mutation". Do not mention repositories, code, APIs, database names, or ticket numbers.
  3. Use the names the user sees on screen. Write button and menu names in bold, exactly as shown in the app.
  4. Use tables for "who can do what" and numbered steps for "how to do it".
  5. Be honest. If something is planned and not built yet, say so. If behaviour is unclear, add it to the "Open questions" section at the bottom of the page, not as a guess in the main text.
  6. Keep pages short. If a page grows past what a person can read in about 10 minutes, split it.
  7. Same layout everywhere. Every module page uses the template below, so readers always know where to look.

docs.title: Where permissions come from
docs.text:
The Roles & Rights sheets (RIQS wiki, "Roles & Rights" pages) are the source of truth for who can do what. They win over the feature list when the two disagree.

The app does not always match them yet. Pages always describe the intended rule from the sheets. If the app behaves differently, do not write that on the page. Add it to App permission gaps (internal file in the repository) (internal fix list, not for clients).

docs.title: Role names
docs.text:
Always use these names (see Roles & permissions):

RiQS Administrator · Group Administrator · Administrator · Power User · Management · Professional

Function roles (given on top of a role): CIRS Officer, Complaint Officer, Ideas Officer, Feedback Officer, Fault Officer, Hint Officer, Equipment Officer, RiQS-Pedia Officer, Auditor, Committee, Unit Manager, Organisation Manager.

"Unit" is the business word. In some places of the app a unit is also shown as a "Client". Always write "unit" and mention the other name only in the glossary.

docs.title: Module page template
docs.text:
# <Module name>

> **In one sentence:** <what this module is for>.
> **Menu:** <where to find it in the left menu>  ·  **Status:** Live | In progress | Planned

## What it is
2–4 short paragraphs. What problem it solves, in everyday words. An everyday comparison helps.

## Key terms
| Term | Meaning |

## Who uses it
| Role | What they typically do here |

## How it works
The main flow, step by step, from start to finish (e.g. create → assign → do → review → report).
A simple flow line is welcome, e.g. `Draft → Published → Completed`.
Include the statuses an item can have and what moves it from one to the next.

## How to …
One sub-section per common task. Each one:
### How to <task>
**Who can do this:** <roles>
1. Step
2. Step
**Result:** what the user sees afterwards.

## Rules to know
Bullet list of business rules: limits, who gets notified, what happens on delete, approval rules, audit-safe mode, etc.

## Who can do what
Permission table: rows = actions, columns = the six roles (plus function roles where relevant).
Use ✅ allowed · ❌ not allowed · text for conditions (e.g. "own unit only").

## Connected modules
How this module uses or feeds other modules, with links.

## Open questions
Things that are not yet clear. Remove a line when it is answered.

docs.title: AI features
docs.text: In one sentence: RIQS uses artificial intelligence (AI) to translate content into each user's own language and to answer questions about documents in RiQS-Pedia. Menu: No own menu. AI appears as buttons inside other modules (Translate, Ask RiQS AI). · Status: Mixed: see the table below

docs.title: What it is
docs.text:
Many RIQS customers have teams who speak different languages. A task written in German may be read by a colleague whose first language is Portuguese. AI translation lets that colleague see the text in their own language with one click.

The second feature is an AI assistant called RiQS AI. You ask it a question in normal words, for example "What is our procedure for cleaning the autoclave?". It searches the documents in RiQS-Pedia and answers. It also shows the documents its answer comes from.

AI use costs money for the provider, so it is measured in tokens (small pieces of text). Each organisation buys a token budget as part of its subscription.

docs.title: Status at a glance
docs.text: Feature Where Status AI translation (Translate button) Monitoring, To-Dos, Training, Process Guide, Forms (Configurator) details Live RiQS AI chat for documents RiQS-Pedia (Ask AI button in the toolbar) In progress: built in the new web app, rollout to be confirmed Ask RiQS AI about a device Equipment details (Ask RiQS AI button) Planned: the button is shown but does not do anything yet Token budget and usage Organisation and unit subscription pages Live

docs.title: Key terms
docs.text: Term Meaning AI translation Automatic translation of text written by people (tasks, answers, remarks) into the reader's language. Native language The language set as "native language" in your user profile. Translation always goes into this language. RiQS AI The AI assistant that answers questions about RiQS-Pedia documents. Sources The documents RiQS AI used for its answer. They are listed under the answer. Token A unit used to measure AI use. Longer texts use more tokens. Language tokens The token budget for AI translation. Manual tokens The token budget shown on the subscription page for the AI assistant (see Open questions).

docs.title: Who uses it
docs.text: Role What they typically do here RiQS Administrator Sets token budgets for offline customers; checks usage. Group Administrator Uses translation and RiQS AI. Token rights: see Open questions. Administrator Buys tokens and shares them between units; checks usage. Power User Buys extra tokens for the unit; checks the unit's usage. Management Uses translation and RiQS AI. Professional Uses translation and RiQS AI.

docs.title: AI translation (Live)
docs.text:
Open item → Translate → text shown in your language → Translate again → original text

  1. You open a task, To-Do, training, process guide or form that someone wrote in another language.
  2. You click Translate.
  3. RIQS checks that:
  4. you have a native language in your profile
  5. the language is supported
  6. your unit has tokens left
  7. the subscription is active
  8. The texts on the page are shown in your language. The button is highlighted while the translation is shown.
  9. Click Translate again to go back to the original text.

docs.title: RiQS AI chat (In progress)
docs.text:
Open RiQS-Pedia → Ask AI → choose documents (optional) → ask → answer with sources

  1. In RiQS-Pedia, click the AI button in the toolbar. The RiQS AI panel opens: "Hello! I am RiQS AI".
  2. Optional: click Select Document to limit the question to certain documents.
  3. Type your question and send it. The answer appears word by word.
  4. Under the answer, Sources shows which documents were used.
  5. You can ask follow-up questions in the same chat. When you close the panel, the chat starts fresh next time.

docs.title: How to translate content into your language
docs.text:
Who can do this: all roles who can open the item 1. Make sure your native language is set in your user profile. 2. Open the task, To-Do, training, process guide or form. 3. Click Translate.

Result: The text is shown in your native language. Click Translate again to see the original.

docs.title: How to ask RiQS AI a question (In progress)
docs.text:
Who can do this: users who can open RiQS-Pedia 1. Open RiQS-Pedia and click the AI button in the toolbar. 2. Optional: choose documents with Select Document. 3. Type your question in Type here and send it.

Result: RiQS AI answers and lists its Sources.

docs.title: How to check or buy tokens
docs.text:
Who can do this: Administrator (organisation); Power User (own unit); RiQS Administrator (organisations licensed offline) 1. Open the organisation or unit details and go to the subscription section. 2. Check Language Tokens and Manual Tokens: used and remaining. 3. Use the subscription update to buy more tokens.

Result: The new balance is available right away. The purchase is added to the next bill. See the subscription page for prices and rules.

docs.title: Rules to know
docs.text:
• Translation goes into your native language only. If your profile has no native language, you see "User native language not found".
  • Supported languages:
  • English, German, French, Italian, Spanish, Portuguese
  • Russian, Ukrainian, Serbian, Croatian, Albanian, Bulgarian
  • Turkish, Czech, Polish, Romanian, Hungarian
  • Tamil, Tagalog
  • Translations are not saved into the item. The original text stays as written. A translation you already made on the page is reused without using new tokens.
  • No tokens, no translation. When the token budget is used up you see "Token limit exceeded". When the subscription has expired, translation stops too.
  • Budgets exist at organisation and unit level. The organisation buys tokens and can share them out to units.
  • Low-balance alerts. The feature list says admins and Power Users get an alert when tokens run low.
  • RiQS AI and confidentiality. The rule is that RiQS AI only uses documents you are allowed to see (see Open questions).
  • RiQS AI does not keep chat history after you close the panel. Every question and answer is still logged for usage counting.

docs.text:

docs.title: Cockpit (Workflow-Navi)
docs.text:
In one sentence: Your personal "my work" page: every task and document that is waiting for you, from every module, in one list. Menu: Workflow-Navi · Status: Live

Workflow-Navi as a Professional sees it: open tasks with group, orderer and due date. Screens show test data.

docs.title: What it is
docs.text:
RIQS has many modules, and each one can give you work: a To-Do, a guide to follow, a training, a checklist from the shift plan, a maintenance job, a document to approve, a form to sign. Without a central place you would have to check every module every day.

The Cockpit is that central place. Think of it as your inbox for work. Whatever any module assigns to you shows up here, with its due date. You click a line and RIQS takes you straight to the right page to do the job. When the job is done, it leaves the list.

In the left menu this page is called Workflow-Navi. Some documents and these docs call it the Cockpit. Both names mean the same page.

The Cockpit has two tabs:

  • Tasks: things you must do (To-Dos, guides, trainings, shifts, checklists, maintenance, reports, surveys).
  • Documents: documents that need your action: Documents to approve, Read confirmation and Forms to sign.

Leads (administrators, Power Users and Management) can switch from Personal to Unit to see the open work of everyone in the unit.

docs.title: Key terms
docs.text: Term Meaning Workflow-Navi (Cockpit) The menu name of this page: your list of open work. These docs also call it the Cockpit. Task One piece of work assigned to you, created by another module. Group The kind of task, shown with an icon: Guide, Training, To-do, Maintenance, Reporting module, Shift, Template, Survey. Reporting items also show their type (CIRS, Complaint, Idea, Feedback, Fault, Hint). Orderer The person who gave you the task. Assigned to The person or people who must do the task. Due date When the task must be done. Shown as Due today, Due tomorrow, "Due in X days", or "Overdue by X days". Personal view Only your own tasks and documents. Unit view Tasks and documents of the other people in the selected unit. Read confirmation A document you are asked to read and confirm.

docs.title: Who uses it
docs.text: Role What they typically do here RiQS Administrator Looks across organisations with the organisation and unit filter and the Unit view. Can delete tasks and documents from the overview. Group Administrator Works their own list and uses the Unit view to follow up units. Administrator Works their own list and uses the Unit view to follow up units. Power User Works their own list and checks the unit's open work in the Unit view. Management Works their own list and uses the Unit view to follow up the unit. Professional Works their own list: opens each task and completes it.

docs.title: How it works
docs.text:
1. Another module creates work for you. For example a To-Do is assigned, a guide is shared, a shift with a guide is planned for today, a document needs your approval.
  2. It appears in your Cockpit. Shift and checklist tasks appear on the day itself (RIQS assigns them automatically each morning). Other tasks appear as soon as they are assigned.
  3. You open it. Click the line. RIQS opens the right page: the To-Do, the guide, the training, the maintenance details, the shift, the survey, or the document.
  4. You do it there. Complete the To-Do, finish the guide, fill in the form, approve the document, and so on.
  5. It leaves the list. Once it is done, the item disappears from your Cockpit and from the Unit view.

Assigned → Open in Cockpit → Done (leaves the list)

By default the list shows open tasks due from today up to 30 days ahead, plus anything still open from earlier (overdue). You can change the period with the date filter.

docs.title: How to see and do your work
docs.text:
Who can do this: All roles 1. Click Workflow-Navi in the left menu. The Tasks tab opens. 2. Look at the Due Date column. Overdue tasks are highlighted. 3. Click a task. RIQS opens the matching page. 4. Do the work and complete it there.

Result: The task is gone from your list when you return.

docs.title: How to handle documents
docs.text:
Who can do this: All roles 1. Open the Documents tab. 2. Choose Documents to approve, Read confirmation or Forms to sign. Each shows how many are waiting. 3. Click a document to open it, then approve, confirm reading, or sign.

Result: The document leaves the list once your action is recorded.

docs.title: How to search and filter
docs.text:
Who can do this: All roles 1. Type in Search by to search by title. 2. Click Filter. Choose a Group, an Orderer, Assigned to, or a Date range. 3. Click Apply filter. Each active filter is shown as a chip; remove a chip to undo it, or click Reset.

Result: The list shows only matching items.

docs.title: How to see the unit's open work
docs.text:
Who can do this: RiQS Administrator, Group Administrator, Administrator, Power User, Management 1. In the Cockpit, switch the view from Personal to Unit. 2. If you belong to several units, pick the unit.

Result: You see the open tasks and documents of the other people in that unit. The choice is remembered on this device.

docs.title: How to look at another organisation or unit (RiQS Administrator)
docs.text:
Who can do this: RiQS Administrator 1. Open the filter. 2. Choose an Organization and a Unit, then apply.

Result: The list shows that unit's items.

docs.title: How to delete tasks or documents from the overview
docs.text:
Who can do this: RiQS Administrator only 1. Tick the items (or Select all). 2. Click Delete and confirm.

Result: The items are removed from the overview.

docs.title: Rules to know
docs.text:
• Done means gone. An item stays in the Cockpit from the moment it exists until it is done.
  • Shift and checklist tasks appear on their day. They disappear as soon as they are completed, or after 24 hours if not.
  • A checklist stays until its last task is done, not its first.
  • Approvals with several approvers stay in each approver's list until the required number of approvals is reached.
  • Maintenance shows as one task, "Maintenance: equipment name", which opens the maintenance overview.
  • Reporting items (CIRS, complaints and so on) show the report card's title. Their due date is the earliest open To-Do or guide assigned to you for that report.
  • Surveys cannot be opened from the Cockpit once their due date has passed. You see "cannot access as due date has passed".
  • Personal shows only your own items. Unit shows only items assigned to other people in the unit.
  • Two Power Users of the same unit see the same items in the Unit view.
  • Notifications elsewhere: absence decisions show as a red dot and bell in the Shift Plan. Some menu entries, for example Equipment and Surveys, show a counter of new items.
  • Only the RiQS Administrator can delete items from the Cockpit, in both the regular version and audit-safe mode.

docs.title: Who can do what

docs.title: Configurator
docs.text:
In one sentence: The workshop where admins and unit leads build the reusable content that other modules run: guides, trainings, control task lists, equipment reports, interactive documents and surveys. Menu: Configurator · Status: Live

Configurator: one tab per template type (Guides, Trainings, Monitor, Equipment Reports, Interactive documents, Survey). Screens show test data.

docs.title: What it is
docs.text:
Many RIQS modules need ready-made content. A process guide needs its steps. A training needs its questions. A maintenance job needs a report form. A survey needs its questionnaire. The Configurator is where all these templates are made, kept and looked after.

Think of it as the unit's template cupboard. You build a template once, decide which organisations and units may use it, and from then on people use it in the daily modules: they follow the guide in Process Guide, take the training in Training, and so on. When something changes, you update the template here.

You open it with Configurator in the left menu. Older documents call it "Forms" or the "Module creator". It has six tabs, one per kind of template: Guides, Trainings, Monitor, Equipment Reports, Interactive documents and Survey.

Professionals do not use the Configurator. They only use what is built here.

docs.title: Key terms
docs.text: Term Meaning Module In this page, one template you build: a guide, a training, a monitor, a report, a document or a survey. Guide A step-by-step procedure with sections and tasks. Used in Process Guide and attached to shifts. Training A learning unit with multiple-choice questions and a pass mark. Used in Training. Monitor (control task list) A list of control tasks, for example with a rating scale. Used in Monitoring. Equipment report A report template filled in during equipment maintenance. Used in Equipment. Interactive document A form people fill in online. See Interactive documents. Survey A questionnaire template. Used in Surveys. Sector and Topic Labels that sort guides, trainings and monitors. Both are required. Availability The organisations and units that may use a template. You can choose single units or all units of an organisation. Qualification The pass mark of a training, as a percentage from 0 to 100. Drafted / Published The two states of a report, document or survey template. A draft can still change. A published template is in use. Version Each change to a published template creates a new version. Older versions stay viewable.

docs.title: Who uses it
docs.text: Role What they typically do here RiQS Administrator Builds and maintains templates for any organisation. Can delete in audit-safe mode. Group Administrator Builds templates for the organisations in the group and shares them across units. Administrator Builds templates for the organisation and its units. Power User Builds and maintains templates for their own unit. Management Builds and maintains templates for their own unit. Professional Does not open the Configurator. Uses the finished templates in other modules.

docs.title: How it works
docs.text:
Guides, trainings and monitors

  1. Create. Click Create Guide, Create Training or Create Monitor. Fill in the details and the content.
  2. Share. Choose the organisations and units that may use it.
  3. Save. It appears in the list and can be used straight away in the matching module.
  4. Maintain. Preview, edit, copy, deactivate or delete it from the row menu (⋮).

Equipment reports, interactive documents and surveys

Drafted → Published → (edit) → new version

  1. Create. Click Create Report, Create Document or Create Survey. A builder opens.
  2. Build. Set the layout (cover page, table of contents, deviation overview). Add sections and content: headlines, text, images, tables, system data, summaries, signatures, attachments, deviations. Add questions: multiple choice, rating scale, Likert scale, open text, dropdown, ranking, yes/no and date.
  3. Save as draft. The template is Drafted. You can still change it.
  4. Approve. Use Approve on the draft. It becomes Published and can be used.
  5. Change later. Editing a published template creates a new version.

Filled-in reports based on these templates have their own statuses (for example Pending, Generated, Partially Approved, Approved, Signed). These are described on the module pages that use them.

docs.title: How to find a template
docs.text:
Who can do this: RiQS Administrator, Group Administrator, Administrator, Power User, Management 1. Click Configurator in the left menu. 2. Choose a tab, for example Trainings. 3. Type in the search field, or open the filter to narrow the list (for example by status, unit or tag).

Result: The list shows matching templates with title, status, unit and dates.

docs.title: How to create a guide
docs.text:
Who can do this: RiQS Administrator, Group Administrator, Administrator, Power User, Management 1. On the Guides tab, click Create Guide. 2. Enter the Sector, the title, the Topic and an optional description. 3. Choose where it is available: one or more organisations and units, or all units of an organisation. 4. Add sections and tasks. Attach files or forms if needed. 5. Click Save.

Result: The guide is listed on the Guides tab and can be used in the Process Guide and attached to shifts in the Shift Plan.

docs.title: How to create a training
docs.text:
Who can do this: RiQS Administrator, Group Administrator, Administrator, Power User, Management 1. On the Trainings tab, click Create Training. 2. Fill in the training information: title, sector, topic, description, the Qualification (pass mark, 0–100) and any files. 3. Add at least one question. Each question needs answer options and at least one correct answer. 4. Click Save.

Result: The training is listed and can be assigned in Training.

docs.title: How to create a monitor (control task list)
docs.text:
Who can do this: RiQS Administrator, Group Administrator, Administrator, Power User, Management, if the unit has the Monitoring module 1. On the Monitor tab, click Create Monitor. 2. Fill in the details and availability. 3. Add the control tasks, for example a rating scale with from, to and step values. 4. Click Save.

Result: The list can be used in Monitoring.

docs.title: How to build and publish a report, document or survey
docs.text:
Who can do this: RiQS Administrator, Group Administrator, Administrator; Power User and Management only at unit level 1. Open Equipment Reports, Interactive documents or Survey. 2. Click Create Report, Create Document or Create Survey. 3. Build the layout, sections and questions. Use Preview to check it. 4. Save it as a draft. 5. When it is ready, open the row menu (⋮) and click Approve.

Result: The template is Published and ready to use.

docs.title: How to preview, edit, copy or delete a template
docs.text:
Who can do this: see Who can do what 1. Find the template and open the row menu (⋮) in the Action column. 2. Choose Preview, Edit, Copy or Delete. 3. For interactive documents you can also choose Upload to RiQS-Pedia (not for drafts).

Result: - Copy creates a new, separate template. Report, document and survey templates can only be copied once published, and only if your unit is on the template. - Edit of a published report, document or survey creates a new version. - Delete removes the template, if it is not in use (see Rules).

docs.title: How to delete several templates and download a list
docs.text:
Who can do this: see Who can do what 1. On Guides, Trainings or Monitor, tick the templates you want to delete. Only templates you may delete can be ticked. 2. Click the delete button and confirm. 3. To download a report of the list, use the download button.

Result: The selected templates are removed. The download gives you the list as a file.

docs.title: Rules to know
docs.text:
• Templates in use cannot be deleted. A guide, training or monitor that is still used by active guides, trainings or tasks cannot be selected for deletion. Deactivate it instead, or end its use first.
  • Who can delete what: RiQS Administrators, Group Administrators and Administrators can delete any guide, training or monitor. Power Users and Management can delete only the ones they created themselves.
  • Editing guides, trainings and monitors made by others: RiQS Administrators, Group Administrators, Administrators and Power Users can edit those created by people below them (subordinate persons). Management can edit only their own.
  • Creating guides depends on the unit: guide creation must be switched on for the unit (RiQS Administrators are not limited by this).
  • Creating monitors needs the Monitoring module in the unit's package.
  • Power User and Management create report, document and survey templates only at unit level. Only administrator roles can share templates more widely.
  • Field limits: the Sector is required (up to 100 characters); title and descriptions up to 1000 characters; a training needs at least one question with a correct answer.
  • Audit-safe mode: only the RiQS Administrator can delete.

docs.title: Equipment
docs.text:
In one sentence: Keep a register of every device in your units, plan and record its maintenance and validation, and keep its manuals, contacts and reports in one place. Menu: Equipment · Status: Live (RiQS AI on the device page is in progress)

Equipment Management: the device list, with tabs for Reports and Locations. Screens show test data.

docs.title: What it is
docs.text:
Medical practices and clinics depend on devices: sterilisers, ECGs, fridges, glucose meters. Many must be serviced or checked on a fixed schedule, and auditors want proof that this happened. The Equipment module is the logbook for all of them.

Each device gets a record with its name, location, serial and other numbers, supplier, manufacturer, contacts and documents. On that record you plan maintenance (servicing) and validation (checking that it still works correctly). RIQS reminds the right people when an event is due, collects their answers and forms, and asks for approval if needed. External service companies can complete their part through a secure link, without a RIQS account.

Each device also has a QR code. Print it and stick it on the device so it is easy to identify.

docs.title: Key terms
docs.text: Term Meaning Equipment One device or piece of equipment, registered in one unit. Location A place where equipment stands, such as a room or building, with an address. Exact location is free text for the precise spot, for example "Shelf 2, left". Maintenance A planned service of a device (shown as M in the list). Validation A planned check that the device still works as required (shown as V in the list). Event One scheduled maintenance or validation. The list shows the Latest event and Next event. Preparation time How many days (1–30) before the due date the event starts, so people have time to prepare. Executing group The users who must carry out the event. Approvers The users who must approve the result, when an approval process is required. Equipment Officer A function role. The officer looks after all equipment of a unit (unit level) or of the whole organisation (organisation level). Equipment Manager A person responsible for one specific device. Supplier The service provider of the device, chosen from the unit's suppliers. External user A person from a service company who completes an event through an emailed link. Equipment report A report built from a report template, for example a validation report. A preparation report may have to be done first. UDI number Unique Device Identification number, used for medical devices.

docs.title: Who uses it
docs.text: Role What they typically do here RiQS Administrator Supports clients. Can see and manage all equipment. Cannot create fault reports. Group Administrator Manages equipment in the group's organisations and names Equipment Officers at organisation and unit level. Administrator Manages equipment across all units and names Equipment Officers at organisation and unit level. Power User Manages the unit's equipment, locations and maintenance, and names unit-level Equipment Officers. Management Adds, edits and copies equipment, plans maintenance, names Equipment Managers for devices, and carries out events they are assigned to. Cannot delete. Professional Views and adds equipment and locations, downloads QR codes, reports faults, and carries out events they are assigned to. Edits equipment and plans events only as Equipment Officer or Equipment Manager. Equipment Officer Manages equipment, locations, events and reports for their unit or organisation, and names unit-level Equipment Officers, whatever their role. Equipment Manager Plans and edits events for the devices they manage.

docs.title: How it works
docs.text:
1. Set up locations. On the Location tab, add the rooms or sites where equipment stands.
  2. Register the device. Add the equipment with its location, supplier and numbers. RIQS creates its QR code.
  3. Attach what belongs to it. Add files (such as manuals and forms from RiQS-Pedia), guides, report templates and photos. Name Equipment Managers.
  4. Plan events. Schedule maintenance and validation, once or repeating, with executing users, approvers and optional external service providers.
  5. Get reminded. On the start day of the event (due date minus preparation time), RIQS emails the responsible people. If a form is attached, it also creates a task for the executing users, due on the event date.
  6. Carry out and record. The executing users (or the external user) complete the attached guide, form or template and click Mark as done, with remarks and attachments.
  7. Approve. If approval is required, the approvers review and approve. Then the event is completed.
  8. Report. Download lists and reports for audits.

An event moves through these statuses:

Pending → Submitted → In progress → Done

Status Meaning What moves it on Pending Planned, nobody has answered yet. The first executing user marks it as done. Submitted At least one answer is in, but not all, or approval is still needed. More answers, or approvals. In progress All executing users answered; waiting for approval. The approvers approve. Done Completed. It can no longer be deleted. —

Without an approval process, the event is Done as soon as all executing users have answered (or as soon as one person answers if no executing users were named). An event documented as a past maintenance or past validation is Done right away.

docs.title: How to add a location
docs.text:
Who can do this: All roles 1. Open Equipment and go to the Location tab. 2. Click Add Location. 3. Enter a Name and Remarks. Enter the address, or pick a service provider's address from the unit's contacts. You can place a pin on the map and add photos. 4. Click Save.

Result: The location appears in the list and can be chosen for equipment.

docs.title: How to add equipment
docs.text:
Who can do this: All roles 1. Open Equipment and click Add Equipment. 2. Fill in the required fields: unit (Select Unit), Equipment Name, Location and Suppliers. 3. Add optional details: Exact location, Serial number, Internal number, Installation number, UDI number, Year of manufacture, Date of purchase, Placing in service, Manufacturer, category and sub-category, Additional information fields, Contacts and Remarks. 4. Optionally choose which user qualifications (User additional information) are needed to work with the device. 5. Save.

Result: The equipment appears in the list. Its QR code is created in the background.

docs.title: How to edit, copy or delete equipment
docs.text:
Who can do this: see Who can do what 1. Open the equipment. 2. Click the More (⋮) menu and choose Edit, Copy or Delete. 3. Copy opens a new equipment form pre-filled from this one. 4. To change only the location, use Update location on the Info tab. Every change is kept in the Location Log.

Result: The record is updated, copied or removed. Deleting equipment also deletes all its events, and the people involved get an email about the deleted events.

docs.title: How to schedule a maintenance or validation
docs.text:
Who can do this: RiQS Administrator, Group Administrator, Administrator, Power User, Management and Equipment Officers. Professionals only as Equipment Officer or Equipment Manager of this device. 1. Open the equipment and go to the Maintenance or Validation tab. 2. Click Schedule. 3. Choose Maintenance or Validation. 4. Set the Date and Preparation time. For a repeating event, set the recurrence. To record something that already happened, choose to schedule a past maintenance or validation. 5. Choose the Executing users. Optionally turn on the approval process, choose the type, and pick Approvers. 6. Optionally attach a guide, a RiQS-Pedia Form, an Interactive Form or a report template, and choose external service providers. Only items already assigned to this device are offered. 7. Optionally require an electronic signature, then click Save.

Result: The event appears under Upcoming Events. A past event appears under Past Events as completed, without reminders or tasks.

docs.title: How to complete a maintenance or validation
docs.text:
Who can do this: The executing users assigned to the event. The RiQS Administrator can also complete events. 1. Open the event from the equipment, your Cockpit or the reminder email. 2. Complete the attached guide, form or template, if there is one. 3. Click Mark as done, add remarks and attachments, and submit.

Result: Your answer is saved and the status moves on. If approval is required, the approvers can now Review and approve.

docs.title: How an external service provider completes an event
docs.text:
Who can do this: The service provider named on the event 1. The provider opens the link from the email. 2. RIQS sends a verification code to the provider's email address. The provider enters it. 3. The provider sees the equipment information and its events, and can download the QR code. 4. On the event, the provider clicks Mark as Done, adds remarks and files, and saves. This is not possible before the event's start date.

Result: The provider's answer is stored on the event under the supplier response.

docs.title: How to name Equipment Officers and Equipment Managers
docs.text:
Who can do this: Organisation-level officers: RiQS Administrator, Group Administrator, Administrator. Unit-level officers: the same, plus Power User and Equipment Officer. Managers: RiQS Administrator, Group Administrator, Administrator, Power User, Management and Equipment Officer. 1. To name officers, click Assign Officer on the equipment list. Choose organisation level or unit level, the user type and the users. 2. To name an Equipment Manager for one device, use the row menu on the equipment list. Any user except the RiQS Administrator can be chosen. 3. Save.

Result: The people appear in the responsibility section of the equipment details and get the rights of their function.

docs.title: How to download the QR code and reports
docs.text:
Who can do this: QR code: all roles. Reports: RiQS Administrator, Group Administrator, Administrator, Power User, Management and Equipment Officers. Professionals only as Equipment Officer or Equipment Manager. 1. For the QR code: open the equipment, click More (⋮) and choose Download QR code. The label shows the numbers that exist for the device (device, serial, internal). 2. For one device: click Download report and choose Report (XLSX) or Report (DOCX). 3. For the list: on the Equipment tab, click Download report and choose this unit or all units. 4. Equipment reports made from templates are on the Reports tab. Filter by status: Created, Completed, Partially approved, Approved, Signed.

Result: The file is downloaded. The Excel list includes location name, address and exact location.

docs.title: How to report a fault
docs.text:
Who can do this: All roles except RiQS Administrator (see Rules) 1. Open the equipment. The Info tab shows a fault summary (New Malfunction, In Progress, Completed). 2. Click Create fault report.

Result: RIQS opens the fault report form in Incident Reports. The fault report shows the device's exact location.

docs.title: Rules to know
docs.text:
• Required to add equipment: unit, name (up to 100 characters), location and supplier. Year of manufacture must be a 4-digit year from 1900 to this year.
  • Reminders: on the event's start day (due date minus preparation time) RIQS emails the responsible people. If a form is attached, a task is created for the executing users, due on the event date.
  • Past events are saved as completed and trigger no emails or tasks.
  • Approval types: a standard approval needs at least one approver. The four-eye and six-eye principles need at least two.
  • Done events cannot be deleted. Select all and bulk delete only include events that are not done.
  • Deleting a location first checks whether anything still uses it. If so, deletion is blocked.
  • Deleting equipment deletes all its events and emails the people involved.
  • Fault reports: RiQS Administrators cannot create them. If the unit's fault management is set to "unit without insight", Administrators and Group Administrators cannot either.
  • Audit-safe mode: only the RiQS Administrator can delete equipment, locations, events or reports. Others deactivate instead. See Audit-safe mode.
  • Manuals and RiQS AI: manuals attached from RiQS-Pedia are prepared for RiQS AI, so the AI can answer questions about them in RiQS-Pedia. The Ask RiQS AI button on the equipment page is visible but not working yet (in progress).
  • Planned: planning a special shift in the Shift Plan directly from a maintenance or validation event. Not built yet.

docs.title: Interactive documents and forms
docs.text: In one sentence: Interactive documents and PDF forms let an organisation turn its paper forms (checklists, protocols, records) into controlled digital forms that people fill in, sign and keep as a traceable record. Menu: built in Configurator → tab Interactive Documents; stored and filled in RiQS-Pedia → tabs Interactive Documents and PDF-Forms · Status: Live

docs.title: What it is
docs.text:
Many tasks in a practice end with a form: a cleaning record, a device check, an onboarding checklist, a consent sheet. On paper these get lost, are filled in with old versions, and nobody can prove who signed what.

RIQS offers two kinds of digital forms:

  • PDF forms: an existing fillable PDF is uploaded to RiQS-Pedia. People fill in its fields in the browser.
  • Interactive documents: a form built from scratch in the Configurator with building blocks (questions, tables, text, signatures). It looks like a document but behaves like a smart form: required questions, deviations, automatic data about the person, unit or device, and a clean PDF at the end.

Think of the form as a stamp pad: the master stays in the library (approved and versioned, like any RiQS-Pedia file). Every time someone fills it, RIQS makes a copy (a "response") with their answers, name and time. The master never changes by filling.

Both kinds of form can be used on their own from RiQS-Pedia, or attached to work in other modules (a Day Planner checklist, an equipment maintenance, a guide task, an incident report).

docs.title: Key terms
docs.text: Term Meaning Interactive document A form built in the Configurator and stored in RiQS-Pedia. PDF form A fillable PDF uploaded to RiQS-Pedia with Upload Pdf-forms. Response One filled copy of a form, saved with the person's name and date. The master form is not changed. Draft A response that is saved but not finished. Only drafts can still be changed. Section / element The parts of an interactive document: sections hold elements such as questions, text, tables, images, signature fields. Deviation An answer that is "not OK" (for example "No" to "Fridge temperature in range?"). Deviations are numbered and can be collected in a Deviation Overview. Module information / System Data An element that fills itself with data about the user, the unit or the equipment when the form is opened. Header / footer Optional lines on every page that show file name, created by, edited by, approved by and version, taken from RiQS-Pedia. Electronic signature A signature applied when the form is completed: Simple (SES), Advanced (AES, with 2-factor code) or Qualified (QES, legally equal to a handwritten signature; needs an identity check by AutoIdent or VideoIdent). Send for signature Asking other people (internal users or external e-mail addresses) to sign a filled form. Standard form A form handed out by the organisation to several units. Each unit fills its own copies.

docs.title: Who uses it
docs.text: Role What they typically do here RiQS Administrator Can build, upload, approve and fill forms like an administrator, sees all responses, and is the only role that may delete responses and inactive forms in audit-safe mode. Group Administrator / Administrator Build organisation-wide interactive documents, upload them to RiQS-Pedia, approve them, hand them to units. Power User Build and upload unit forms, approve them, assign them, see all responses of the unit. Management Build unit forms, approve unit forms (Standard and 4 eyes), assign forms for completion, fill forms, see their own responses. Professional Fill the forms assigned to them and see their own responses. Can upload PDF forms but not build or upload interactive documents. RiQS-Pedia Officer Approves forms like any other library file.

docs.title: How it works
docs.text:
A. Build (interactive documents only). In Configurator → Interactive Documents, click Create Document. Give it a title, logo, optional header and footer, then add sections and elements. Save it as a draft while you work. When it is ready, Approve it in the Configurator; it is then Published.

B. Put it in the library. In the Configurator row menu choose Upload to Riqs Pedia (PDF forms: in DMS choose Upload → Upload Pdf-forms). The normal upload steps follow: version, folder, electronic signature, approval principle, re-approval and key words. The form is Pending in RiQS-Pedia until it is approved.

C. Share or attach. Once approved, the form is shared with units, groups or people (see RiQS-Pedia), or attached to a task in another module.

D. Fill. A user opens the form, fills it and either Save as Draft or saves it as complete. If a signature is required, they sign (or Send for signature to others).

E. Keep the record. Each completed response is stored, can be downloaded as a PDF, and shows who filled it and when. The module it was attached to (for example the checklist) is marked as done.

Status of the master interactive document in the Configurator:

Drafted → Published (then uploaded to RiQS-Pedia: Pending → Approved)

Status of one response:

Draft → Completed → (Pending signature) → Signed

docs.title: How to build an interactive document
docs.text:
Who can do this: RiQS Administrator, Group Administrator, Administrator; Power User and Management at unit level only (see table) 1. Open Configurator and the tab Interactive Documents. 2. Click Create Document. 3. Basic Information: enter the Template Title, optional Description, Template logo, and switch on Header / Footer if wanted. 4. Optional: Create Cover Page with text, images, tables, System Data, Document History, signature or confirmation elements. 5. Add Sections and fill them with elements: Question, text, headline, table, image, Attachment, summary, signature, confirmation, module information. 6. For each question pick the type: Multiple Choice, Rating Scale, Likert Scale, Open Text, Dropdown (typed or from Excel), Ranking, Binary, Date Selection. Mark it mandatory or optional. 7. Optional: Add Table of Content, Add Deviation Overview, Add Comment Log. 8. Use Preview to check the layout. Click Save Draft while working, Save when finished. 9. In the list, choose Approve in the row menu.

Result: The template is Published and ready to be uploaded to RiQS-Pedia. Elements can be duplicated and moved; table cells can be merged and resized.

docs.title: How to upload an interactive document to RiQS-Pedia
docs.text:
Who can do this: RiQS Administrator, Group Administrator, Administrator, Power User, Management (not Professional) 1. In Configurator → Interactive Documents, open the row menu of a published template. 2. Choose Upload to Riqs Pedia. Group Administrators first choose the organisation. 3. Go through the steps: Version, folder, Electronic Signature, Approval Principle, re-approval, Key Words. 4. Click Save.

Result: "Template sent to RiqsPedia for approval." The document is Pending in the RiQS-Pedia Approval tab.

docs.title: How to upload a PDF form
docs.text:
Who can do this: every role 1. In RiQS-Pedia, click Upload → Upload Pdf-forms. 2. Choose a fillable PDF. 3. In Electronic Signature, decide if the filled form must be signed, pick the Signature type and, if wanted, 2 Factor authentication required. 4. Finish the approval, re-approval and key word steps and click Save.

Result: "File sent for approval." The form appears in PDF-Forms once approved.

docs.title: How to fill a form from RiQS-Pedia
docs.text:
Who can do this: people the form is shared with (see table) 1. Open RiQS-Pedia and the tab Interactive Documents or PDF-Forms. 2. In the row menu choose Fill Interactive Document or Fill Form. 3. For a standard form, first choose the folder where your copy is saved. 4. Fill in the fields. Mandatory questions must be answered. 5. Click Save as Draft to continue later, or Save to finish. 6. If a signature is required, the button is Sign Form: choose Sign or Send for signature.

Result: "Form filled successfully". Your response is stored with your name. A draft can be reopened and finished later.

docs.title: How to sign or send a form for signature
docs.text:
Who can do this: the person filling the form 1. On a form that needs a signature, click Sign Form. 2. To sign yourself: enter the 5-digit code if 2-factor is on, then sign in the signing window. 3. To ask others: choose Send for signature, pick Internal users (with filters by organisation, unit, user group, designation) and/or type External users e-mail addresses, then Send document.

Result: The PDF is created at the moment of signing and contains the answers, attachments, deviations, comments and the signature. Forms waiting for your signature appear in Workflow-Navi under Forms to be Signed.

docs.title: How to see the responses of a form
docs.text:
Who can do this: see table (Management and Professionals see only their own) 1. Open RiQS-Pedia → Interactive Documents. 2. Open the responses of a document. The panel Interactive documents Response lists each response with status and the person who completed it. 3. For PDF forms, open the form's history list to see the filled copies. 4. Open or Download a response.

Result: You see who filled the form, when, and what they answered. Downloads are always PDF.

docs.title: How to fill a form that is attached to a task
docs.text:
Who can do this: the person assigned to the task 1. Open the task in its module (Day Planner checklist or shift, equipment maintenance, guide task, To-Do, incident report). 2. Click the attached form. 3. Fill and save it as above.

Result: The response is linked to the task, and the task shows the form as completed.

docs.title: Rules to know
docs.text:
• The master never changes by filling. Every fill creates a new response. To change the form itself, edit it in the Configurator (interactive) or upload a new version (PDF), and approve it again.
  • Completed responses cannot be edited. Only drafts can be changed.
  • Old drafts and new versions. If the form was updated after you started a draft, RIQS warns: "Template is updated. Please fill the updated template instead of old one."
  • Approval comes first. A form can only be filled after it is approved in RiQS-Pedia. It follows the same approval, re-approval and sharing rules as every other library file.
  • Signature settings belong to the form. They are set at upload and apply to every response. With AES or QES, the separate 2-factor switch is not needed (it is part of the signature).
  • QES identity check is done once per user (AutoIdent or VideoIdent) and reused for later signatures.
  • PDF output. The PDF keeps the exact layout, answers, attachments, deviations, comments and the header/footer data. With a signature, the PDF is created at signing.
  • Who sees responses. Management and Professionals see only their own responses. RiQS Administrators, Administrators, Group Administrators and Power Users see all responses in their area.
  • Editing the released original. A released PDF form can never be edited. A released interactive document can be edited only by users authorised in the Configurator (never by Professionals); the edit creates a new version.
  • Deactivating a form removes it from new use in workflows. A form still used by an open task cannot be deactivated.
  • Deleting responses. In regular mode, the RiQS Administrator and authorised persons with the Group Administrator, Administrator or Power User role may delete completed responses and inactive forms; in audit-safe mode only the RiQS Administrator.
  • Configurator editing rights follow the role ranking: a Power User can only edit templates created by a Power User or lower.

docs.text:
• RiQS-Pedia: stores, versions, approves and shares every form; tabs Interactive Documents and PDF-Forms.
  • Configurator: where interactive documents are built (tab Interactive Documents). The same builder is used for Equipment Reports and Surveys.

docs.title: Open questions
docs.text:
1. RiQS Administrator and forms. The feature list says the RiQS Administrator cannot edit interactive documents or fill forms; the rights sheet says "Yes, if authorised in the Configurator" for editing and "Yes" for filling. This page follows the rights sheet; please confirm.
  2. Interactive documents in To-Dos. The rights sheet says the completion of an interactive form can be assigned through the To-Do module. Should To-Dos record interactive document responses the same way as PDF form responses, and is this planned?
  3. Interactive documents in Process Guide. Guides can attach interactive documents, but the answers are not written back to the guide task (only PDF form answers are). Is this intended?
  4. "Authorised persons". Which people exactly may delete or deactivate completed responses (officers? the person who filled it?)?
  5. Form type. The earlier app let uploaders mark a PDF form as Normal, Confidential or General. The current app does not offer this choice. Is it still needed, and what are the rules for Confidential and General forms?
  6. External signers. What does an external e-mail recipient receive, how long is the link valid, and can they see anything besides the form?

docs.title: Interface Manager
docs.text:
In one sentence: The Interface Manager moves large amounts of existing data into RIQS in one go: documents into RiQS-Pedia, and equipment, users and suppliers through Excel templates. Menu: Interface manager (the page is titled Integration Manager) · Status: Live

Interface manager (page title Integration Manager): imports for RiQS-Pedia, equipment, users and contacts. Screens show test data.

docs.title: What it is
docs.text:
When an organisation starts with RIQS, it usually already has a lot of data somewhere else: hundreds of documents on a shared drive or in SharePoint, a spreadsheet of devices, a list of staff. Typing all of that in by hand would take days. The Interface Manager is the "moving company" for this data.

It has two parts:

  • My Documents: copy files and folders into RiQS-Pedia, either from Microsoft SharePoint / OneDrive or from your own computer. RIQS then helps you group the files into document versions and set their RiQS-Pedia settings (approval type, review interval, signature) before they go live.
  • Data management: add or update equipment, users and suppliers in bulk. You download an Excel template, fill it in, upload it again, check the result in a preview table, and confirm.

Every import is first a draft. Nothing reaches the real modules until you click Complete migration. You can save a draft, leave, and continue later.

docs.title: Key terms
docs.text: Term Meaning Migration Copying data from outside into RIQS through the Interface Manager. Template An Excel file you download from the Interface Manager. It has the right columns for the data you want to import. Draft / saved import An import that is started but not completed. It is shown as Continue previous imports so you can resume it. Version group A set of files that are versions of the same document (for example "Hygiene plan v1" and "Hygiene plan v2"). In RiQS-Pedia they become one document with a version history. File list (Excel) An Excel file listing all uploaded documents. You can use it to rename documents and decide which files belong to the same version group. Preview table / review table The table shown after an upload. You check and complete the data here before you confirm. Organisation level / unit level Documents uploaded by an Administrator are organisation documents (versions 1.00, 2.00 …). Documents uploaded by a Power User are unit documents (versions 0.01, 0.02 …).

docs.title: Who uses it
docs.text: Role What they typically do here RiQS Administrator Supports clients during onboarding; can do every import. Group Administrator Imports or updates data for the organisations of the group. Administrator Main user: moves the organisation's documents, devices, staff and suppliers into RIQS at the start. Power User Imports and updates data for the own unit. Management Imports and updates documents, equipment, users and contacts / suppliers, like the Power User. Professional No access.

docs.title: Documents (RiQS-Pedia migration)
docs.text:
Upload files → Prepare version grouping → Check version groups → Configure files → Complete migration

  1. Upload. Choose the source: Log in with Microsoft (SharePoint / OneDrive) or Upload from your computer (a whole folder, or single files).
  2. Prepare version grouping. RIQS proposes which files belong together. You can improve this with the file list in Excel, or Skip and group manually.
  3. Document version groups. Check the groups on screen. Move a file to another group, take it out of a group, change its version number or order. Then confirm.
  4. Configure. In the review table, set for each file (or many files at once) the folder, file type, approval type, review interval, signature settings and the original upload date and uploader.
  5. Complete migration. RIQS creates the documents in RiQS-Pedia.

docs.title: Equipment, users and suppliers
docs.text:
Download template or current data → Fill in Excel → Upload → Complete the preview table → Complete migration

There are two actions for each kind of data:

Kind of data Add new Update existing Equipment Add New Equipment: empty template Update Existing Equipment: download of the current equipment data Users Add New User: empty template Update Existing User: download of the current user data Suppliers Add New Supplier: empty template Update Existing Supplier: download of the current supplier data

After the upload, the preview table shows every row. Some details cannot come from Excel and are chosen in the table:

  • Equipment: location, manufacturer, supplier and a RiQS-Pedia attachment. You can also enter the last maintenance or validation (responsible person and status). This becomes the Last Event in the Equipment module.
  • Users: unit, role, language, qualifications and permits, and Configurator permissions. A unit that has used all its user licences is marked Unit is at full capacity.
  • Suppliers: supplier category.

docs.title: How to migrate documents from SharePoint or OneDrive
docs.text:
Who can do this: RiQS Administrator, Group Administrator, Administrator, Power User, Management 1. Open Interface manager. Make sure the right unit is selected. 2. In Migrate Files, click Log in with Microsoft and sign in with your Microsoft account. 3. Choose the site. Then tick the files and folders you want to copy. 4. Click Start migration and wait for the progress window to finish. 5. Continue with "How to group versions" below.

Result: The selected files are copied into the Interface Manager as a draft. They are not yet visible in RiQS-Pedia.

docs.title: How to migrate documents from your computer
docs.text:
Who can do this: RiQS Administrator, Group Administrator, Administrator, Power User, Management 1. Open Interface manager and click Upload in the Upload Files card. 2. Choose Upload Folder (a whole folder, with its sub-folders) or Upload Files (one or more files). 3. Pick the folder or files and wait for the progress window. It shows the overall progress and the file being copied right now.

Result: The folder structure is kept. Files that cannot be migrated are listed with the reason (Why are … files being skipped?).

docs.title: How to group versions with Excel
docs.text:
Who can do this: RiQS Administrator, Group Administrator, Administrator, Power User, Management 1. In Prepare version grouping, click Download file list. 2. In the File Lists sheet, use the same Normalised document name for all versions of one document. Put them in order with Version sequence (1, 2, 3 …). Use Proposed group to move a file into another group. You can also add a File note. 3. Save the file. Click Upload completed file. 4. Check the groups in Document version groups. Fix anything you need by hand. Then click the confirm button.

Result: The version groups are built again from your Excel file, and you move on to the review table.

Not using Excel? Click Skip and group manually and do the grouping on screen.

docs.title: How to configure documents and complete the migration
docs.text:
Who can do this: RiQS Administrator, Group Administrator, Administrator, Power User, Management 1. In the review table, check each row. Use the row menu to change a single file. To change many files at once, select them and use the bulk update. 2. Set the Approval type (Standard, 4-Eye, 6-Eye), Interval duration, Re-Approval Process Duration, Signature type (SES, AES, QES) and, for QES, Authentication for QES (AutoIdent or VideoIdent). 3. If needed, change Upload date, Uploaded by and Uploader email so the original history is kept. 4. Click Save progress if you want to stop and continue later. 5. Click Complete migration and confirm.

Result: The documents appear in RiQS-Pedia with their versions, folders and settings.

docs.title: How to add or update equipment, users or suppliers
docs.text:
Who can do this: RiQS Administrator, Group Administrator, Administrator, Power User, Management 1. Open Interface manager. In the Equipment Management, User or Suppliers column, click Add New … or Update Existing …. 2. Click Download Template (add) or Download … Data (update). Fill in or change the Excel file. 3. Upload the file in the same window. 4. Complete the missing details in the preview table. Use bulk update to set the same value for many rows. 5. Click Complete migration and confirm.

Result: The records appear in the Equipment module, in Users, or in the supplier list of the unit. They work exactly like records created by hand.

docs.title: How to continue or delete a saved import
docs.text:
Who can do this: RiQS Administrator, Group Administrator, Administrator, Power User, Management 1. Open Interface manager. A saved import shows Continue previous imports with the date it was last saved. 2. Click it to go on where you stopped, or click Delete draft to throw the import away.

Result: When you delete a draft, its files and rows are discarded. Nothing moves into RIQS.

docs.title: Rules to know
docs.text:
• Nothing is final until you complete it. Uploaded data stays in a draft until you click Complete migration.
  • One document draft at a time. While a document import is saved as a draft, the Upload button is disabled. Continue or delete the draft first.
  • Maximum 1,000 files per folder or per file selection when you upload from your computer.
  • Unsupported files are never dropped silently. They are listed with a reason.
  • Automatic grouping is careful:
  • Files of different types (for example Word, Excel and PDF) are never grouped together.
  • Only a version or status ending is ignored when names are compared (for example "v2", "2.0", "final", "draft", a date).
  • An unclear ending is not grouped automatically.
  • Templates stay separate. A file whose name ends with "template", "vorlage", "modèle", "modele" or "modello" is always its own group. It never becomes a version of a normal document.
  • Version numbers depend on who imports.
  • Administrator: organisation documents, versions 1.00, 2.00 …
  • Power User: unit documents, versions 0.01, 0.02 …
  • Upload date can only be a date in the past, with no time. You can change it for one file or for many at once.
  • File type can only be changed for PDF files.
  • Review interval and re-approval apply to all files you select in a bulk update.
  • Users are updated by user ID. You cannot change a user's unit in an update import.
  • Select a unit first. You cannot start a migration until a unit is selected.
  • Who may import. Every role except Professional may use all Interface Manager actions. Professionals have no access.

docs.text:
• RiQS-Pedia: receives all migrated documents, with their version groups, folders and settings.
  • Equipment: receives new and updated equipment, including the last maintenance or validation event.
  • Users: receives new and updated users with their unit, role, language and qualifications. Unit licence limits apply.
  • Organisation & units (supplier list of the unit): receives new and updated suppliers under their category.
  • Tutorials and help: the Interface Manager has its own help videos and manual.

docs.title: Open questions
docs.text:
• Suppliers or contacts? The current app shows Suppliers (add / update supplier data). The rights sheet and older feature lists say "Contacts". These docs follow the app. Are they the same thing?
  • Approval status after migration. The feature list says migrated documents are approved automatically and skip the normal approval process. Please confirm this is still true in the current version.
  • Google Drive. Older feature lists mention migration from Google Drive. The current start screen only offers Log in with Microsoft. Is Google Drive still offered, or was it dropped?
  • Rights sheet vs feature list. The rights sheet gives Management (and every role except Professional) all Interface Manager actions. The feature list names only Administrator and Power User for migration and for adding equipment, users and suppliers, and Group Administrator, Administrator and Power User for bulk updates. These docs follow the rights sheet. Please confirm Management should have full access.
  • Group Administrator and RiQS Administrator versions. It is not clear which version numbering (1.00 or 0.01) applies when these roles import documents.

docs.title: Monitoring
docs.text:
In one sentence: Plan regular control checks for a unit, record on the day how well each one was fulfilled, and see at a glance what has been checked and what has not. Menu: Monitor · Status: Live

Monitor, tab Overview: the control tasks due today and how many are done. Screens show test data.

docs.title: What it is
docs.text:
A practice has things that must be checked again and again: the fridge temperature, the emergency kit, the cleaning of a room, the sterilisation log. Monitoring turns these into control tasks that appear on the unit's calendar on the right days. On the day, a responsible person records how well the task was fulfilled (for example 80%), who did the work, and any remarks.

Think of it as the inspection sheet on the back of a door, where someone ticks and scores each item every day, except that RIQS reminds people, moves forgotten checks to the next day, and shows management the fulfilment level of the whole unit.

The questions themselves are kept in a control task list, built in the Configurator (tab Monitor). Monitoring is where you schedule these lists for a unit, answer them, and review the results.

Which one do I use? Process Guide, Monitoring and Open Items are easy to mix up.

Use … when … Example Process Guide a job has several steps that people must work through "Morning opening: 8 steps" Monitor you want to check regularly how well something is done, with a score from 0 to 100% "Fridge temperature checked: daily" Open Items one thing must be done by one date "Replace the broken lamp in room 2 by Friday"

Rule of thumb: many steps → Process Guide. A score → Monitoring. A single job → Open Items. If a control check shows a problem, create a To-Do from it (see How to create a To-Do from a control task).

docs.title: Key terms
docs.text: Term Meaning Control task list (Task list) A set of control tasks built in the Configurator, for one topic. Control task One check in the list, with a text, an optional keyword, and a scale (by default 0–100% in steps of 20%, with labels such as "Incomplete" and "Complete"). Schedule (assign) Putting selected control tasks on a unit's calendar, once (due date) or repeating. Answer (control) Recording the result on the day: fulfilment level, executing user(s), remarks. Controlled / Uncontrolled A task that has been answered / has not been answered yet. Fulfilment level The score given when answering. The overview shows the average. Executing user The person who actually did the work being checked. Distinct list One row per scheduled control task (the whole series). The all view shows the same rows with a status switch and delete.

docs.title: Who uses it
docs.text: Role What they typically do here RiQS Administrator Supports clients; can schedule, answer and delete in any unit. Group Administrator Oversees control tasks across the organisations of the group. Administrator Oversees control tasks across the units of the organisation. Power User Sets up the unit's control plan, answers the daily checks, follows the fulfilment level, deletes old schedules. Management Schedules and updates control tasks for the unit, answers them, switches schedules active or inactive, and looks at the overview and reports. Cannot delete. Professional No access to Monitoring. Takes part through To-Dos created from a control task.

docs.title: How it works
docs.text:
Build list (Configurator) → Schedule → Due on the day → Answer (controlled) → Review / report
                                           └─ not answered → moved to next day (optional) + email
  1. Build. A control task list is built in the Configurator, tab Monitor.
  2. Schedule. In Monitor, a Power User picks the unit, category, topic and task list(s), sets a due date or a repeat schedule, chooses email notifications, then picks the control tasks to schedule.
  3. Due. RIQS creates one task per date. It appears in the Overview of that day.
  4. Answer. On the scheduled day, a responsible person opens the task, sets the fulfilment level on the scale, picks the executing user(s), adds remarks and clicks Save Answer. The task is now controlled.
  5. Not answered? If Move unchecked task to next day is on, the task moves to the next day and the chosen people get an email. If Mail if task is not checked is on, the chosen people get an email.
  6. Review. The overview shows a progress circle and key figures. Lists can be filtered and downloaded.

Statuses you will see

Status Meaning Due · date Scheduled, not answered yet (uncontrolled) Completed · date Answered (controlled) Active / Inactive Whether the schedule is still running (switch in the list)

docs.title: How to schedule control tasks
docs.text:
Who can do this: RiQS Administrator, Group Administrator, Administrator, Power User, Management

  1. Open Monitor and make sure the right unit is selected at the top.
  2. Click Assign Task. The drawer opens on step 1 (Creation).
  3. Pick the Category and then the Sub-Category. Both are required.
  4. Pick one or more Topics, then one or more Task lists. Only lists for this unit and topic are offered.
  5. Set a Due Date, or switch on Mark as a recurring task and choose Daily, Weekly, Monthly or Yearly, how often it repeats, the week days, and start and end date. You can tick Avoid Weekends.
  6. Choose the Email notification options and the people for each: Mail if task is not checked, E-mail if fulfilment is below a percentage, and Move unchecked task to next day.
  7. Click Next. Tick the control tasks you want to schedule (or tick all).
  8. Optional: switch on Assign more afterwards to start again with an empty form after saving.
  9. Click Assign.

Result: A message confirms the scheduling. The tasks appear in the lists and on the overview of each due date.

docs.title: How to answer a control task
docs.text:
Who can do this: RiQS Administrator, Group Administrator, Administrator, Power User, Management

  1. Open Monitor. The Overview shows today's tasks.
  2. Click an uncontrolled task.
  3. Set the fulfilment level on the scale.
  4. Pick the Executing user(s) (required). If nobody specific was assigned, all users of the unit are offered.
  5. Add Remarks if needed.
  6. Click Save Answer. Use Next task / Previous task to move on without going back to the list.

Result: The task shows Completed · date and counts as controlled. If you leave a task with unsaved changes, RIQS asks you to confirm.

docs.title: How to change an answer
docs.text:
Who can do this: same as answering, and only on the scheduled day

  1. Open the controlled task.
  2. In the menu, choose Edit answer, change it and save.

docs.title: How to review results and download a report
docs.text:
Who can do this: RiQS Administrator, Group Administrator, Administrator, Power User, Management

  1. On the Overview tab, see the progress circle (controlled vs. total) and the figures: assigned tasks, fulfilment level of all tasks, controlled tasks, fulfilment of controlled tasks, uncontrolled tasks.
  2. Use the view selector to show All, Controlled task or Uncontrolled task.
  3. Open Filters: date range, minimum/maximum fulfilment, topic, category, users, interval. Click Apply Filter.
  4. Switch to the list tab to see List of distinct control tasks or List of all control tasks.
  5. Click Download Report.

Result: An Excel file is downloaded: the reporting list from the overview, or the task list from the list tab.

docs.title: How to change or stop a schedule
docs.text:
Who can do this: update and activate/deactivate: RiQS Administrator, Group Administrator, Administrator, Power User, Management. Delete: RiQS Administrator, Group Administrator, Administrator, Power User (in audit-safe mode, once tasks are assigned: RiQS Administrator only).

  1. In the list tab, open the row menu and choose Update task. Unit, topic and task list are fixed; you can change category, notifications, dates and which control tasks are included. Click Update.
  2. To pause a schedule, switch its status to Inactive in the all view.
  3. To delete, open the task and choose Delete. For a repeating task choose Selected monitoring tasks (only this one) or Present and future tasks. In the all view you can also tick several rows and click Delete.

Result: Changes apply from today on. Updating does not create a second schedule.

docs.title: How to create a To-Do from a control task
docs.text:
Who can do this: RiQS Administrator, Group Administrator, Administrator, Power User, Management

  1. Open the control task.
  2. In the menu, choose Create open items.
  3. The To-Do form opens with the task details filled in. Choose the people and due date, then save.

Result: A To-Do is created in Open Items and sent to the chosen people.

docs.title: Rules to know
docs.text:
• Answer on the day only. A control task can only be answered, and its answer edited, on its scheduled date. Other days show "Task can be answered on the scheduled date only".
  • Executing user is required when answering.
  • No controller field. You do not pick a "controller" when scheduling. Whoever answers is recorded; the executing users are the unit's users.
  • Move unchecked task to next day: an unanswered task moves to the next day, and the chosen people get one email per move.
  • Mail if task is not checked and E-mail if fulfilment is below a percentage send an email to the chosen people when the condition is met.
  • Recurring limits: a daily or weekly schedule can run up to 3 years; monthly or yearly up to 10 years.
  • Changing the unit in the schedule form clears category, lists, notifications and selection.
  • Delete: Management and Professionals cannot delete control tasks. In audit-safe mode, tasks not yet assigned to anyone can be deleted by RiQS Administrators, Group Administrators, Administrators and Power Users; once tasks are assigned, only the RiQS Administrator can delete them.
  • Not in the Cockpit: control tasks are not listed in the Cockpit. People must open Monitoring.
  • Unit scope: a Power User only sees and schedules for the units they belong to.
  • Planned: switching several schedules active or inactive at once (today one row at a time), and a reminder before a repeating schedule ends.

docs.title: Who can do what
docs.text:
Action RiQS Admin Group Admin Admin Power User Management Professional See the Monitoring overview ✅ ✅ ✅ ✅ ✅ ❌ See the list of control tasks ✅ ✅ ✅ ✅ ✅ ❌ Schedule control tasks ✅ ✅ ✅ ✅ ✅ ❌ Update a schedule ✅ ✅ ✅ ✅ ✅ ❌ Answer a control task (and edit the answer) ✅ ✅ ✅ ✅ ✅ ❌ Activate / deactivate ✅ ✅ ✅ ✅ ✅ ❌ Delete (regular) ✅ ✅ ✅ ✅ ❌ ❌ Delete (audit-safe, not yet assigned) ✅ ✅ ✅ ✅ ❌ ❌ Delete (audit-safe, once assigned) ✅ ❌ ❌ ❌ ❌ ❌ Create a To-Do from a control task ✅ ✅ ✅ ✅ ✅ ❌ Download reports ✅ ✅ ✅ ✅ ✅ ❌ Build control task lists (Configurator) ✅ ✅ ✅ ✅ ✅ ❌

The exact buttons a person sees come from the rights set up for each role. If a button is missing, see Roles & permissions.

docs.title: Connected modules
docs.text:
• Configurator: control task lists and their scales are built on the Monitor tab.
  • Open Items: a To-Do can be created from a control task, for example when a check shows a problem.
  • Organisation & units: categories and sub-categories used when scheduling belong to the unit.
  • Process Guide and Open Items: the other two ways to give people work. See "Which one do I use?" above.

docs.title: Open questions
docs.text:
• Management and the list of control tasks: the rights table lets Management see and edit control tasks; the feature list says Management cannot see the list of control tasks. This page follows the rights table. Should the feature list be corrected?
  • Professional and To-Dos from control tasks: the feature list says a Professional can complete "the To-Do linked to a control task". Does completing that To-Do also answer the control task, or are they separate?
  • Controller field: the feature list still describes choosing a Controller when scheduling. The app no longer has this field. Is the feature list out of date?
  • Sub-Category required: both category and sub-category are required when scheduling. A request to make the sub-category optional is open. Will it change?
  • Reminder before a series ends: a reminder before a repeating schedule runs out has been requested but is not built. Is it planned?
