docs.title: Open Items
docs.text:
In one sentence: Give someone a clear job with a due date (a "To-Do"), see when it is done, and keep their response, cost and files as proof. Menu: ToDos · Status: Live

ToDos: the list of To-Dos with responsible people, due date and status. Screens show test data.

docs.title: What it is
docs.text:
Not every job needs a checklist or a score. Often you just need someone to do one thing by one date: order new gloves, read a new policy, fill in a form, carry out a measure from a risk assessment. Open Items is RIQS's To-Do list for this.

Think of it as a job card you hand to a colleague: what to do, by when, and who checks it. The colleague marks it Done (or Alternatively Done if they solved it another way), adds remarks, the actual cost and files, and submits. You see who has responded and who is still pending.

To-Dos are also created by other modules. A risk measure in Risk Management, an assigned Training, a report in Incident Reports or a control task in Monitoring can all produce To-Dos. They all land in this one list.

Which one do I use? Process Guide, Monitoring and Open Items are easy to mix up.

Use … when … Example Process Guide a job has several steps that people must work through "Morning opening: 8 steps" Monitoring you want to check regularly how well something is done, with a score from 0 to 100% "Fridge temperature checked: daily" ToDos one thing must be done by one date "Replace the broken lamp in room 2 by Friday"

Rule of thumb: many steps → Process Guide. A score → Monitoring. A single job → Open Items.

docs.title: Key terms
docs.text: Term Meaning To-Do (open item) One job with a title, a due date and the people who must do it. Type of To-Do General (a plain job), Training (complete a training), Form (fill in a form), Template (fill in a document template). To-Dos from other modules have the type Risk-Management or Reporting module. Assigned to (Responsible) The people who must do the To-Do. Assigned by (Orderer) The person who created the To-Do. Person in Charge Optional person who checks the To-Do and can confirm an Alternatively Done response as done. Completion Requirement One User (the first response closes it) or All assigned users (set with Must be completed by all). Done "Task completed as specified." Alternatively Done "Task completed with deviations": the job is finished, but not exactly as asked. Budget / Actual cost Planned cost set by the orderer, and the real cost entered by the person who did it. Active / Inactive Whether the To-Do is still in the working list.

docs.title: Who uses it
docs.text: Role What they typically do here RiQS Administrator Supports clients; can see, change and delete To-Dos. Group Administrator Creates and follows up To-Dos across the group. Administrator Creates and follows up To-Dos across the organisation. Power User Creates To-Dos for the unit, follows up responses, deactivates and deletes old ones. Management Creates To-Dos and follows them up; deactivates and deletes their own To-Dos. Professional Sees only the To-Dos assigned to them, and completes them.

docs.title: How it works
docs.text:
Create → Assigned (Pending) → Response submitted (Done / Alternatively Done) → Completed → Inactive (48 h later)
  1. Create. Someone creates a To-Do in two steps: Creation (unit, type, title, what to do) and Assignment (who, by when).
  2. Notify. The assigned people see it in their ToDos list and in their Cockpit (Workflow-Navi).
  3. Do. Each person opens the To-Do, does the job (for a form or template: fills it in; for a training: passes it), chooses Done or Alternatively Done, adds remarks, cost and files, and clicks Submit Response.
  4. Check. The orderer sees the responses and the people still pending. A Person in Charge can confirm an Alternatively Done response with Mark as done.
  5. Close. When the completion requirement is met, the To-Do is completed. 48 hours later it becomes Inactive automatically.

Statuses you will see

Status Meaning What moves it on Pending Waiting for a response A response is submitted Library Form Submitted / Library Template Submitted The attached form or template was filled in, but the person has not yet confirmed Done The person confirms Done Done Completed as specified — Alternatively Done Completed with deviations Person in Charge clicks Mark as done Overdue (shown in red) Due date passed, not completed Completing it, or deactivating it Active / Inactive Still in the working list or not Status action, or automatic 48 hours after completion

docs.title: How to create a To-Do
docs.text:
Who can do this: RiQS Administrator, Group Administrator, Administrator, Power User, Management

  1. Open ToDos and click Create ToDo.
  2. Creation step: choose the unit (Select unit) and the Type of To-Do.
  3. Training: pick the training. Form: pick the form. Template: pick the template.
  4. Enter the To-Do Title, the category and sub-category, and what must be done. You can add a Budget, Attachments from RiQS-Pedia, and Remarks.
  5. Click Next.
  6. Assignment step: leave the default (all members of the unit's executing group) or pick specific people or a user group. Optionally set a Person in Charge.
  7. Tick Must be completed by all if every person must respond.
  8. Set the Due Date, or switch on Mark as a recurring To-Do and set the recurrence, Repeat every, and the end date. You can tick Avoid Weekends.
  9. Optional: switch on E-Mail if not completed and choose who gets the email.
  10. Click Save.

Result: "To-Do created successfully." The To-Do appears in the list and in the assignees' Cockpit.

docs.title: How to complete a To-Do
docs.text:
Who can do this: RiQS Administrator, Group Administrator, Administrator; Power User, Management and Professional if assigned to the To-Do

  1. Open the To-Do from ToDos or from your Cockpit.
  2. Read the Information (description, orderer, budget, completion requirement, attachments).
  3. If it is a Form or Template To-Do, click Fill Out Form / Fill Out Template and complete it. If it is a Training To-Do, click Start Training and pass it.
  4. Under My Response, choose Done or Alternatively Done.
  5. Add Remarks, the Actual cost and files if needed.
  6. Click Submit Response. Use Next task / Previous task to move through your To-Dos.

Result: "Response saved." Your response appears under Responses. If you were the last person needed, the To-Do is completed.

docs.title: How to check responses
docs.text:
Who can do this: RiQS Administrator, Group Administrator, Administrator, Power User, Management (Professionals: only on their own To-Dos)

  1. Open the To-Do.
  2. Open Responses: each answered person shows their choice, remarks, cost and files. The pending list shows who has not answered yet.
  3. If you are the Person in Charge and a response is Alternatively Done, open it and click Mark as done to accept it.

docs.title: How to edit, deactivate or delete a To-Do
docs.text:
Who can do this: edit and deactivate: RiQS Administrator, Group Administrator, Administrator, Power User, Management. Delete: RiQS Administrator, Group Administrator, Administrator, Power User, Management, own To-Dos only (in audit-safe mode: RiQS Administrator only).

  1. Open the To-Do and open the actions menu, or tick rows in the list.
  2. Choose Edit To-do, Inactivate To-Do / Activate To-Do, or Delete.
  3. For a recurring To-Do, choose Selected To-Do (only this one) or Present and future To-Dos. Confirm.

Result: Inactive To-Dos leave the default list; use the Inactive filter to find them. Deleted To-Dos are gone.

docs.title: How to find To-Dos and download a report
docs.text:
Who can do this: search and filter: every role. Download: RiQS Administrator, Group Administrator, Administrator, Power User, Management.

  1. Type in Search, or open Filters: type, category, sub-category, executing users, scheduling, module status (active/inactive) and progress status.
  2. Click a column to sort.
  3. Click Download, choose the date range and download the To-Do Report (Excel).

docs.title: Rules to know
docs.text:
• Professionals see only their own To-Dos, and can only open To-Dos they are assigned to.
  • One User vs. all: without Must be completed by all, the first response closes the To-Do for everyone; the other assignees can no longer answer.
  • Training To-Dos can only be completed after the person has passed the training (reached the pass mark).
  • Form and Template To-Dos: filling in the document is step one. The person must still confirm Done. The To-Do stays in the Cockpit until this is confirmed.
  • To-Dos from Incident Reports cannot be edited in Open Items.
  • Automatic inactive: a completed To-Do becomes inactive 48 hours after the last completion.
  • Overdue: a To-Do past its due date and not completed is shown in red.
  • E-Mail if not completed: when the To-Do becomes overdue, the chosen people get one email listing who has not completed it.
  • Notification: assigned people are notified in their Cockpit.
  • Recurring To-Dos create one To-Do per date. The list shows all To-Dos by default, not only the next 14 days.
  • Audit-safe mode: only the RiQS Administrator can delete To-Dos.
  • Planned: sending an Alternatively Done response back for rework, with a reason (see Open questions).

docs.title: Who can do what
docs.text: Action RiQS Admin Group Admin Admin Power User Management Professional See the To-Do list ✅ ✅ ✅ ✅ ✅ Own To-Dos only Open To-Do details ✅ ✅ ✅ ✅ ✅ If assigned Create a To-Do (any type) ✅ ✅ ✅ ✅ ✅ ❌ Make it recurring / add email reminder ✅ ✅ ✅ ✅ ✅ ❌ Edit a To-Do ✅ ✅ ✅ ✅ ✅ ❌ Complete a To-Do ✅ ✅ ✅ If assigned If assigned If assigned See responses ✅ ✅ ✅ ✅ ✅ Own To-Dos only Confirm an "Alternatively Done" response As Person in Charge As Person in Charge As Person in Charge ✅ (or as Person in Charge) ✅ (or as Person in Charge) As Person in Charge Activate / deactivate ✅ ✅ ✅ ✅ ✅ ❌ Delete (regular, own To-Dos only) ✅ ✅ ✅ ✅ ✅ ❌ Delete (audit-safe) ✅ ❌ ❌ ❌ ❌ ❌ Create and download reports (own and all To-Dos) ✅ ✅ ✅ ✅ ✅ ❌

docs.title: Connected modules
docs.text:
• Risk Management: measures for a risk are created as To-Dos; their status feeds Measures taken / pending.
  • Training: assigning a training creates Training To-Dos for people who have not passed it yet.
  • Incident Reports: actions on a report can be given out as To-Dos.
  • Monitoring: Create open items turns a control task into a To-Do.
  • RiQS-Pedia and Interactive documents: files, forms and templates attached to To-Dos.
  • Cockpit (Workflow-Navi): shows each person's open To-Dos.
  • Process Guide and Monitoring: the other two ways to give people work. See "Which one do I use?" above.

docs.title: Open questions
docs.text:
• Management deleting To-Dos: the rights table says Management may delete their own To-Dos; the feature list says Management cannot delete. This page follows the rights table. Should the feature list be corrected?
  • Group Administrator and recurring / email reminder: the rights table lets the Group Administrator create To-Dos; the feature list marks recurring and email reminder "No*" for the Group Administrator. What does the footnote mean? This page follows the rights table.
  • Who completes To-Dos: the rights table says RiQS Administrators, Group Administrators and Administrators can answer To-Dos, and the other roles if assigned; the feature list says RiQS and Group Administrators cannot complete To-Dos ("No*"). This page follows the rights table. Should the feature list be corrected?
  • Professionals and responses: the rights table lets Professionals see the answers on their own To-Dos; the feature list says Professionals cannot view other users' responses. Should a Professional see other assignees' responses on a shared To-Do?
  • Rejecting an "Alternatively Done" response: the requirement says the checker can Cancel with a reason, which sends the To-Do back to the assignee for rework. Today Cancel only closes the panel. When will rework be built?
  • Opening a To-Do from a report in the Cockpit opens the report, not the To-Do. Is that intended?
  • Menu name: the menu shows ToDos in some places and To-Do's in others. Which name should be used everywhere?

Last reviewed: 2026-10-26

docs.title: Organisation & units
docs.text:
In one sentence: Set up the customer organisation, its units (teams, sites, practices) and the settings each unit needs before daily work can start. Menu: My Organization (RiQS Administrators: Organizations) · My Unit (the unit list, titled Unit) · Status: Live (some parts planned, see below)

My Organization: the organisation with its number of units and contact details. Screens show test data.

My Unit: the units of the organisation; the primary unit is marked. Screens show test data.

docs.title: What it is
docs.text:
RIQS is built in layers. An organisation is the customer company, for example "Medical Centre North Ltd.". It holds the subscription, the billing and a few organisation-wide settings. Inside it there are one or more units: a team, a site or a practice, for example "Practice Zurich". Almost all daily work (documents, shift plans, tasks, reports) happens inside a unit. Several organisations can also be looked after together as a group by a Group Administrator. See How RIQS is organised.

Think of it like a company building: the organisation is the building with one address and one electricity bill, and each unit is an office on its own floor, with its own team, its own filing cabinets and its own contact list.

This page covers the organisation profile, the unit profile and the unit settings: contact list, categories, qualification groups, the reporting set-up, Cirrnet and fault groups. Subscription and payment have their own page: Subscription & billing. People and roles are on Users.

docs.title: Key terms
docs.text: Term Meaning Group Several organisations managed together by a Group Administrator. Organisation The customer company. Holds subscription, billing, theme (logo and colours) and external reporting offices. Unit A team, site or practice inside an organisation. In some screens it is called a Client. Organisation Admin / Deputy Admin The two named contact persons of the organisation. They are the billing contacts and can see billing. Primary unit The unit a user belongs to first. RIQS opens it after login. RIQS version Each unit runs either the Regular Version or the "Audit save" Version (audit-safe mode). In audit-safe mode almost nothing can be deleted. Contact list The unit's address book of suppliers and service providers (shown as Contact List). Categories / sub categories The unit's own list of topics used to sort content in other modules. Qualification & authorisation groups Shown as Qualifications & Permits. Lists which devices and activities the unit is allowed to perform. Reporting scope For each reporting module (CIRS, complaints, ideas, hints, employee feedback, faults): Organisational, Unit with insight or Unit without insight. Cirrnet The Swiss national network for sharing critical incident reports. A unit can forward CIRS reports to it. Fault groups Shown as Malfunction Group. Groups used to sort equipment fault reports. Clone Copy entries (categories, contacts, qualification groups, fault groups) from one unit into another.

docs.title: Who uses it
docs.text: Role What they typically do here RiQS Administrator Creates organisations for invoice customers, sees every organisation and unit, deletes organisations, deletes anything in audit-safe mode, changes a unit back from audit-safe mode. Group Administrator Looks after all organisations of the group: creates organisations online, edits and deactivates organisations, creates, edits, deactivates and deletes units, sets up unit settings and clones them between units. Administrator Looks after the own organisation and all its units: edits and deactivates the organisation, creates, edits, deactivates and deletes units, clones unit settings, adds external reporting offices. Power User Keeps the own unit's profile and settings up to date (contacts, categories, qualification groups, fault groups), sets up Cirrnet. Management Reads the unit profile, maintains contacts, categories and qualification groups; works on fault groups as Fault Officer. Professional Reads the unit profile and contact list, adds contacts; works on fault groups as Fault Officer.

docs.title: How it works
docs.text:
Organisation created  →  Units created  →  Unit settings filled in  →  Users added  →  Daily work
  1. The organisation is created. Either a RiQS Administrator creates it for a customer who pays by invoice, or the customer signs up online and pays (see Subscription & billing). The organisation gets a name, address, contact details, a subscription and a theme (logo and colours).
  2. Units are created under the organisation. Each unit gets a name, an address, a number of full-time users, its RIQS version (regular or audit-safe), the modules it may use (Access Control) and its reporting set-up.
  3. Unit settings are filled in on the unit's Information tab: contact list, categories, qualification groups, Cirrnet and fault groups.
  4. Users are added to the unit (see Users).
  5. Units are kept up to date or, when no longer needed, deleted.

Where you land: - RiQS Administrators and Group Administrators see the list of organisations and the list of units. - Administrators land on their own organisation (menu My Organization). - Power Users, Management and Professionals open My Unit / My Organization and land directly on their own unit's page.

Unit page tabs: Information (profile and settings, everyone) and Billing details (not shown to Management and Professional).

Organisation page tabs: Overview (profile, administration, purchase rights, external reporting offices, colours, usage, list of units) and Billing details.

RIQS version of a unit:

Regular Version  →  "Audit save" Version      (one way for normal users)
"Audit save" Version  →  Regular Version      (RiQS Administrator only)

docs.title: How to create an organisation for a customer
docs.text:
Who can do this: RiQS Administrator. A Group Administrator can also create an organisation online (paid online or on invoice), see Subscription & billing. 1. Open Organizations and click Add organisation. 2. Step General Information: enter the name, organisation number, membership, website, customer software, computer system, address and contact details. 3. Step Subscription: choose the package, number of full-time users (5 to 500), business year start, responsible person, payment method (By Invoice is the default, Online Payment is also possible) and optional extras (tokens, storage, e-signatures). The estimated bill updates as you type. 4. Step Theme customisation: upload a logo and choose the primary and secondary colour. 5. Click Save.

Result: The organisation appears in the list. Customers can also sign up themselves online, see Subscription & billing.

docs.title: How to edit the organisation profile or branding
docs.text:
Who can do this: RiQS Administrator, Group Administrator, Administrator 1. Open the organisation and click Edit. 2. Change General Information or Theme customisation (logo, colour scheme). 3. Click Update.

Result: The new details and colours are shown in the app.

docs.title: How to add an external reporting office
docs.text:
Who can do this: RiQS Administrator, Administrator 1. Open the organisation's Overview tab and go to Reporting offices. 2. Click Add external office. 3. Enter name, contact person, email, phone, location and choose Reporting office for (which reporting modules it handles). 4. Click Save.

Result: The office is listed. An organisation can have at most 2 external offices.

docs.title: How to create a unit
docs.text:
Who can do this: RiQS Administrator, Group Administrator, Administrator 1. Open the list of units and click Add New Unit. 2. Step 1 (Unit information): choose the organisation, choose the RIQS Version, then enter name, unit number, membership, Number of full-time users (at least 5), website, customer software, computer system, address and phone. Tick Address same as organisation to copy the address. 3. Under Reporting Module, choose the scope for each module (Organisational, Unit with insight, Unit without insight). For CIRS and Fault Management, also choose who may see the reports (All or Officer). 4. Click Next. Step 2 (Access Control): switch on the modules this unit may use. Some standard modules are always on and cannot be switched off. 5. Click Save.

Result: "Unit created successfully". The unit appears in the list and in the unit switcher.

docs.title: How to edit a unit
docs.text:
Who can do this: RiQS Administrator, Group Administrator, Administrator, Power User 1. Open the unit and click Edit (or the three-dot menu). 2. Change the information, address, access control or reporting set-up. 3. Click Save.

Result: "Unit updated successfully".

docs.title: How to add contacts, categories and qualification groups
docs.text:
Who can do this: contacts: everyone (Professionals can add contacts but not edit them); categories and qualification groups: everyone except Professional 1. Open the unit's Information tab. 2. Contact List: click Add Contact, choose the supplier category (supplier of goods, service provider, external supplier), and enter the company, address, customer number, VAT number and up to 3 contact persons (one marked Primary Contact). You can attach files. Import Contacts loads contacts in bulk. 3. Categories: click Add Category, enter the Category Name and, if needed, add sub categories. Click Save Category. 4. Qualifications & Permits: click Add Qualification and enter the group.

Result: The entries are shown on the unit page and can be used in other modules.

docs.title: How to clone settings from another unit
docs.text:
Who can do this: RiQS Administrator, Group Administrator, Administrator. Fault groups can also be cloned by Power Users, Management and Professionals who are Fault Officer of the organisation. 1. Open the unit that should receive the data. 2. Click the clone button next to the section (Clone category, Clone for suppliers group, Clone for qualification or fault groups). 3. Tick the entries to copy (or Select all) and confirm.

Result: "Category cloned successfully" (or similar). The copies are independent of the originals.

docs.title: How to switch on Cirrnet forwarding
docs.text:
Who can do this: RiQS Administrator, Group Administrator, Administrator, Power User 1. Open the unit's Information tab and go to Cirrnet Configuration. 2. Switch on CIRRNET Forwarding. 3. Click Add under Cirrnet credentials and enter the Cirrnet username and password.

Result: The section shows "Cirrnet already connected". CIRS reports can now be forwarded to Cirrnet.

docs.title: How to delete a unit
docs.text:
Who can do this: RiQS Administrator, Group Administrator, Administrator (regular version). In audit-safe mode only the RiQS Administrator. 1. Open the unit and click the three-dot menu, then Delete. 2. Confirm with Yes.

Result: "Successfully deleted". If the unit is the primary unit of the Organisation Admin or Deputy Admin, a warning explains that it cannot be deleted.

docs.title: Rules to know
docs.text:
• Full-time users per unit: at least 5, at most 500. Only active users count against the limit (see Users).
  • Audit-safe mode is one-way for customers. A unit can be switched from Regular Version to "Audit save" Version by RiQS Administrators, Group Administrators, Administrators and Power Users. Once audit-safe, the switch is locked for everyone except the RiQS Administrator.
  • Delete in audit-safe mode: only the RiQS Administrator can delete units and unit settings.
  • A unit cannot be deleted if it is the primary unit of the Organisation Admin or the Deputy Admin.
  • A category or sub category cannot be deleted once it is used somewhere else. Deactivate it instead.
  • Fault groups: RiQS Administrators, Group Administrators, Administrators and Power Users may add, edit, deactivate and delete fault groups. Management and Professionals may do this only as Fault Officer. Cloning fault groups to another unit: RiQS Administrator, Group Administrator and Administrator, and other roles only as Fault Officer of the organisation. A fault group that is already used in a fault report cannot be deleted (except by the RiQS Administrator).
  • External reporting offices: at most 2 per organisation.
  • Organisation delete: only the RiQS Administrator. RIQS shows a warning when something blocks the delete.
  • Deactivate: organisations and units can be deactivated by the RiQS Administrator, Group Administrator and Administrator. Contacts, categories and qualification groups can be deactivated by everyone except Professional.
  • Unit switching: RiQS Administrators, Group Administrators and Administrators change unit with the Unit Switcher in the sidebar. Other users who belong to several units choose the unit when they log in. RIQS always opens the user's primary unit by default.
  • Planned: the organisation tabs Group Builder and Roles & Permit exist in design but are not shown yet.

docs.title: Process Guide
docs.text:
In one sentence: Send a step-by-step checklist (a "guide") to the right people, let them work through it step by step, and keep proof of who did what and when. Menu: Guide · Status: Live

Guide: assigned guides with execution mode, progress and due dates. Screens show test data.

docs.title: What it is
docs.text:
Many jobs in a practice follow fixed steps: opening the practice in the morning, preparing a treatment room, onboarding a new colleague. A guide writes these steps down once. The Process Guide module sends that guide to the people who must do the work, and records each step as they complete it.

Think of it as a printed checklist on a clipboard, but one that knows who must sign it, shows the manager the progress in real time, and keeps the signed copy forever. Each step can carry help: an instruction, a file, or a form from RiQS-Pedia that must be filled in.

The guide itself (its steps and attachments) is built in the Configurator. The Process Guide module is where you send it to people, do it, and follow it up.

Which one do I use? Process Guide, Monitoring and Open Items are easy to mix up.

Use … when … Example Guide a job has several steps that people must work through in order "Morning opening: 8 steps" Monitoring you want to check regularly how well something is done, with a score from 0 to 100% "Fridge temperature checked: daily" Open Items one thing must be done by one date "Replace the broken lamp in room 2 by Friday"

Rule of thumb: many steps → Process Guide. A score → Monitoring. A single job → Open Items.

docs.title: Key terms
docs.text: Term Meaning Guide A checklist made of steps. Built in the Configurator, then assigned here. The app sometimes calls it a Checklist. Step (task) One line of the guide. It can have a description, a budget, extra information and attachments. Assign Sending a guide to a unit and its people, with a due date or a repeat schedule. Each assignment creates its own copy of the guide. Individual guide Every assigned person works through their own copy. The guide is finished when each person has finished. Collaborative guide All assigned people share one copy. Any of them can complete a step for everyone. Cross-unit guide A guide with a separate part for each unit. Each unit works on its own part and can only read the other parts. Always collaborative. Standard guide (template) A guide that is not sent to anyone. Users start it themselves with Use Template whenever they need it, which makes a personal copy. Case details Optional fields Case ID 1, Case ID 2 and ID Date that link a guide to a specific case. Draft A step with remarks or attachments saved but not completed yet. Execution mode List column that shows Individual or Collaborative.

docs.title: Who uses it
docs.text: Role What they typically do here RiQS Administrator Supports clients. Can assign, deactivate and delete guides in any unit. Group Administrator Assigns guides across the organisations of the group, also across several units at once. Administrator Assigns guides across the units of the organisation; creates standard guides. Power User Runs guides for their unit: assigns them, creates standard guides, follows progress, deactivates and deletes. Management Assigns guides, creates standard guides, follows progress, deactivates and deletes guides. Professional Opens the guides assigned to them and completes the steps. Starts standard guides with Use Template.

docs.title: How it works
docs.text:
Build (Configurator) → Assign → Work through the steps → 100% complete → Inactive
  1. Build. A Power User or administrator builds the guide in the Configurator: title, topic, steps, attachments, and the units that may use it.
  2. Assign. In Guide, they assign the guide to one or more units and to all or selected people, with a due date or a repeat schedule. They choose Individual or Collaborative.
  3. Notify. The guide shows up in the assignees' Process Guide list and in their Cockpit (Workflow-Navi).
  4. Work. Each assignee opens the guide and goes step by step. For each step they can add remarks, attach files, fill in the attached forms, then click Save as draft or Save & Complete.
  5. Follow up. The manager sees the progress in percent, who completed what, and who is still pending. They can download a report.
  6. Close. When all steps are complete the guide reaches 100%. Guides are then set to Inactive (by hand, or automatically for some guide kinds, see Rules to know).

Statuses you will see

Status Meaning What moves it on Pending / 0% Assigned, nothing done yet An assignee completes a step In Progress (1–99%) Some steps done More steps completed Completed (100%) All required steps done by the required people — Overdue (row shown in red) Due date has passed and the guide is not 100% Completing it, or deactivating it Active / Inactive Whether the guide is still in the working list The status switch, bulk action, or the automatic job

docs.title: How to assign a guide
docs.text:
Who can do this: RiQS Administrator, Group Administrator, Administrator, Power User, Management

  1. Open Guide and click the assign button. The Assign Checklist panel opens.
  2. Choose a Topic, then the guide (Select a guide). Only guides released for your unit are offered.
  3. Choose the Unit (or several units). Administrators can tick Select all units.
  4. Choose the mode: Individual Guide (each person their own copy) or Collaborative Guide (one shared copy). With Individual you can also tick Must be completed by all.
  5. Under Assignment, leave the default (all employees of the unit) or pick specific people.
  6. Set a Due Date, or switch on the recurring option (shown as Mark as Recurring To-do) and set the interval, start and end date. You can tick Avoid Weekends.
  7. Optional: tick Add Case Details (Case ID 2 and ID Date then become required), Add Category Details, and Mail if task is not checked with the people who should get the email.
  8. Click Save.

Result: The guide appears in the list with 0% and its execution mode. Assignees see it in their list and Cockpit.

docs.title: How to create a standard guide (template)
docs.text:
Who can do this: RiQS Administrator, Group Administrator, Administrator, Power User, Management

  1. Open the Assign Checklist panel as above.
  2. Tick Create Guide Template.
  3. Choose topic, guide and unit, then click Save. No due date or assignees are needed.

Result: The guide appears on the Standard guide tab. Users of the unit can start it whenever they need it.

docs.title: How to use a standard guide
docs.text:
Who can do this: every role

  1. Open Guide and switch to the Standard guide tab.
  2. Click Use Template on the guide you need.
  3. Fill in the case details if asked, and work through your copy.

Result: You get your own copy of the guide. Once completed, it is listed under Responses on the template, as proof.

docs.title: How to complete a guide
docs.text:
Who can do this: every role, for guides assigned to them (if the guide was sent to the whole unit: anyone in that unit)

  1. Open the guide from Guide or from your Cockpit. The first step you have not done yet opens automatically.
  2. Read the step and open its attachments. If a form is attached, click Fill out template / open the RiQS-Pedia Form and complete it.
  3. Add remarks (Add Remarks), attach photos or files, and enter the Actual Cost if the step has a budget.
  4. Click Save as draft to keep your work without completing the step, or Save & Complete to finish it.
  5. Repeat for each step.

Result: Completed steps turn green and the progress circle goes up. At 100% the manager's list shows who completed it and when.

docs.title: How to follow up and download a report
docs.text:
Who can do this: every role (Professionals see and download only the guides assigned to them)

  1. On the Guide tab, use Search and Filters (topic, category, guide type, assigned user, completed by, due date range, case details, progress and module status).
  2. Click a column header to sort. Click a row to open its details: who is assigned, who completed it, and who is still pending.
  3. Click Download Report and choose Xls file (the list) or Docx file (a photo documentation report).

Result: The file is prepared and downloaded.

docs.title: How to deactivate or delete guides
docs.text:
Who can do this: RiQS Administrator, Group Administrator, Administrator, Power User, Management (in audit-safe mode, once a guide is assigned: RiQS Administrator only)

  1. On the Guide tab, tick one or more rows.
  2. Click Inactive to remove them from the working list, or Delete.
  3. For a recurring guide, choose whether to delete only the selected guide or present and future guides. Confirm.

Result: Inactive guides are found with the status filter Inactive. Deleted guides are gone.

docs.title: Rules to know
docs.text:
• One guide, several kinds. The Guide Type filter shows where a guide came from: General (assigned here), Equipment (maintenance), Shift plan (Shift Plan) or Reporting (Incident Reports).
  • The list shows everything by default. There is no "next 14 days" filter any more.
  • Overdue = the due date is before today and the guide is not 100%. The whole row is shown in red. Standard guides are never overdue.
  • Individual + Must be completed by all: the guide only counts as done when every assignee has finished it. Progress shows the share of people who finished (two people, one done = 50%).
  • Collaborative: one person's draft is visible to the others; a completed step shows who did it and when.
  • Cross-unit guides are always collaborative. Each unit answers its own part; other units' parts are read-only. When a cross-unit guide is sent to several units you can tick Notify assignees via Workflow-Navi.
  • Forms come first. If a step has a RiQS-Pedia form attached, Save & Complete stays blocked until the form is complete.
  • A draft needs content. You can only save a draft once you have added remarks or an attachment.
  • Shift plan guides are tied to their day. A guide created from a shift can only be worked on its due date. After that day it is locked.
  • Case details can be changed until the guide reaches 100%.
  • Recurring guides create one guide per date of the series. The end date is required.
  • Automatic inactive: guides from a shift become inactive after their day. Copies made with Use Template become inactive 24 hours after they reach 100%, or after their end date if never started. (See Open questions about other guides.)
  • Deleting a standard guide also deletes all copies made from it. Every role except Professional may delete guides; Professionals cannot delete anything.
  • Audit-safe mode: a guide that is not yet assigned to anyone can be deleted by every role except Professional. Once a guide has been assigned, only the RiQS Administrator can delete it.
  • Emails: with Mail if task is not checked switched on, the chosen people get an email when the guide is overdue.

docs.title: Connected modules
docs.text:
• Configurator: where guides and their steps are built and released for units.
  • RiQS-Pedia and Interactive documents: files, forms and templates attached to steps. Answers to forms are stored as filled-in documents.
  • Cockpit (Workflow-Navi): shows the guides a person must work on, until they have finished.
  • Shift Plan: a shift or daily task can carry a guide. It creates a guide for the person on that shift.
  • Equipment: maintenance can come with a guide.
  • Incident Reports: a guide can be assigned from a report.
  • Monitoring and Open Items: the other two ways to give people work. See "Which one do I use?" above.

docs.title: Open questions
docs.text:
• Management deleting and deactivating: the rights table lets Management delete guides (also used templates) and use bulk Delete / Inactive; the feature list says Management cannot. This page follows the rights table. Should the feature list be corrected?
  • Who may download reports: the rights table lets every role download reports; the feature list says Professionals cannot download guide reports and Management cannot download a single guide. This page follows the rights table. Should the feature list be corrected?
  • RiQS Administrator completing guides: the rights table lets every role work on guides assigned to them; the feature list says the RiQS Administrator cannot complete guides. This page follows the rights table. Should the feature list be corrected?
  • Automatic inactive after 48 hours: the feature list says every completed guide becomes inactive 48 hours after completion. The system does this only for shift guides (after their day) and for Use Template copies (24 hours after completion). Should normal assigned guides also become inactive automatically, and after 24 or 48 hours?
  • "Not Completed" button: the feature list describes an orange Not Completed button for saving a step without completing it. The app uses Save as draft instead. Is the feature list out of date?
  • Copies from Use Template: should a copy that is still in progress appear in the user's Guide list straight away? Today it does not, and Responses on the template stays empty until a copy is completed.
  • Overdue email: the feature list says assignees get an overdue reminder. The assign panel sends it to the people picked under Mail if task is not checked. Who should receive it by default?

docs.title: Incident Reports
docs.text:
In one sentence: One place where staff report incidents, complaints, ideas, feedback, device faults and hints, and where officers follow each report up until it is closed. Menu: Reporting module (the page is titled Reporting) · Status: Live

Reporting module: one tab per report type; each report is a card that moves from left to right. Screens show test data.

docs.title: What it is
docs.text:
Every organisation needs a way to hear about things that went wrong, things that could go better, and things that are broken. Incident Reports gives everyone in the unit one simple place to say "something happened". It also gives a named person, the officer, one place to deal with it.

Think of it as six pin boards hanging side by side. Each board is for one kind of report. A new report is pinned on the left. The officer moves it to the right as the work gets done. When it reaches the last column, it is finished.

Each board can be set up for the whole organisation or for a single unit. Some reports can be sent anonymously, so staff can speak up without fear. Officers turn a report into real actions: a To-Do for a colleague, a process guide to follow, or a linked risk.

This page explains what all six boards have in common. Each report type has its own page with the details and its own "Who can do what" table.

docs.title: The six report types at a glance
docs.text: Report type (tab) What it is for Columns on the board Anonymous? Who handles it Can be set up at Details CIRS Critical incidents and near misses (e.g. a wrong medicine almost given) To Be Approved → To Do → In Progress → Done Always CIRS Officer Organisation or unit CIRS Complaint Management Complaints from patients, customers, suppliers or partners New Complaint → In Progress → Complete Optional Complaint Officer Organisation or unit Complaints Idea Management Suggestions to improve how work is done New Idea → In Process → Implemented Optional Ideas Officer Organisation or unit Ideas Employee Feedback Personal concerns and wishes of staff (e.g. workload, conflicts) Assignment → In Progress → Completed Optional Feedback Officer Organisation or unit Employee Feedback Fault Management Broken or faulty devices and equipment New Fault → Fault Clearance → Completed No Fault Officer, plus the people responsible for the device Organisation or unit Faults Hint Management Whistleblowing: suspected fraud, harassment, safety or compliance breaches New Hint → In Process → Implemented Optional Hint Officer (and, if chosen, an external reporting office) Organisation only Hints

docs.title: Key terms
docs.text: Term Meaning Report (card) One reported item. On the board it is a card with a number, e.g. #12. Board (tab) The list of reports of one type, shown in columns. Each report type has its own tab. Officer The person (or people) appointed to handle one report type, e.g. the CIRS Officer. A function role given on top of a normal role. See Roles & permissions. Reporting level How a report type is organised for a unit: Organizational, Unit with insight or Unit without insight. Older documents call these Option 1, 2 and 3. Organizational One officer team for the whole organisation. They see and handle the reports of all units. Unit with insight Each unit has its own officer. The organisation's administrators can still look in. Unit without insight Each unit has its own officer. The organisation's administrators are mostly kept out. Active / inactive An inactive report is "switched off": hidden from the normal board and read-only, but kept. It can be reactivated. Officer-only visibility A report that only the officers (and the person who wrote it) can see. External reporting office An outside contact (e.g. an ombudsperson) who receives CIRS or hint reports by email and opens them through a link. CIRRNET An external network where organisations share anonymous incident reports so that others can learn from them. CIRS reports can be forwarded to it. Malfunction group A category for fault reports (e.g. "IT", "Medical devices"). Older documents call it a "fault group".

docs.title: Who uses it
docs.text: Role What they typically do here RiQS Administrator Supports clients, appoints officers when asked, and is the only role that can delete reports in audit-safe mode (for most report types also outside it). Does not write reports. Group Administrator Switches report types on, chooses the reporting level for units, appoints organisation-level officers. Administrator Same as Group Administrator for the own organisation. Often processes reports when a type runs at organisation level. Power User Appoints officers for the own unit and, at unit level, often processes reports too. Management Writes reports, reads the unit's reports and downloads overviews. Professional Writes reports and follows the own reports. Officers (CIRS, Complaint, Ideas, Feedback, Fault, Hint) Review new reports, decide what to do, assign To-Dos and guides, and close the report.

docs.title: How it works
docs.text:
All six report types follow the same life cycle:

Reported → Reviewed by the officer → Actions taken → Closed

  1. Report. Anyone allowed to report opens the right tab, clicks the create button and fills in a short form. The report appears in the first column.
  2. Officer review. The officer sees a New badge on the card (and, for some types, gets an email). They open it, read it and decide what is needed.
  3. Actions / measures. The officer drags the card to the middle column and acts:
  4. Create To Do gives a task to a colleague. It shows up in that person's Workflow-Navi in the Cockpit.
  5. Attach Guide attaches a process guide that someone must follow.
  6. The officer records what was done or planned in the report's fields (e.g. Measures, Decision, Remarks).
  7. Close. When the work is done, the officer drags the card to the last column. A closed report can go back to the middle column if more work is needed.

Cards move step by step. A card can move one column forward, or from the last column back to the middle one. It cannot skip a column; the app shows Invalid move. The CIRS board has one extra step at the start: To Be Approved. There the officer checks a report before the rest of the unit can see it.

At any time, a person with the right can Deactivate a report, for example a duplicate or a report sent by mistake. This also deactivates the To-Dos and guides attached to it.

docs.title: How to create a report
docs.text:
Who can do this: Everyone except the RiQS Administrator. When Employee Feedback or Fault Management runs at Unit without insight level, Group Administrators and Administrators cannot create those reports. 1. In the left menu, click Reporting module. The board opens on Complaint Management. 2. Click the tab of the report type you need, e.g. CIRS. 3. Click the create button above the board. 4. Fill in the form. Title and Description are always required. The other fields depend on the type (see the type pages). 5. If the type allows it and you want to stay anonymous, switch on Send anonymously. 6. Optionally attach files. 7. Click Report. Click Cancel to close the form without saving anything.

Result: The card appears in the first column of the board.

docs.title: How to find a report
docs.text:
Who can do this: Everyone who can see the board. 1. Open the tab of the report type. 2. Type a word in the search box. The board shows only matching reports. Clear the box to see all again. 3. Click Filters to filter, e.g. by status, date, urgency or keyword. Click Apply, or Cancel to close without changing the board. 4. To see switched-off reports, change the view from active to inactive cards.

Result: The board shows only the matching reports.

docs.title: How to process a report
docs.text:
Who can do this: The officer of that report type, and the other roles named in the type's "Who can do what" table. 1. Click the card number (e.g. #12) to open the report. 2. Fill in or change the officer fields, then save. 3. Drag the card to the next column. 4. To add work, open the card's More options menu (three dots) and choose Create To Do or Attach Guide. These are only offered while the report is active and not yet closed, and only if the unit has the To-Do or Process Guide module.

Result: The card moves. To-Dos and guides appear on the report and in the assignees' Workflow-Navi.

docs.title: How to deactivate or reactivate a report
docs.text:
Who can do this: See the type pages (usually the officer and the administrators of that level). 1. Open the report. 2. Open More options and click Deactivate. In the inactive view, click Activate instead.

Result: The report moves to the inactive cards and becomes read-only. Its To-Dos and guides are deactivated too.

docs.title: How to download an overview
docs.text:
Who can do this: See the type pages (usually everyone except Professionals). 1. Open the tab of the report type. 2. Click Download in the toolbar, or Download report in a card's More options menu.

Result: An Excel overview is downloaded. Anonymous reports show "Anonymous" instead of a name.

docs.title: How to appoint an officer
docs.text:
Who can do this: At Organizational level: RiQS Administrator, Group Administrator, Administrator. At unit level: RiQS Administrator and Power User. The exact rules differ per type; see the type pages. 1. Open Reporting module and the tab of the report type. 2. Click the officer button in the board's toolbar. 3. In Select user, pick one or more people. You can pick Power Users, Management and Professionals; for CIRS, Complaint and Ideas Officers also Administrators. (Hint Officers: Administrators, Power Users and Management.) 4. Click Appoint.

Result: The chosen people become officers for this report type. The tab shows that you are the officer when you open it.

docs.title: How to set up reporting for a unit
docs.text:
Who can do this: RiQS Administrator, Group Administrator, Administrator. For CIRS at Unit without insight level, the RiQS Administrator and the Power User choose the level and the visibility (not the Group Administrator or Administrator). For Idea Management at Unit without insight level, the Power User can also choose it. 1. Open the unit's settings (see Organisation & units). 2. In the Reporting Module section, choose for each report type: Organizational, Unit with insight or Unit without insight. Hint Management can only be Organizational. 3. For CIRS, choose Visibility of CIRS Reports: All or Management & CIRS officers. 4. For Fault Management, choose Report visibility for fault management in the same way. 5. Save.

Result: The unit's board shows the tabs with the chosen rules. Malfunction groups and CIRRNET are set up in the unit's reporting configuration (see Faults and CIRS).

docs.title: Rules to know
docs.text:
• Anonymity.
  • CIRS reports are always anonymous. There is no switch, and the reporter's name is never shown.
  • Complaint, Idea, Employee Feedback and Hint reports have a Send anonymously switch. It is off by default.
  • Fault reports are never anonymous.
  • When a report is anonymous, the name is hidden on the card, in the details and in the Excel download.
  • Who sees a report. The person who wrote a report can always see it. So can the officers, and anyone given a To-Do or guide on it. Beyond that, each type has its own rules (see the type pages). Some reports can be limited to officers only:
  • Complaints: the Complaint only visible to officer switch on the report.
  • Employee Feedback: the Feedback only visible to officer switch on the report.
  • Faults: the Send fault only to officer switch on the report, plus the unit setting.
  • CIRS: the unit setting Visibility of CIRS Reports.
  • Unit without insight. Group Administrators and Administrators do not see the CIRS, idea, employee feedback and fault reports of such a unit. For complaints they see the unit's complaints that are not officer-only.
  • Notifications (email).
  • New CIRS or hint report: the officers get an email.
  • New hint or employee feedback: the reporter gets a confirmation email.
  • Idea requalified as employee feedback: the reporter gets an email.
  • Hint for the external reporting office: the office gets an email when the hint is created, or later when the officer sends it on.
  • CIRS report with an external reporting office: the office gets an email when the report is approved (moved from To Be Approved to To Do).
  • To-Dos created from a report follow the normal To-Do notifications.
  • New-report badge. New cards show a New badge, and each tab shows how many new reports are waiting.
  • Inactive reports are read-only. You cannot edit, move, copy or add To-Dos to them. Reactivate first.
  • Deleting. In audit-safe mode, only the RiQS Administrator can delete a report. Outside audit-safe mode, complaints and ideas can also be deleted by some other roles (see Complaints and Ideas). For all other types only the RiQS Administrator can delete. Everyone else deactivates instead.
  • The RiQS Administrator does not write reports. The create button is not offered to that role.
  • Moving between boards. Only ideas can move to another board: the officer can requalify an idea as Employee Feedback.
  • Attachments open in a preview window inside RIQS. They do not open a new tab and have no download button on the card.

docs.title: Reports and downloads
docs.text:
In one sentence: The Downloads menu is the download centre: every report you request anywhere in RIQS is built in the background and collected here, ready to download. Menu: Downloads · Status: Live

Downloads: requested reports with module, format and status. Screens show test data.

docs.title: What it is
docs.text:
Many RIQS pages have a download button: Monitoring, To-Dos, Training, Process Guide, Equipment, Risk Management, Users, RiQS-Pedia, Shift Plan and others. Big reports can take a while to build. So RIQS does not make you wait on the page. It builds the file in the background and puts it in one central list: the download centre.

Think of it like a print queue. You send the job, carry on working, and pick up the result later.

This page also explains report templates in short. A report template is the layout of a document that people fill in, for example an equipment maintenance report or a survey. Templates are built in other modules (see below).

docs.title: Key terms
docs.text: Term Meaning Download centre The list on the Downloads page with all reports you requested. Report request Clicking a download button in a module. RIQS then starts building the file. File name The name of the report. Many modules let you type your own name when you request it. Report classification What kind of report it is, for example "Task monitor report", "Training report" or "Risk details report". Report type The file format: Word (docx), Excel (xlsx) or PDF. Report template A reusable layout (cover page, sections, questions, signatures) for documents that people fill in.

docs.title: Who uses it
docs.text: Role What they typically do here RiQS Administrator Sees the reports of all users in the selected organisation and unit, for support. Group Administrator Downloads reports they requested. Administrator Downloads reports they requested. Power User Downloads reports they requested. Management Downloads reports they requested. Professional Downloads reports they requested, from the modules where they may download.

docs.title: How it works
docs.text:
Request in a module → Pending → In Progress → Complete (download) or Failed

  1. In a module, you click its download button. Some modules ask for a file name or format first.
  2. A new row appears in the download centre with the status Pending.
  3. RIQS builds the file. The status changes to In Progress.
  4. When it is ready, the status changes to Complete and the download button becomes active. If something goes wrong, the status is Failed.
  5. You can delete rows you no longer need.

The list shows these columns: File Name, Module, Report classification, Requested Date, Generated by, Report type and Status.

docs.title: How to request a report
docs.text:
Who can do this: anyone who has the download button in that module 1. Open the module, for example Monitor or Equipment. 2. Click its download button. Choose a format or type a name if you are asked. 3. Confirm.

Result: The report is added to the download centre.

docs.title: How to download a report
docs.text:
Who can do this: all roles 1. Click Downloads in the left menu. 2. Find your report. Search by name, or use Filter. 3. When the status is Complete, click the download icon in the row.

Result: The file is saved to your computer.

docs.title: How to search and filter
docs.text:
Who can do this: same as above 1. Type part of the file name in the search field. 2. Click Filter. You can filter by: - Start date and End date - Module - Report classification - Generated by - Report type - Status 3. Apply the filter. Each active filter is shown as a chip. Remove one chip, or clear all.

Result: The list shows only matching reports.

docs.title: How to delete a report
docs.text:
Who can do this: same as above 1. Click the delete icon in the row. 2. Confirm.

Result: The report is removed from the list and does not come back after reloading.

docs.title: Rules to know
docs.text:
• Every role sees the download centre. All users can open Downloads, search and filter their reports, download them and delete them.
  • Only finished reports can be downloaded. The download button is disabled until the status is Complete.
  • You see your own reports. Each user sees only the reports they requested. The RiQS Administrator can see all reports in the selected organisation and unit.
  • Unit matters. The list shows reports of the unit and organisation you have selected.
  • Default date range. The list opens showing the last 7 days up to 6 days ahead. Change the dates to see older reports.
  • Formats: Word (docx), Excel (xlsx) and PDF, depending on the module.
  • Modules that send reports here:
  • Monitoring and To-Dos
  • Training, Process Guide and Forms
  • Risk Management
  • Equipment, including maintenance reports
  • Incident reports
  • Units and users
  • RiQS-Pedia (overview, approval view, documents, forms)
  • Shift Plan (daily and weekly)

docs.title: Report templates (short)
docs.text:
A report template is a reusable layout for a document that people fill in on screen and that RIQS then turns into a PDF. The same template builder is used in three places:

Used for Where you build it Special parts Equipment maintenance / validation reports Configurator, linked to Equipment Assigned unit, header and footer text, optional preparation report Interactive documents RiQS-Pedia Header and footer chosen from a list Surveys Surveys Organisation and unit, survey type, comments section

A template can have a cover page, a table of contents and sections. A section can contain:

  • text, images and tables
  • system data (filled in automatically from the module)
  • questions
  • signatures and confirmation elements

When a report is confirmed, the user may be asked to confirm with two-factor authentication. The finished report can be previewed and downloaded as a PDF. The details are described on the pages of the modules that use the templates.

Whether a user can request a report depends on the rights in each module. See the module pages.

docs.title: Connected modules
docs.text:
• Every module with a download button feeds this list, for example Monitoring, Open Items, Training, Process Guide, Risk Management, Equipment, Users, RiQS-Pedia and Shift Plan.
  • Configurator, Interactive documents, Equipment and Surveys use report templates.
  • AI features: according to the feature list, remarks translated with AI also appear in downloaded reports.

docs.title: Open questions
docs.text:

  • "Generated by" filter. Normal users see only their own reports, so this filter only helps the RiQS Administrator. Should Administrators also see the reports of their team?
  • Deleted files. When a report is deleted from the list, is the file itself also removed from storage?

docs.title: RiQS IT (Whiteboard / Notes)
docs.text: In one sentence: RiQS IT is a digital whiteboard for quick sticky notes, either private or shared with everyone in your unit. Menu: Not in the left menu. Open it with the round RiQS-It button in the bottom-right corner of every screen. · Status: Live

docs.title: What it is
docs.text:
Think of the sticky notes on the fridge or the notice board in the staff room. RiQS IT is the same idea, inside RIQS. It is meant for short, informal messages: "Printer toner is ordered", "Team meeting moved to Thursday", or a personal reminder.

There are two whiteboards:

  • Personal: your private board. Only you can see it.
  • Unit: a shared board for everyone in your current unit.

RiQS IT opens as a panel that slides in from the right. You can keep working on the page behind it. You can drag the button anywhere on the screen. You can also make the panel wider or narrower, or open it full screen.

docs.title: Key terms
docs.text: Term Meaning Note A small card on a whiteboard with an optional title, text, colour and attachments. Personal whiteboard Your own board. Nobody else can see it. Unit whiteboard The shared board of the unit you are working in. Pinned note A note on the unit whiteboard that is fixed at the top. Nobody can move it while it is pinned. Mention Typing @ and a colleague's name in a note or comment. The colleague is notified. Badge The red number on the RiQS-It button. It shows unread notes on the unit whiteboard.

docs.title: Who uses it
docs.text: Role What they typically do here RiQS Administrator Can open the unit whiteboard of a unit they choose, read only. Has no personal whiteboard. Group Administrator Personal notes. Writes and comments on the unit whiteboard. Administrator Personal notes. Writes and comments on the unit whiteboard. Power User Moderates the unit whiteboard: pins important notes, tidies up, removes old notes. Management Moderates the unit whiteboard, like the Power User. Professional Personal notes. Writes and comments on the unit whiteboard.

docs.title: How it works
docs.text:
Write note → Save → (unit board) colleagues are notified → comment / pin / move → delete when no longer needed

  • A new note goes onto the board you are looking at (Personal or Unit).
  • Notes keep their place on the board, also after you log out.
  • On the unit whiteboard, every note shows who wrote it and when. On the personal whiteboard, it shows the date.
  • When someone adds a note to the unit whiteboard, all other unit members see a badge on the RiQS-It button. Clicking the badge opens the Unit tab. When you open the unit board, the notes count as read.
  • Pinned notes stay at the top in a Pinned section.

docs.title: How to open RiQS IT
docs.text:
Who can do this: all roles 1. Click the round RiQS-It button in the bottom-right corner. 2. Choose the Personal or Unit tab. 3. Use Expand for full screen, drag the left edge to resize, or click Close.

Result: The whiteboard opens on top of the page you were on.

docs.title: How to write a note
docs.text:
Who can do this: Group Administrator, Administrator, Power User, Management, Professional 1. Open the board you want and click Add Notes. 2. Type a title (up to 50 characters) and your text. You can use Bold, Italic, alignment and checklists. 3. Pick a background colour. 4. Optional: click Attach to add a file from RiQS-Pedia, Upload from device, or Upload image. 5. Optional: type @ and a name to mention a colleague. 6. Click Done.

Result: The note appears on the board. On the unit board, colleagues get a notification.

docs.title: How to comment on a note
docs.text:
Who can do this: Group Administrator, Administrator, Power User, Management, Professional 1. On the unit whiteboard, open the note's menu (More options) and choose Add Comments. 2. Type your comment and click Comment. You can Reply to other comments.

Result: The note shows how many comments it has.

docs.title: How to pin a note
docs.text:
Who can do this: Power User, Management 1. On the unit whiteboard, open the note's menu. 2. Choose pin (or unpin).

Result: The note moves to the Pinned section and cannot be moved by anyone.

docs.title: How to move or delete a note
docs.text:
Who can do this: moving: the author of the note (Group Administrator, Administrator, Power User, Management, Professional); Power User and Management also for other users' notes on the unit whiteboard. Deleting: the author; Power User and Management also any note on the unit whiteboard. Nobody can move a pinned note. 1. Drag the note to a new place on the board. Or open its menu and choose delete. 2. Confirm the deletion.

Result: The new order is saved for everyone, or the note is removed.

docs.title: Rules to know
docs.text:
• Personal notes are private. Only the author sees them.
  • Unit notes are shared with all members of the unit you are working in. If you switch unit, you see that unit's board.
  • Only the author can edit a note or a comment.
  • Deleting:
  • Everyone can delete their own notes and comments.
  • Power User and Management can delete any note or comment on the unit whiteboard.
  • Moving:
  • Everyone can move their own notes.
  • Power User and Management can also move other people's notes on the unit whiteboard.
  • A pinned note cannot be moved by anyone, not even its author.
  • Pinning is only for Power User and Management.
  • Notifications come only from the unit whiteboard. A mentioned person sees the note highlighted.
  • RiQS Administrator can only read. They pick a unit and see its unit whiteboard. They have no personal board and cannot write, comment, move or delete.
  • External users (for example people reporting from outside) do not see RiQS IT.

docs.text:
• RiQS-Pedia: you can attach RiQS-Pedia documents to a note.
  • Organisation & units: the unit whiteboard always belongs to the unit you have selected.
  • Tutorials and help: RiQS IT has its own help content.
