docs.title: RiQS-Pedia (document library)
docs.text:
In one sentence: RiQS-Pedia is the organisation's controlled library for documents, forms and manuals: one place to store them, approve them, share them and reuse them in other modules. Menu: RiQS-Pedia · Status: Live

RiQS-Pedia: folders and files with version, uploader, attachments and active status. Screens show test data.

docs.title: What it is
docs.text:
Every practice has documents that must be "the official version": hygiene rules, work instructions, checklists, device manuals, forms. Without a shared library, copies live in e-mails and personal folders, and nobody knows which one is valid.

RiQS-Pedia solves this. Think of it as a library with a librarian:

  • Folders are the shelves, files are the books.
  • Before a new book goes on the shelf, someone approves it (one, two or three people, depending on how important it is).
  • The librarian decides who may read or change each book (sharing).
  • Every few years the book is checked again (re-approval).
  • Other modules (Process Guide, Day Planner, Equipment, To-Dos …) borrow the same book, so everyone always works with the latest approved version.

You will also hear the names DMS, Document Manager or Library. They all mean RiQS-Pedia.

docs.title: Key terms
docs.text:
Term Meaning Organisation level Folders and files that belong to the whole organisation. Created by a RiQS Administrator, Administrator, Group Administrator or organisation-level RiQS-Pedia Officer. Shown with a key icon ("Created by admin"). Unit level Folders and files that belong to one unit. Created by the unit's own users. Secret folder / file A restricted folder or file of one unit, shown with a lock icon. Only people of that unit who were given access can see it. Organisation-level admins do not see it. Approval principle How many people must approve a file: Standard (1), 4 eyes (2), 6 eyes (3, with the uploader counted). Chosen per file when uploading. Re-approval A repeat approval after a set number of months, so documents are reviewed regularly. Version Each change creates a new version number. Organisation versions use whole numbers (1.00 → 2.00). Unit versions use small steps (1.00 → 1.01, or 0.01 for a first unit upload). Draft A saved, unfinished edit. Shown with a Draft badge. Cover page A page RIQS creates automatically for every file: file name, version, approval principle, uploader, approvers and signatures. Template ("Standard") An organisation document that is handed to units so they can create their own unit copy. Shown with a Standard badge; a unit copy shows Child Standard. RiQS-Pedia Officer A person who may approve (and manage) library content, at organisation level (also called Organisation Manager) or unit level (Unit Manager). Set in RiQS-Pedia Rights. Viewer / Editor The two access levels when sharing: read and download only, or also change. Read confirmation Proof that a person has opened and confirmed a shared document. Attached to The list of places in other modules where a file is used.

See also the Glossary.

docs.title: Who uses it
docs.text: Role What they typically do here RiQS Administrator Sets RiQS-Pedia officers and approval rights at organisation and unit level. Has full rights on organisation and unit folders and files, holds approval rights at both levels, and is the only role that may delete released content in audit-safe mode. Group Administrator / Administrator Builds the organisation folder structure, uploads and approves organisation documents, hands out templates to units, sets organisation-level officers. Power User Runs the unit's library: unit folders, uploads, approvals, sharing, unit templates, unit-level officers. Management Uploads, shares and approves unit documents (Standard and 4 eyes), edits unit documents, moves files, manages secret folders. Professional Reads and downloads shared documents, fills forms, creates unit folders and uploads files. RiQS-Pedia Officer (organisation or unit) Approves documents according to their approval right; gets extra management rights at their level.

docs.title: How it works
docs.text:
1. Upload. A user clicks Upload and picks Create New Folder, Upload File, Upload Pdf-forms or Equipment manual. During upload they choose the version, the folder, the approval principle, the re-approval cycle and key words.

2. Approval. The new file is Pending and appears in the Approval tab. The right approvers approve it (with an electronic signature if required). After the last approval it is Approved, gets its cover page and becomes visible to everyone it is shared with.

3. Share and use. The file is shared with units, user groups or single people as Viewer or Editor. People find it in the library, read it, download it, fill it (forms) or see it attached in other modules.

4. Change. Someone with edit rights edits the document online or uploads a new version. The new version goes through approval again. Once approved, it replaces the old version everywhere.

5. Re-approval. When the re-approval date comes, the file shows Re-approval started and must be approved again.

6. End of life. A file can be set Inactive (kept, but not offered for new use) or Removed (deleted).

Approval status of a file:

Pending → Partially approved (4 or 6 eyes only) → Approved → Re-approval started → Approved …

Separately, every file is Active or Inactive. There is no "Rejected" status. See Open questions.

docs.title: The screen
docs.text:
• Tabs: All (folders and files), Approval (files waiting for you), DOCX (Word files), PDF-Forms, Manuals (equipment manuals), Interactive Documents. The tabs are views on the same library, not separate libraries.
  • Toolbar: search with Filter, Folder search (only inside a folder: include sub-folders or not), Keep Selection (keep ticked items while you move between folders), View details (side panel), Library report (Excel list), the RiQS AI button (ask questions about selected documents), RiQS-Pedia Rights and Upload.
  • View control: people who are both a normal user and an officer see a switch: Personal or Officer (ORG) / Officer (UNIT). Officer rights only apply while the switch is on the officer side.
  • Row menu (⋯): shows only the actions you are allowed to do right now (see below).

docs.title: How to create a folder
docs.text:
Who can do this: RiQS Administrator, Group Administrator, Administrator and organisation officers (organisation folders); RiQS Administrator, Power User, Management, Professional (unit folders); Power User and Management only (secret folders) 1. Open RiQS-Pedia, go to the place where the folder should be. 2. Click Upload → Create New Folder. 3. Enter a Folder Name and pick a Folder Color. 4. Optional, at the top level of a unit only: switch on Secret Folder. 5. Click Create.

Result: The folder appears in the list. If you try to create a folder at a level you do not belong to, you see "You're not allowed to create folders at the ORG/UNIT level".

docs.title: How to upload a file
docs.text:
Who can do this: every role (into secret folders: RiQS Administrator, Power User and Management only) 1. Open the folder where the file belongs (it is pre-selected later). 2. Click Upload → Upload File (or Upload Pdf-forms / Equipment manual, PDF only). 3. Version: choose New or Replace Version (pick the document you replace). You can adjust the suggested version number. 4. File: drag and drop or browse. Check the folder. Maximum size is 2 GB. 5. For PDF forms only, Electronic Signature: decide if filling needs a signature, choose the Signature type (simple, advanced or qualified) and, if wanted, 2 Factor authentication required. 6. Approval Principle: Standard, 4 eyes or 6 eyes. 7. Re-approval: choose the Interval Duration (1–12, 24, 36, 48 or 60 months; default 36) and the Duration of the re-approval process (default 6 months), or switch on Re-Approval not required. 8. Key Words: add words that help people find the file. 9. Click Save.

Result: "File sent for approval." The file is Pending and is listed in the Approval tab until it is approved.

docs.title: How to approve a file
docs.text:
Who can do this: see "Rules to know → Who may approve" 1. Open the Approval tab (or the link in Workflow-Navi). 2. Open the file and check it. Changes since the last version are shown. 3. Click Approve. 4. If a signature is required, enter the 5-digit code (2-factor) and/or sign in the signing window.

Result: "File approved". The cover page is updated. With 4 or 6 eyes, the file stays Partially approved until the last approval.

docs.title: How to share a file or folder
docs.text:
Who can do this: files: RiQS Administrator, Group Administrator, Administrator, Power User, Management; organisation folders: Group Administrator, Administrator; unit and secret folders: Power User (secret folders also Management); RiQS-Pedia Officers at their level 1. In the row menu choose Share (or Share Folder). 2. In Basic assignment, pick the Organization, then Units, User Group or single Users. Use Advanced Assignment for detailed per-person settings with filters. 3. Set the Permission type: Viewer or Editor. 4. Optional: tick Notify user and choose whether to notify only added or removed users or all assigned users. 5. Click Share.

Result: "File Shared". The people can now find the file in the list and in search.

docs.title: How to edit a document or create a new version
docs.text:
Who can do this: people with edit rights on that document (see table) 1. In the row menu choose Edit Document (or Edit Excel / Edit PPT). If a draft already exists, the menu says Continue Editing. 2. Edit in the browser. Your work is saved as a draft. 3. Save the new version. A unit user who edits an organisation document chooses a unit folder for their unit version.

Result: A new version is created and sent for approval. Older versions stay in Version History.

docs.title: How to use a template
docs.text:
Who can do this: Administrator / Group Administrator (hand out); Power User and unit officers (create unit version); assigned users (fill) 1. An organisation document is handed to units with Share as Template: pick the units and click Confirm. 2. In a unit, a Power User opens it and chooses Create Unit Standard to make the unit's own copy, or Make Unit Standard to turn a unit document into a unit template. 3. A normal user chooses Fill Template. Their filled copy is saved as a personal copy; the template itself does not change.

Result: The template shows a Standard badge; unit copies show Child Standard.

docs.title: How to rename, move, recolour or tag
docs.text:
Who can do this: see table 1. In the row menu choose Rename, Move, Change Color (folders) or Key Words. Use Add file note for a short note (up to 100 characters). 2. For Move, pick the destination folder. RIQS warns you that the item will now be visible to whoever can see the new folder ("Change who has access"). 3. Confirm.

Result: The change is shown at once. A new name is also shown in Equipment, To-Dos and Configurator items that use the file.

docs.title: How to download a file
docs.text:
Who can do this: anyone who can see the file 1. In the row menu choose Download.

Result: You get a ZIP with the original file and its cover page as PDF.

docs.title: How to see who has read a file and where it is used
docs.text:
Who can do this: anyone who can see the file; revoking a read confirmation needs management rights (see table) 1. Open View details for the file. 2. Open the assignment list to see Assigned members and Read confirmations (pending / completed). Officers can Revoke a confirmation. 3. Click the Attached to info to see the modules where the file is used.

Result: You see who still has to read the file and where it is in use.

docs.title: How to set approvers (RiQS-Pedia Rights)
docs.text:
Who can do this: RiQS Administrator, Group Administrator, Administrator (organisation level); Power User (unit level) 1. Click RiQS-Pedia Rights. 2. Choose Organization or a unit. 3. Add people to Standard approval right, 4-eyes approval right or 6-eyes approval right. 4. Click Save.

Result: These people become RiQS-Pedia Officers at that level.

docs.title: How to deactivate or delete
docs.text:
Who can do this: see table 1. Use the Active switch, or Bulk activate / Bulk deactivate for several files. 2. To delete, choose Remove (or Delete for a selection) and confirm.

Result: "File removed". The file disappears from the library and from the modules that used it.

docs.title: Rules to know
docs.text:
Organisation vs unit - Organisation-level users (Administrator, Group Administrator) work in organisation folders. Unit-level users work in unit folders. Neither can create folders on the other's level. - Power Users, Management and Professionals cannot rename, move, deactivate or delete organisation content (key icon), even if they can see it. - A unit user can turn an organisation Word document into a unit version; it is saved in a unit folder.

Who may approve - Organisation documents are approved by RiQS Administrators, Administrators, Group Administrators and organisation-level officers. Unit documents are approved by RiQS Administrators and the unit's Power Users, Management and unit-level officers. - Approval rights add up: a 6-eyes approver may also do 4-eyes and Standard approvals; a 4-eyes approver may also do Standard and the first of the two 6-eyes approvals. Only a 6-eyes approver may give the final 6-eyes approval. - Each person can be in only one of the three lists (the higher list already includes the lower rights). - Administrators always hold 6-eyes rights at organisation level; this cannot be removed. Power Users are approvers of their unit by default for Standard, 4 eyes and 6 eyes; Management by default for Standard and 4 eyes. They can be moved to a lower list. - 4 eyes: the uploader cannot approve their own file. 6 eyes: the uploader and anyone who already approved in this cycle cannot approve again. - Professionals cannot approve unless they are made an officer.

While a file is pending - Only View File, Download, Approve, Key Words, Edit Document, Version History and Remove are offered. Share, Move and Rename come back after approval. - Approvers and the uploader may edit a pending version. This does not create a new version number.

Sharing - When a folder or file is moved, it takes over the access rights of the new folder. Moving into a secret folder makes it secret; moving out of one removes the secret mark. - New sub-folders take over the access of their parent folder. A new file in a shared folder becomes visible to that audience once it is approved. - Professionals can only be given Viewer access to normal documents. Editor is possible for forms and unit template copies. - Templates and their unit copies are handed out with Share as Template, not with normal Share.

Versions - A new approved version replaces the old one in all modules and keeps the same assignments. - Version history shows the differences between versions.

Delete and deactivate - A file that is still used by an open task (for example a To-Do, equipment maintenance or incident report) cannot be set inactive. - Deleting a folder deletes everything inside it. There is no recycle bin. - Deleting removes the file's links in other modules. - In audit-safe mode only the RiQS Administrator may delete released files and folders with content. Files not yet released may still be deleted by Group Administrators, Administrators and organisation officers (organisation files) and by Power Users and unit officers (unit files). Empty unit folders may still be deleted by Group Administrators, Administrators, Power Users and officers.

Notifications - Workflow-Navi lists documents assigned to you, documents edited by others, files to approve, files to re-approve and forms to sign.

docs.title: Open questions
docs.text:
1. Rejecting a file. There is no "Rejected" status. How should an approver say "no"? Today the only ways seem to be editing the pending version or removing it.
  2. RiQS Administrator rights. The rights sheet lets the RiQS Administrator upload, share, approve (organisation and unit), create unit folders and fill forms. The feature list says the RiQS Administrator may do none of these. This page follows the rights sheet; please confirm.
  3. Management and 6 eyes. The feature list says Management holds Standard, 4-eyes and 6-eyes rights by default. The rights sheet says Management cannot give the final 6-eyes approval. This page follows the rights sheet; please confirm.
  4. Management sharing files. The rights sheet lets Management share (assign) documents; the feature list says Management may not use Share. This page follows the rights sheet; please confirm.
  5. Organisation templates. The feature list says Management and Professionals cannot see organisation templates and Group Administrators cannot edit them. The rights sheet says "Yes (if assigned)" and "Yes". This page follows the rights sheet; please confirm.
  6. Rights sheet: general rows vs level breakdown. The general rows of the rights sheet say Professionals cannot create folders and Management cannot deactivate documents; the organisation/unit breakdown says Professionals may create unit folders and Management may deactivate unit documents. This page follows the more detailed breakdown. Which is right? The sheet also leaves Professionals blank for sharing files and editing key words.
  7. Sharing with one person. On the test system, ticking a single user leaves Share disabled; only a whole role works. Intended?
  8. Viewer vs Editor. What exactly may an Editor do that a Viewer cannot (edit, new version, move, delete)? And after a share is removed, should the file disappear at once and what happens to open read confirmations?
  9. Form type. The earlier app let uploaders mark a PDF form as Normal, Confidential or General (General forms cannot be shared). The current app has no such choice. Is this planned, and what does Confidential mean?
  10. Re-approval timing. Does "Duration of the re-approval process" mean how many months before the due date re-approval starts? Who is reminded?
  11. Deleting used files. A file used by an open task cannot be deactivated, but can it still be deleted? And can deleted files be restored by support?

docs.title: Risk Management
docs.text:
In one sentence: Find the risks in your unit, rate how serious they are, decide what to do about them, and follow the measures until the risk is under control. Menu: Risk-Management · Status: Live

Risk-Management: the risk matrix (current and target value) and the list of risks. Screens show test data.

docs.title: What it is
docs.text:
Every practice or department has things that could go wrong: a device fails, a drug is mixed up, a new colleague is not trained in time. Risk Management is the place to write these risks down before something happens, and to keep track of what you are doing about them.

Think of it as a risk register with a built-in to-do list. For each risk you describe what could happen, why, and what is already in place. Then you assess it: how bad would the impact be, and how likely is it? RIQS turns this into a risk value (for example 3/4) and shows it on a coloured matrix. You decide on a measure (avoid, reduce, monitor or accept the risk) and create To-Dos for the people who must act. When the risk is under control, an Administrator, Power User or Management user approves it.

The dashboard gives management a picture of all risks in the unit at a glance: how many there are, how serious they are, and how many measures are still open.

docs.title: Key terms
docs.text: Term Meaning Risk Something that could go wrong in the unit. It has a name, a topic, a category and sub-category, owners, and a description. Topic The broad area of the risk. The app offers four: instruments, administration, staff, and drug products. Risk Owner The person responsible for the risk. Professional (on a risk) The people who work on the risk. This is not the same as the Professional role. Assessment One rating of the risk at a point in time. A risk can have many assessments. The newest one counts. Impact How bad the damage would be: 1 insignificant, 2 low, 3 noticeable, 4 critical, 5 catastrophic. Probability How likely it is: 1 unlikely, 2 very rare, 3 rare, 4 possible, 5 frequently. Assessment (verdict) Your judgement of the risk: 1 acceptable, 2 conditionally acceptable, 3 not acceptable. Current value Impact and probability together, written as impact/probability, for example 4/3. Target value The value you want to reach after the measures, for example 2/2. Measure Your strategy: Avoid risk, Mitigate risk, Monitor risk or Accept risk. Measures taken / Measures pending The To-Dos created for this risk that are done, or still open. CIRS incident A report from the Incident Reports module that you can link to a risk as evidence.

docs.title: Who uses it
docs.text: Role What they typically do here RiQS Administrator Supports clients. Can see and manage risks and delete assessments. Cannot approve risks. Group Administrator Oversees risks across the organisations in the group. Cannot approve risks. Administrator Manages and approves risks across all units of the organisation. Power User Runs risk management for their unit: creates, assesses, follows up and approves risks. Management Creates, edits, assesses and approves risks, and creates To-Dos. Cannot delete risks. Professional No access to Risk Management as a role. A Professional can still be named as a risk owner or professional on a risk, and receives the To-Dos.

docs.title: How it works
docs.text:
1. Identify. Someone creates a risk and fills in what could happen, the impact, the causes and the existing measures. They can link CIRS incidents that show the risk is real.
  2. Assess. They rate impact, probability and verdict, pick a target value and choose a measure. This can be done straight away or later.
  3. Act. From the risk, they create To-Dos for the people who must carry out the measures. The risk shows how many measures are taken and pending.
  4. Re-assess. When things change, they add a new assessment. The history of all assessments is kept.
  5. Approve. When the risk is under control, an Administrator, Power User or Management user approves the risk. It is then locked.

A risk has one of three statuses. The status is set automatically:

Identified → Pending → Approved

Status Meaning What moves it on Identified The risk exists but has no assessment yet. Adding the first assessment. Pending The risk has at least one assessment and is not approved yet. An Administrator, Power User or Management user chooses Approve Risk. Approved The risk has been approved. The risk is read-only. No way back (see Open questions).

Separately, each risk is Active or Inactive. Inactive risks are kept for the record but hidden from the default list.

docs.title: How to create a risk
docs.text:
Who can do this: RiQS Administrator, Group Administrator, Administrator, Power User, Management 1. Open Risk-Management and click Create a risk. 2. On the Creation step, fill in the Risk name, Topic, Category, Sub category, at least one Risk Owner and at least one Professional. These are required. 3. Optionally describe the incident, Impact, Causes, Existing measures and Remarks. 4. Optionally click Use CIRS incident to link one or more CIRS reports. 5. Click next to go to the Assessment step. Fill it in (see the next task), or choose Save without assessment to assess later. 6. Save.

Result: The risk appears in the list with status Identified (no assessment) or Pending (with assessment).

docs.title: How to assess a risk
docs.text:
Who can do this: RiQS Administrator, Group Administrator, Administrator, Power User, Management 1. Open the risk. 2. In Assessments, click Add Assessment. 3. Choose Impact, Probability and Assessment, then a Target Value and a Measure. All five are required. 4. Save.

Result: The new assessment becomes the current one. The matrix shows the current and target values. Older assessments stay in the history.

docs.title: How to create To-Dos for the measures
docs.text:
Who can do this: RiQS Administrator, Group Administrator, Administrator, Power User, Management, while the risk is not approved 1. Open the risk and click the ⋮ (more) menu. 2. Choose Create To-Do. 3. RIQS opens the To-Do form with the risk, its category and topic already filled in. Choose the people and the due date, then save.

Result: The To-Do is sent to the people you chose. It appears on the risk under Measures pending until it is completed, then under Measures taken.

docs.title: How to approve a risk
docs.text:
Who can do this: Administrator, Power User, Management 1. Open the risk and click the ⋮ menu. 2. Choose Approve Risk.

Result: The status changes to Approved. Editing, assessing and creating To-Dos are no longer possible for this risk.

docs.title: How to copy, edit, deactivate or delete a risk
docs.text:
Who can do this: see Who can do what 1. Open the risk. 2. Use the Active / Inactive switch to deactivate or reactivate it. 3. Use the ⋮ menu for Copy, Edit or Delete. Copy opens a new risk pre-filled from this one. 4. To delete several risks, select them in the list and click the delete button.

Result: The list updates. A deleted risk disappears, together with its assessments and its To-Dos.

docs.title: How to find risks and download reports
docs.text:
Who can do this: RiQS Administrator, Group Administrator, Administrator, Power User, Management 1. Use Search risk to search by name. 2. Click Filter to filter by category, topic, risk status, owner, professional, added by, created or updated date, measure status, active status, impact, probability, assessment, measure, value or target value. 3. Click the download icon and choose: - Risk Overview report (PDF) for the unit, with charts. - Excel report for the filtered unit. - Excel report for all units. 4. To download one risk, open it and click the download icon. You get a PDF of that risk.

Result: You choose a file name and the file is downloaded.

docs.title: Rules to know
docs.text:
• Required to create: risk name, topic, category, sub-category, at least one risk owner and one professional.
  • Who can be picked as owner or professional: active users of the unit with the role Power User, Management or Professional.
  • Approved means locked. After approval nobody can edit the risk, add, edit or delete assessments, or create To-Dos for it.
  • Who approves: Administrators, Power Users and Management users. RiQS Administrators and Group Administrators cannot approve risks.
  • The last assessment cannot be deleted. Delete only appears when a risk has more than one assessment.
  • Deleting a risk also deletes its assessments and the To-Dos created from it.
  • Audit-safe mode: in organisations that run audit-safe, only the RiQS Administrator can delete risks. Others deactivate instead. See Audit-safe mode.
  • Dashboard charts show the current and target values of risks on a matrix by topic, a bar chart of identified, pending and approved risks split by verdict (acceptable, conditionally acceptable, not acceptable), and an Action Graph of the To-Dos.

docs.title: Connected modules
docs.text:
• Incident Reports: CIRS reports can be linked to a risk as evidence.
  • Open Items: measures are carried out as To-Dos created from the risk. Their status feeds Measures taken / pending.
  • Configurator: the categories and sub-categories used for risks are set up there.
  • Equipment: device risks are usually recorded under the instruments topic.
  • Reports & downloads: risk overview and single-risk reports.

docs.title: Open questions
docs.text:
• Can an approved risk be reopened? There is no button to undo an approval. Is that intended?
  • RiQS Administrator and the Active switch. The Roles & Rights sheet says the RiQS Administrator can activate and deactivate risks. The feature list leaves it open. Please confirm.
  • Topic names. Some topic names show placeholder text in English (for example "Topic 7"). What are the correct on-screen names for the four topics?
  • Equipment Officer column. The source role sheet gives the Equipment Officer full risk rights. Does being an Equipment Officer really grant Risk Management rights?
  • Delete assessment is limited to RiQS and Group Administrators in the feature list (the Roles & Rights sheet does not mention it). Should Administrators and Power Users not be able to remove a wrong assessment?

docs.title: Shift Plan (Day Planner)
docs.text:
In one sentence: Plan who works when in your unit, record absences, schedule daily checklists, and see at a glance where the plan has gaps or clashes. Menu: Day Planner · Status: Live

Day Planner, tab Shifts: the week view with planned shifts. Screens show test data.

docs.title: What it is
docs.text:
Every unit needs to know who is on duty, who is away, and which routine jobs must be done each day. The Shift Plan (also called the Day Planner) is the unit's shared planning board for all of this.

Think of it as a wall calendar that also hands out the work. You first set up shifts once (for example "Early shift", "Late shift"), then place them on the calendar and assign people. A shift can carry a guide, documents and forms, so the people on that shift know exactly what to do. On the day itself, RIQS puts each person's shift tasks and checklists into their Cockpit automatically.

The same page also handles absences (holidays, sickness, training days) and checklists (short lists of everyday tasks). Because shifts and absences live in one place, RIQS can warn you when someone is planned for a shift while they are absent, inactive, or already on another shift.

The page has three tabs: Shifts, Absence and Checklist. Each tab can be shown as a calendar (Day, Week, Month) or as a list. The Shifts tab also has a Shift schedule grid: people down the side, days across the top.

docs.title: Key terms
docs.text: Term Meaning Shift A reusable shift definition, set up once. It has a name, an abbreviation, a display colour, and optionally default time slots, a guide, documents and forms. Regular shift A planned shift based on one of the shift definitions. It can be one day or repeating (daily, weekly, monthly, yearly). Special shift A one-off task with its own title, date, colour and optional time span, for example an equipment maintenance or validation. Time span Start and end time of a shift. A shift can have several time slots. They are shown together on one shift card. Absence type A category of absence, such as "Holiday". It has a name, abbreviation, colour and a scope: Unit or Organization. Standard absence An absence of an Organization-scope type. It is created in every unit the person belongs to. Checklist A reusable list of everyday tasks (with descriptions, colour, and optional guide). You schedule it for a date and people. Inside the app it is sometimes called a "quick task" or "everyday task". Individual guide / Collaborative guide How a guide attached to a shift or checklist is completed: each person completes their own copy (individual), or the team completes one copy together (collaborative). With an individual guide you can also tick Must be completed by all users. Conflict A planning problem RIQS has detected, for example a shift with nobody assigned. Change log The history of changes made to a shift after its date has passed.

docs.title: Who uses it
docs.text: Role What they typically do here RiQS Administrator Supports clients. Can see and plan across all organisations. Group Administrator Plans and oversees the units of the organisations in the group. Can set up organisation-wide absence types. Administrator Plans across all units of the organisation. Approves absences. Power User Runs the unit's planning: sets up shifts and checklists, plans the month, approves absences, resolves conflicts. Management Plans shifts and checklists for the unit, enters absences for others, and approves or rejects absences in the unit. Professional Sees the plan and its conflicts, completes their shift tasks and checklists, and requests their own absences.

docs.title: How it works
docs.text:
1. Set up once. A planner creates the shift definitions (Create on the Shifts tab), the absence types (Setup on the Absence tab) and the checklists (Create on the Checklist tab).
  2. Plan. The planner places shifts on the calendar with Plan, or by clicking an empty day. They choose people, dates, times and whether it repeats. Checklists are scheduled the same way.
  3. Check. While planning, RIQS checks if the chosen people are already on an overlapping shift in the same unit, and shows a warning. It also flags conflicts (see below).
  4. Do. Each morning, RIQS assigns that day's shift and checklist tasks to the people on duty. They appear in each person's Cockpit. People open the shift, work through the guide, fill in forms, and click Complete.
  5. Follow up. The calendar shows progress with a status dot: done, partially done, or not done. Completed items show who completed them and when.

There is no separate "publish" step. A plan is visible to the unit as soon as it is saved.

Absence flow: Pending → Approved or Pending → Denied

  • A new absence always starts as Pending.
  • An authorised person opens it and clicks Approve or Deny. When denying, they must write a Reason for Denial.
  • Other statuses you may see: Cancelled and Inactive.

Conflict causes. RIQS marks a shift or checklist as a conflict when:

  • an assigned person is absent (approved or pending absence) at that time,
  • an assigned person is inactive, or
  • nobody is assigned.

A partial-day absence only counts if it overlaps the shift time. Conflicts on dates that have passed are inactive and hidden by default.

docs.title: How to set up a shift
docs.text:
Who can do this: RiQS Administrator, Group Administrator, Administrator, Power User, Management 1. Open Day Planner and go to the Shifts tab. 2. Click Create. The Manage Shift panel opens. 3. Enter a Shift title and an Abbreviation (both required). 4. Optionally choose a Display Color, add one or more default time slots (Add Time Span), attach a guide, documents, forms or interactive documents. 5. Click Save. 6. To change the order of shifts, drag them in the Created Shifts list. The calendar uses this order. Use Download to get the list of shifts.

Result: The shift appears in Created Shifts and can now be planned.

docs.title: How to plan a regular shift
docs.text:
Who can do this: RiQS Administrator, Group Administrator, Administrator, Power User, Management 1. On the Shifts tab, click Plan (or click an empty day in the calendar). 2. Choose Regular shift and select the shift. 3. Choose the people (Select Users). This is optional; you can save a shift without people, but it will show as a conflict. 4. Set the time span(s). Default time slots from the shift are filled in. 5. To repeat it, choose an interval (Daily, Weekly, Monthly or Yearly), Repeat every, and an end date. 6. If a person is already on an overlapping shift, you see "Selected user is not available for the chosen time span". This is a warning only; you may still save. 7. Click Save.

Result: The shift appears on the calendar for each date. The people see it in their Cockpit on the day.

docs.title: How to plan a special shift
docs.text:
Who can do this: RiQS Administrator, Group Administrator, Administrator, Power User, Management 1. Click Plan and choose Special shift. 2. Enter a title, date, colour and optional time span. Add a guide, documents or forms if needed. 3. For an equipment job, choose Maintenance and Validation, pick the equipment (only equipment with a maintenance or validation due today or later is offered) and the executing person or group. 4. Click Save.

Result: The special shift appears on the calendar. Its time span is for information only and never causes a conflict.

docs.title: How to change, copy or delete a planned shift
docs.text:
Who can do this: RiQS Administrator, Group Administrator, Administrator, Power User, Management. In audit-safe mode only the RiQS Administrator can delete. 1. Click the shift on the calendar. The detail panel opens with Overview, and for past shifts a Change log tab. 2. Use the menu to Edit, Copy (Clone shift to other dates) or Delete. 3. For a repeating shift, choose whether the change applies to This shift only or to All recurring shifts. 4. To copy all shifts of one day at once, use the copy option on that day.

Result: The calendar updates. Changes to shifts in the past are written to the Change log (who, when, what). Deleted past shifts can be found again with the Deleted shift filter.

docs.title: How to complete a shift or checklist
docs.text:
Who can do this: The people assigned. Assigned checklists can be worked on by every role except the RiQS Administrator. 1. Open the shift or checklist from the calendar or from your Cockpit. 2. Work through the attached guide, click Fill out form for any forms, and tick off tasks. 3. Click Complete (or Complete task / Complete guide).

Result: The item is marked done and leaves your Cockpit. A completed form can be opened later to read the answers.

docs.title: How to use the shift schedule grid
docs.text:
Who can do this: All roles can view the schedule of their own unit (Group Administrators and Administrators: all units of their organisation(s); RiQS Administrator: all organisations). Assigning shifts in the schedule: RiQS Administrator, Group Administrator, Administrator, Power User, Management. 1. On the Shifts tab, click Shift schedule. 2. Each row is a person, each column a day. Cells show the shift abbreviation and colour, a red box for an absence, and a yellow circle with the number of special shifts. If a cell has more than two items, click the counter to see all. 3. Filter by name or by user status (Active, Inactive, All). Hide rows you do not need with Hide user; bring them back with Show hidden users. 4. Drag a shift to another cell. A dialog opens to confirm the assignment. 5. Click Download to get the schedule as a PDF. It contains exactly the people currently shown.

Result: You see the whole team's week or month at a glance.

docs.title: How to set up absence types
docs.text:
Who can do this: Unit types: RiQS Administrator, Group Administrator, Administrator, Power User, Management. Organization types: RiQS Administrator, Group Administrator, Administrator. 1. Go to the Absence tab and click Setup. 2. Enter a name, abbreviation, colour and Scope (Unit or Organization). 3. Click Save.

Result: The type can be used when scheduling absences. Organization-scope types always use a fixed colour.

docs.title: How to schedule or request an absence
docs.text:
Who can do this: Own absence (in your own or primary unit): Group Administrator, Administrator, Power User, Management, Professional. Absences for other users of the unit: RiQS Administrator, Group Administrator, Administrator, Power User, Management. 1. Go to the Absence tab and click Schedule. 2. Choose the Affected User, the Absence Type, and the start and end (full day, or with times for a partial day). 3. Optionally add remarks and attachments. 4. Click Save.

Result: The absence is created as Pending and appears on the absence calendar. The responsible approver is notified (bell icon in the Shift Plan).

docs.title: How to approve or deny an absence
docs.text:
Who can do this: RiQS Administrator, Group Administrator, Administrator, Power User, Management, for absences of their unit. Approving your own absence: RiQS Administrator, Group Administrator, Administrator, Power User only. 1. On the Absence tab, open the absence (calendar or list view), or use the notification bell. 2. Click Approve, or click Deny and write the reason.

Result: The status changes. The person who asked sees the outcome as a red dot next to the Shift Plan with a message inside.

docs.title: How to create and schedule a checklist
docs.text:
Who can do this: RiQS Administrator, Group Administrator, Administrator, Power User, Management 1. Go to the Checklist tab and click Create. 2. Enter a title, description, colour, optional guide, and add tasks with Add Task. Click Save. 3. Click Plan, select the checklist, the date and the people. Optionally tick Must be completed by all users, and make it repeat. 4. Click Save.

Result: The checklist appears on the calendar and in the people's Cockpit on the day. You cannot schedule a checklist on a past date.

docs.title: How to view and resolve conflicts
docs.text:
Who can do this: All roles can see conflicts and are notified of absence conflicts. Resolving them (changing the shift or its people): RiQS Administrator, Group Administrator, Administrator, Power User, Management. 1. When there are conflicts, a bar shows Conflicts found with the number. Click View all. 2. The Conflicting Schedule list opens. Search and filter by conflict type, cause, shift type or active/inactive. 3. Open a conflict to add people, change the shift, or add remarks.

Result: Once the cause is gone (for example a person is added), the conflict disappears.

docs.title: Rules to know
docs.text:
• Daily tasks are assigned automatically. Once a day, RIQS assigns that day's shifts and checklists to the people on them. No manual assignment is needed.
  • Cockpit items for shifts and checklists disappear as soon as they are completed, or after 24 hours if not.
  • A checklist stays in the Cockpit until its last task is done.
  • Repeat limits: daily and weekly plans can run up to 3 years ahead; monthly and yearly up to 10 years.
  • Overlap warnings only look at other regular shifts in the same unit. Working in two units on the same day is allowed.
  • The overlap warning does not stop you saving.
  • Change log is kept only for shifts whose date has passed.
  • Absences: every new absence starts as Pending. A standard (organisation) absence is created in every unit the person belongs to.
  • Management and Professionals cannot approve their own absence.
  • Deleting a checklist removes the definition. Checklists already scheduled stay on the calendar (see Open questions).
  • Audit-safe mode: only the RiQS Administrator can delete shifts, absences or checklists.

docs.title: Subscription & billing
docs.text: In one sentence: Decide how many users, how much storage, how many AI tokens and e-signatures an organisation has, and pay for them online or by invoice. Menu: My Organization → organisation → Billing details · unit page → Billing details · Price Config (RiQS Administrator) · Status: Live (billing groups planned)

docs.title: What it is
docs.text:
Every organisation that uses RIQS has a subscription. It is like a phone contract: you choose a package (here: a number of users), you can add extras (storage, AI tokens, electronic signatures), and you pay for a period, usually one year. Before the period ends, RIQS reminds you to renew.

The subscription belongs to the organisation. The organisation can share its storage and tokens out to its units, or allow units to buy extras themselves.

There are two ways to become a customer: - Online signup: the customer chooses a package on the RIQS pricing page, pays online, and then creates the organisation with its Admin and Deputy Admin. - On invoice: a RiQS Administrator creates the organisation for the customer (see Organisation & units). The customer pays an invoice. These organisations are called "offline".

The RiQS Administrator sets all prices in Price Config. Every subscription screen takes its prices from there.

docs.title: Key terms
docs.text: Term Meaning Full-time users The number of users the organisation pays for. Minimum 5. The price is per user and month. Authorised users The number of people who may be active at the same time: twice the number of full-time users (for example 5 full-time users = 10 authorised users). Storage Space for files in RiQS-Pedia (RIQS-Pedia Storage). 0.5 GB per full-time user is included; more can be bought. AI tokens Credit for AI features. Two kinds: Translation Tokens (for languages) and Manual Tokens (equipment manual AI). Bought in millions. E-signatures Electronic signatures: Simple (SES), Advanced (AES), Qualified (QES), plus Authentication for QES (AutoIdent or VideoIdent). Online Payment / By Invoice The two payment methods. By Invoice = "offline". Business year The organisation's financial year. Renewals can be aligned to it. Estimated bill The live price summary shown while choosing a package or extras. Custom package A special price (discount) for a number of users, made in Price Config and shared with a customer as a link. Additional purchase permission Organisation setting: units may buy extras themselves. Shown as Unit has additional purchase permission. Allocation Organisation setting: the organisation shares its tokens and capacity out to units. Shown as Organisation allocates tokens and capacity to units.

docs.title: Who uses it
docs.text: Role What they typically do here RiQS Administrator Sets prices and custom packages, creates invoice customers, marks invoices as paid, unpaid or trial, updates offline organisations. Group Administrator Creates organisations online, views billing, buys user licences, updates and renews subscriptions of the group's organisations, buys and assigns tokens and storage for units. Administrator Views billing, buys user licences, updates and renews the own organisation's subscription, buys and assigns tokens and storage for units. Organisation Admin / Deputy Admin The named billing contacts. They can always view billing. Power User Sees the unit's billing details; buys extras for the unit only if an admin has released this. Management, Professional Not involved.

docs.title: How it works
docs.text:
Choose package → Pay (online) or receive invoice → Active → Update (add more) → Reminders → Renew
  1. Choose. Pick the number of full-time users, the period and any extras. The Estimated bill shows the price, VAT and total.
  2. Pay. Online: Make Payment opens the payment page, then RIQS shows "Processing payment" and returns. If payment fails, a Payment Failed page appears. By invoice: RIQS creates an invoice and the RiQS Administrator later marks it paid.
  3. Active. The organisation and its units can use what was bought. The Billing details tab shows the current package, billing period, expiry date, billing contact, payment method and Billing History (invoices).
  4. Update. During the period you can add users, storage, tokens or signatures with Update subscription. You pay only for the rest of the period.
  5. Reminders. For yearly subscriptions RIQS sends reminders 90, 60, 30 and 15 days before expiry. For shorter periods, 14 days before.
  6. Renew. Renew subscription starts the next period. Any credit is applied to the next cycle.

Invoice statuses (by-invoice customers): Not paid → Paid, or Trial Period. Only the RiQS Administrator changes them.

docs.title: How to sign up online as a new customer
docs.text:
Who can do this: anyone (a new customer). Inside RIQS, the RiQS Administrator and the Group Administrator can also create an organisation online. 1. Open the RIQS pricing page (or a custom package link you received). 2. Choose the number of users and the extras. Check the estimated bill. 3. Pay online. 4. Enter your organisation, then your Organisation Admin and Deputy Admin.

Result: The organisation is created and the admins receive their invitations.

docs.title: How to see billing details and download an invoice
docs.text:
Who can do this: RiQS Administrator, Group Administrator, Administrator, Organisation Admin / Deputy Admin; on unit level also Power User 1. Open the organisation (or unit) and click the Billing details tab. 2. In Billing History, click an invoice to open it, then download it.

Result: The invoice PDF opens. If it does not exist yet, RIQS creates it first.

docs.title: How to add users, storage, tokens or signatures (organisation)
docs.text:
Who can do this: RiQS Administrator, Group Administrator, Administrator 1. On Billing details, click Update subscription. 2. Change the Number of full-time users, add storage (Number of GB), tokens (Number of tokens (in million), minimum 5 million) or e-signatures. 3. Check the Estimated bill and click Proceed to Payment / Make Payment.

Result: "Payment process done and subscription data updated". The new numbers show on the organisation's Overview (usage cards).

docs.title: How to give storage and tokens to a unit
docs.text:
Who can do this: RiQS Administrator, Group Administrator, Administrator; Power User only if an admin has released this (when the organisation allocates tokens and capacity to units) 1. Open the unit and click the Billing details tab. 2. Click the update button for allocation. 3. Enter how much storage, tokens or signatures the unit gets from the organisation. Allocation list shows what was given before. 4. Save.

Result: The unit's balance increases and the organisation's balance decreases.

docs.title: How to buy extras for a unit
docs.text:
Who can do this: RiQS Administrator, Group Administrator, Administrator; Power User only if an admin has released this (the organisation gives units additional purchase permission) 1. Open your unit's Billing details tab and click Update subscription. 2. Choose storage, tokens or signatures and click Make Payment.

Result: The unit balance updates right after payment. An email confirms the purchase.

docs.title: How to set the business year
docs.text:
Who can do this: whoever can see the organisation's billing details 1. On Billing details, click Set Business Year. 2. Choose the start date of the business year and review the two invoices shown. 3. Confirm.

Result: The first invoice covers the time until the business year starts. Renewals then follow the business year.

docs.title: How to mark an invoice as paid (by-invoice customers)
docs.text:
Who can do this: RiQS Administrator 1. Open the organisation's Billing details → Billing History. 2. Open the invoice's action menu and choose Mark as paid (or Mark as unpaid, or mark as trial period). Add payment details and an image if needed.

Result: "Successfully marked as paid". The status changes to Paid.

docs.title: How to set prices and make a custom package
docs.text:
Who can do this: RiQS Administrator 1. Open Price Config. 2. Click Edit Pricing to set: price per user (annual, semi-annual, quarterly), price per GB of storage, price per million tokens, price per SES, AES, QES and QES authentication, and VAT per country (Tax For Countries). 3. To make a special offer, click Add Custom Price, enter the number of users and the discount (percentage, amount, or per-user discount), and save. 4. Use the copy link action to copy the package link and send it to the customer.

Result: New prices apply to all subscription screens. The customer can sign up with the custom package link. Packages already used by a customer are marked Already Used.

docs.title: Rules to know
docs.text:
• Users: minimum 5 full-time users, maximum 500 per organisation in the app. Online customers with more than 200 users are asked to contact RIQS (More than 200 users?).
  • Only active users count. Inactive users do not use up a place. When a unit is full, new users stay inactive.
  • Tokens: if you choose tokens, the minimum is 5 million.
  • Included storage: 0.5 GB per full-time user (for example 5 users = 2.5 GB).
  • Limits are enforced (feature list): when storage is used up, uploads to RiQS-Pedia are blocked; when tokens run out, translations stop. Admins get alerts when storage or tokens run low.
  • Who sees billing: the Organisation Admin and Deputy Admin always; RiQS Administrators, Group Administrators and Administrators too. An organisation needs both an Admin and a Deputy Admin before it can be updated or renewed.
  • Unit updates are only possible for yearly subscriptions. RiQS Administrators, Group Administrators and Administrators buy and assign storage and tokens for units. Power Users do this only when an admin has released it (Unit has additional purchase permission).
  • Offline organisations: the RiQS Administrator can update users and tokens directly. Online organisations are updated by their admins through online payment.
  • Regular to audit-safe: a unit on the regular version can switch to audit-safe later if needed.
  • Notifications: renewal reminders before expiry (see How it works); email when an extra purchase is made at organisation or unit level.
  • Notice period: 90 days before renewal (feature list).
  • Planned: billing groups, where Administrators may only buy categories the organisation allows. Built but not switched on.

  • Users: the number of authorised users limits how many users can be active.
  • RiQS-Pedia (DMS): uses storage.

docs.text:
1. Prices in the feature list: the feature list names CHF 9 per 0.5 GB per month for storage and CHF 4 per 1 million tokens. Prices now come from Price Config. Are these numbers still valid, or should they be removed from the wiki?
  2. Number of reminders: the feature list says three reminder emails before renewal; the system plans four for yearly subscriptions (90, 60, 30, 15 days) and one for shorter ones (14 days). Which is right?
  3. Low balance alerts: at what level of storage or tokens are alerts sent, and to whom? Not found in the app.

docs.title: Surveys
docs.text:
In one sentence: Ask staff, patients or partner units a set of questions, collect their answers, compare the results, and, for certifications, have an auditor and a committee check them before a final report is written. Menu: Surveys · Status: Live (some parts planned, see below)

Survey dashboard: package and single surveys by status, and the survey list. Screens show test data.

docs.title: What it is
docs.text:
Surveys lets a unit or an organisation send out a questionnaire and see the results in one place. The questions are not typed in here. They come from a survey template that someone has built beforehand in the Configurator. In the Surveys module you pick the template, decide who should answer and by when, and then follow the answers as they come in.

There are two kinds of survey:

  • A General Survey is a single questionnaire. Example: a yearly staff satisfaction survey.
  • A Certification Package is a bundle: one main survey plus one or more sub-surveys (for example one for staff and one for patients). Once enough answers are in, the package goes through an audit and a committee review. Think of it like an exam: people answer the questions, an examiner (the auditor) checks the work and can send parts back, and an exam board (the committee) gives the final verdict, Certified or Denied.

People inside RIQS answer from the Surveys module or from their Workflow-Navi. People outside RIQS (patients, partner units, external auditors) answer through a link or a QR code, without logging in.

At the end, RIQS shows an evaluation: points per question, how many people answered, and how a person or unit compares with the others (the benchmark). A final report can then be created from a report template and downloaded as a PDF.

docs.title: Key terms
docs.text: Term Meaning General Survey A single survey with its own template, participants and due date. Certification Package A main survey plus at least one sub-survey, with an optional audit and committee review. Main survey / Sub-survey The parts of a certification package. The main survey goes to the unit's Power Users. Sub-surveys are shared with the people who should answer them. Survey template The question list, built in the Configurator. Each answer option can carry points. Basic points / Advanced points Points given per answer option (1 to 5, 1 by default). They are used to score each response. Minimum response How many answers are needed before the survey counts as complete. Minimum basic points The score (as a percentage) a survey should reach. Participants The people the survey is shared with. They can be internal (RIQS users) or external (anyone with the link). Auditor A function role. The person who reviews a certification package, adds remarks, and approves it or sends surveys back. Can be a RIQS user or an external email address. Committee A function role. The person or people who make the final decision: Certify or Decline. Can be internal or external. Send back The auditor returns one or more surveys for correction, with remarks. Close survey Stop collecting answers. The survey moves to Closed. Active / Inactive An inactive survey is hidden from the normal list and accepts no answers or actions. Evaluation The results screen, with the Organization, Units and Individuals tabs. Final report The formal report built from a report template. It can be saved as Draft and later as Completed. Admin View A switch for administrators to see surveys across the whole organisation instead of one unit.

docs.title: Who uses it
docs.text: Role What they typically do here RiQS Administrator Supports clients. Sees surveys across organisations. The only role that can Reopen a closed survey, and the only role that can delete in audit-safe mode. Cannot act as auditor or committee. Group Administrator Creates organisation-level surveys and packages, shares them with units, follows progress in Admin View. Administrator Same as Group Administrator for their own organisation. Power User Runs surveys for their unit: creates, shares, closes, sends to the auditor and writes the final report. Receives the main survey of a package. Management Runs surveys at unit level, like a Power User: creates, shares, closes, sends to the auditor and writes the final report. Sees the surveys assigned to them on the dashboard. Answers surveys shared with them. Professional Answers surveys shared with them (from the Cockpit) and sees their own result compared with the unit. Does not open the Survey dashboard. Auditor Reviews the packages they are named on. Adds remarks, approves or sends back. Committee Reviews the packages they are named on. Certifies or declines, with a comment. External participant Fills in a survey through a link or QR code, without an account.

docs.title: How it works
docs.text:
General Survey

  1. A Power User or administrator creates the survey from a template and assigns it to units.
  2. They share it with participants (internal users, and/or external people through a link or QR code).
  3. Participants fill it in. The completion bar grows.
  4. The creator closes the survey (it can also stop taking answers on its due date, if set up that way), marks it as completed, and generates the final report.

Ongoing → Closed → Final Report → Completed

Certification Package

  1. An administrator or Power User creates the package: main survey, sub-surveys, auditor and committee.
  2. The main survey goes to the Power Users of each assigned unit. Sub-surveys are shared with participants.
  3. When enough answers are in, the unit clicks Send to Auditor.
  4. The auditor reviews everything. They either Send Back some surveys with remarks (the package returns to Ongoing and the participants correct only the affected questions), or Approve.
  5. After approval, the unit clicks Send to Committee.
  6. The committee Certifies or Declines, with a comment. Either way the package moves on to the final report, with the decision recorded.
  7. The unit generates the final report, saves it as draft as often as needed, and then saves it as final.

Ongoing → Closed → Audit Review → Audit Completed → Committee Review → Final Report → Completed

If no audit is set up, the package can be marked complete directly after Ongoing / Closed. If audit is set up but no committee, it can be marked complete after Audit Completed.

Statuses you can see

Status What it means What moves it on Ongoing Answers are being collected. Close Survey, Send to Auditor or Mark as Completed. Closed No more answers are collected. Send to Auditor or Mark as Completed. A RiQS Administrator can Reopen it. Audit Review The auditor is checking the package. Auditor clicks Approve (to Audit Completed) or Send Back (back to Ongoing). Audit Completed The audit is approved. Send to Committee, or Mark as Completed if no committee is set up. Committee Review The committee is deciding. Committee clicks Certify or Decline. Final Report The final report is being written. Saving the report as final. Completed Finished. Read-only. —

The committee decision is shown separately as Certified or Denied, and you can filter by it. Separately from the status, any survey can be Active or Inactive.

docs.title: Planned (not built yet)
docs.text:
These are in the requirements but not (or not fully) built yet:

  • Full organisation cockpit: Admin View already lists surveys by organisation and unit. Still planned: building org-level surveys there before assigning them, an organisation-level consolidated report, and year-over-year comparison.
  • Audit setup at the "Send to Auditor" step only, instead of at package creation.
  • Coded links for external units, so every sub-survey answer can be traced to the right external unit (including lists such as doctors).
  • Organisation vs. group benchmark in the evaluation, and a user list question filtered by designation.
  • Marked pending: full anonymity behaviour, committee data masking, minimum responses per doctor, extra report elements (response rate, duration, past summary), and a progress bar with a threshold marker.

docs.title: How to create a General Survey
docs.text:
Who can do this: RiQS Administrator, Group Administrator, Administrator; Power User and Management at unit level only (see Open questions) 1. Open Surveys and click Create Survey. Choose General Survey. 2. Pick the survey template under Select survey template. Add a Description if you like. 3. Under Assigned to, choose the organisation and the units. 4. Optional: set Minimum response, the minimum required responses per user, the minimum points, and a Due date. You can choose that responses close after the due date. 5. Optional: switch on Allow anonymity. 6. Choose the report template for the final report, then click Create.

Result: the survey appears in the list with status Ongoing. Now share it (see below).

docs.title: How to create a Certification Package
docs.text:
Who can do this: RiQS Administrator, Group Administrator, Administrator; Power User and Management at unit level only (see Open questions) 1. Click Create Survey and choose Certification Package. 2. Survey information step: enter the package name (at least 3 characters) and a description. Set up the Main Survey (template, minimum response, minimum basic points, due date). Add at least one Sub-survey with Add Sub-survey. 3. Leave Enable audit process on if an auditor should check the package. Optionally enter an internal auditor or an External auditor email. 4. Leave Enable external committee review on if a committee should decide. Add committee members (internal, or external email addresses). 5. Assignment step: choose the organisation and units. Click Create.

Result: the package appears with status Ongoing. The main survey is sent to the Power Users of each assigned unit automatically.

docs.title: How to share a survey with participants
docs.text:
Who can do this: RiQS Administrator, Group Administrator, Administrator, Power User, Management (see Open questions). Everyone, including Professionals, can download the QR code. 1. In the list, open the row menu of the survey or sub-survey and click Share Survey. This works only while the survey is Ongoing and Active. 2. Internal users tab: pick people, or whole user groups (for example all Professionals of the unit). 3. External users tab: enter the expected number of external participants. Use Copy Link or the QR code (download it to print or display). 4. Click Share.

Result: internal users get a Fill Survey task in their Cockpit. External people can answer through the link. People who have already answered cannot be removed.

Administrators can also share a whole package with other units, or with External units by email, from Admin View. Each email address gets its own invitation.

docs.title: How to fill in a survey
docs.text:
Who can do this: anyone the survey is shared with (internal or external) 1. Internal users: click the task in the Cockpit, or Fill Survey in the survey's row menu. External users: open the link or scan the QR code, then enter name and email (and, for external units, the unit name and ID) and click Start Survey. 2. Answer the questions and submit.

Result: the answer is counted and the completion bar moves. External users see a thank-you page. Afterwards you can open your answer with View Response.

docs.title: How to close, reopen, deactivate or delete a survey
docs.text:
Who can do this: RiQS Administrator, Group Administrator, Administrator; Power User and Management at unit level only. Delete in audit-safe mode: RiQS Administrator only. Reopen: RiQS Administrator only. 1. Open the row menu. 2. Click Close Survey to stop collecting answers, Inactive / Active to switch the survey off or on, or Delete to remove it (you are asked to confirm).

Result: a closed survey shows Closed and accepts no more answers. External users see "This survey is closed".

docs.title: How to send a package to the auditor
docs.text:
Who can do this: RiQS Administrator, Group Administrator, Administrator; Power User and Management at unit level only 1. Open the package and click Send to Auditor. 2. Check or choose the auditor (an internal person and/or an external email). 3. Choose what the auditor may see: Entire survey, the main survey only, or selected sub-surveys. Set the view permissions (statistics and/or individual answers). 4. Optional: attach one or more documents (attachment templates from the Configurator). 5. Click Send.

Result: status Audit Review. The auditor gets a Cockpit task, or an email if external.

docs.title: How to review a package as auditor
docs.text:
Who can do this: the named Auditor (internal or external). A Group Administrator, Administrator, Power User or Management user can do this only if they are named as auditor. RiQS Administrators and Professionals cannot (see Open questions). 1. Open the package from your Cockpit task (or the email link). 2. Read the answers and evaluation. Add remarks on single questions where needed. 3. Click Send Back to return selected surveys with remarks, or Approve and enter a comment.

Result: Send Back returns the package to Ongoing. A Group Administrator, Administrator or Power User of the unit can Re-share the sub-survey (to the same or new people), and they answer only the flagged questions. Approve moves the package to Audit Completed.

docs.title: How to give the committee decision
docs.text:
Who can do this: the named Committee member (internal or external). A Group Administrator, Administrator, Power User or Management user can do this only if they are named as committee. RiQS Administrators and Professionals cannot (see Open questions). 1. The unit clicks Send to Committee on a package in Audit Completed. 2. The committee member opens the package, reads the results and the auditor's remarks. 3. They click Certify or Decline and write a comment (the comment is required).

Result: the decision (Certified or Denied) is saved and the package moves to Final Report.

docs.title: How to generate the final report
docs.text:
Who can do this: RiQS Administrator, Group Administrator, Administrator; Power User and Management at unit level only (see Open questions). Preview and download: everyone except Professionals. 1. Open the survey or package and click Generate Report. 2. Choose the report template. 3. Fill in the report. It can include evaluations, charts, benchmarks, auditor remarks and committee remarks. Save it as Draft as often as you like. 4. When ready, save it as final.

Result: the report is Completed, and so is the survey. All reports are listed in the Reports tab, with filters for type, status, creator and date. You can preview and download them as PDF.

docs.title: How to see the results
docs.text:
Who can do this: see "Who can do what" 1. Open the survey and go to its evaluation (View Responses). 2. Use the tabs: Organization (administrators only), Units (results compared with the benchmark), Individuals (each person's answers and points).

Result: you see question-level averages, points, number of answers, charts and benchmark comparisons.

docs.title: Rules to know
docs.text:
• A survey can only be filled in while it is Ongoing and Active, and only by people it is shared with.
  • A certification package needs at least one sub-survey. Package and survey names need at least 3 characters. A report template is required.
  • The main survey of a certification package goes to the unit's Power Users automatically. It cannot be shared with external people, but sub-surveys and General Surveys can.
  • For external answers, only the latest answer per email address is kept. The link works until the survey is closed or set to inactive.
  • If a due date is set and "responses close after due date" is chosen, the survey stops accepting answers on that date.
  • Power Users and Management manage surveys at unit level only. Organisation-level surveys (created in Admin View) are managed by administrators.
  • Only the auditor named on a package can review it, add audit remarks and approve. Only the named committee can add committee remarks and certify or decline. A RiQS Administrator or a Professional cannot take either role.
  • After an audit send-back, the people the survey was shared with (any role, including Professionals) edit only the flagged questions.
  • Approve, Certify and Decline always need a comment.
  • Users can edit or delete only their own remarks. An auditor can edit only the remark they are currently writing.
  • External auditors and committee members get emails. Internal users get Cockpit tasks and a red dot in the module. The bell icon groups notifications into Ongoing, Audit Review, Committee Review, Sent Back and Final Report.
  • Deleting a survey or package is a soft delete. In audit-safe mode, only the RiQS Administrator can delete a survey, a package or a final report.
