docs.title: Training
docs.text:
In one sentence: Build short online trainings with test questions, assign them to the right people with a due date, and see who has passed and who has not. Menu: Training (people who only take trainings open them from their Workflow-Navi) · Status: Live

Training: assigned trainings, who still has to complete them, and status. Screens show test data.

docs.title: What it is
docs.text:
Every practice has things staff must know and prove they know: hygiene rules, how to use a device, data protection. Training in RIQS is a simple way to do this online. It works like a short quiz with reading material.

It has two parts:

  1. The training module is the content. It has a description, optional documents or links, and multiple-choice questions with the correct answers marked. It also has a Fulfilment Level: the percentage of correct answers needed to pass (for example 80 %). Training modules are built in the Configurator, under Configurator, tab Trainings.
  2. The training assignment is what you manage in the Training menu. You pick a module, choose the units and people who must take it, and set a due date. RIQS then tells those people, and keeps track of who has passed.

People take the training, see right away whether they passed, and can try again as often as needed. Managers see a list of who has completed the training and who has not, and can download a report as proof, for example for an inspection.

docs.title: Key terms
docs.text: Term Meaning Training module The content: description, attachments and questions. Built in the Configurator. Training (assignment) A training module given to units and people, with a due date. This is what the Training list shows. Topic The subject area of the training (for example Topic 1 to Topic 10 as set up for your organisation). Used to find and filter trainings. Sector / Sub group Further grouping of trainings, shown as columns in the list. Fulfilment Level The pass mark, from 0 to 100 %. Shown in the details as Criteria for completion. Assignment Who must take the training: all employees of the unit, selected users, or selected User-Groups (Power User, Management, Professional). Supervisory group The people who follow the training (Management). Attempt / tries Each time a person submits the training. All attempts are kept. Best Score A person's highest score. This is the score that counts. Completed / Not completed yet Completed means the person's best score reached the Fulfilment Level. Active / Inactive An inactive training is switched off but kept.

docs.title: Who uses it
docs.text: Role What they typically do here RiQS Administrator Supports clients. Can see and manage trainings and delete them, also in audit-safe mode. Group Administrator Assigns trainings to many units at once and follows progress. Administrator Same as Group Administrator for their own organisation. Power User Assigns trainings in their unit (or several units), follows progress, edits and deletes trainings. Management Assigns trainings, follows progress, edits and switches trainings on or off. Cannot delete trainings. Takes trainings assigned to them. Professional Takes the trainings assigned to them, from the Workflow-Navi. Sees only their own results. Does not see inactive trainings or reports.

docs.title: How it works
docs.text:
1. Build the module. In the Configurator, someone creates the training module: title, sector, topic, Fulfilment Level, description, attachments and questions.
  2. Assign it. In Training, a manager clicks Assign Training, picks the topic and module, the units, the people and a due date.
  3. People are told. Each assigned person gets a task in their Workflow-Navi and an email.
  4. People take it. They open the training, read the material, click Start Training, answer all questions and click Submit.
  5. Instant result. RIQS shows Training Passed! or Training Not Passed with the percentage reached. If they did not pass, they can try again.
  6. Follow up. Managers see per training how many people have not completed it yet, look at each answer, and download reports.

From the point of view of one person:

not yet started → Incomplete (tried, not passed yet) → Completed (passed)

The training itself is either Active or Inactive. The due date shows as End in (days left) or Overdue by (days late). The due date does not block anyone from taking the training late.

docs.title: How to create a training module
docs.text:
Who can do this: see the Configurator page 1. Go to Configurator and open the Trainings tab. Click Create Training. 2. Basic Information: enter Title, sector, Topic and Fulfilment Level (0–100). Add a description and attachments if you like. 3. Choose which organisations and units can use the module. 4. Add questions. For each question, add options with Add Option, and mark at least one option as correct (several can be correct). You can add an explanation to each option and attach files to questions and options. 5. Use Add More Question until done, then save.

Result: the module can now be picked when assigning a training.

docs.title: How to assign a training
docs.text:
Who can do this: RiQS Administrator, Group Administrator, Administrator, Power User, Management 1. Open Training and click Assign Training. 2. Select the topic, then select the training module. The training takes its title from the module. 3. Select the unit. You can pick several units or use Select all units (see Open questions). 4. Under Assignment, either leave it as "The training is assigned to all employees", or choose Select user and/or Select User-Groups. 5. Pick the Due Date and click Save.

Result: the training appears in the list. Assigned people get a Cockpit task and an email. A person who belongs to several selected units gets the training only once.

docs.title: How to take a training
docs.text:
Who can do this: anyone the training is assigned to, in any role (see Open questions) 1. Open the task in your Workflow-Navi (or open the training from the list). 2. Read the description and attachments. Click Start Training. 3. Answer every question. Questions and answer options appear in random order. Each question may have more than one correct answer, and the screen does not tell you how many. 4. Click Submit.

Result: you see Training Passed! or Training Not Passed with your percentage. If you did not pass, start again. Your best score is kept. Once you pass, any Training To-Do for it is marked done automatically.

docs.title: How to follow progress
docs.text:
Who can do this: RiQS Administrator, Group Administrator, Administrator, Power User, Management 1. Open Training. The list shows title, sector, sub group, Assigned to, Not completed yet, Assigned On, Due Date and Status. 2. Search by name, unit or topic, or click Filters (topic, sector, assignment, submitted by, due date, required completion rate, Active / Inactive, and Completed / Not completed). 3. Click a training to open Training Details. Completed response lists who passed. Pending response lists who has not. 4. Click a person's entry to see each attempt: score, number of tries and their answers.

Result: you know who still has to complete the training.

docs.title: How to download a training report
docs.text:
Who can do this: RiQS Administrator, Group Administrator, Administrator, Power User, Management 1. In the list, click Download Report for an overview of trainings. Or open a training and use Download Report in its menu for the details of that one training.

Result: RIQS prepares the report ("Training report creation in process") and downloads it.

docs.title: How to edit, deactivate or delete a training
docs.text:
Who can do this: edit and deactivate: RiQS Administrator, Group Administrator, Administrator, Power User, Management. Delete: RiQS Administrator, Group Administrator, Administrator, Power User. In audit-safe mode, a training that is already assigned can only be deleted by the RiQS Administrator. 1. Open the training and use its menu: Edit Training, Inactive Training / Activate Training, or Delete. 2. In Edit Training you can change the title, due date, units and people. The module itself cannot be changed here. 3. To delete several trainings at once, tick them in the list and click Delete, then confirm.

Result: changes are saved. A new title is also copied to the related To-Dos.

docs.title: Rules to know
docs.text:
• Assigning needs a topic, a module, at least one unit and a due date.
  • Pass rule: a person passes when their best score reaches the module's Fulfilment Level. The score is the share of multiple-choice questions answered fully correctly. A question only counts as correct if exactly the right options are ticked.
  • All questions must be answered before Submit works.
  • There is no limit on attempts. Every attempt is stored and shown in the response history.
  • Assigned people get an email when an active training is assigned or updated, and a Cockpit task.
  • A Training To-Do (in Open Items) can only go to people who have not already passed that training. Passing the training completes the To-Do.
  • A training with different participant groups per unit cannot be edited in the drawer. The app asks you to contact support.
  • Delete in the regular version: RiQS Administrator, Group Administrator, Administrator and Power User. In audit-safe mode, a training that is already assigned can only be deleted by the RiQS Administrator.
  • Professionals do not see the Training list. They reach their trainings through the Cockpit and see only their own results. They do not see inactive trainings.

docs.text: Action RiQS Administrator Group Administrator Administrator Power User Management Professional Open the Training list, search, filter ✅ ✅ ✅ ✅ ✅ ❌ (Cockpit only) Assign a training ✅ ✅ ✅ ✅ ✅ ❌ Assign to several units at once ✅ ✅ ✅ ✅ (see Open questions) ✅ (see Open questions) ❌ Edit a training ✅ ✅ ✅ ✅ ✅ ❌ Activate / deactivate ✅ ✅ ✅ ✅ ✅ ❌ Delete (regular, or audit-safe and not yet assigned) ✅ ✅ ✅ ✅ ❌ ❌ Delete (audit-safe, already assigned) ✅ ❌ ❌ ❌ ❌ ❌ View training details and everyone's answers (all completed trainings) ✅ ✅ ✅ ✅ ✅ Own only See inactive trainings ✅ ✅ ✅ ✅ ✅ ❌ Take an assigned training If assigned (see Open questions) If assigned (see Open questions) If assigned If assigned If assigned If assigned See own result, attempts and best score ✅ ✅ ✅ ✅ ✅ ✅ Download reports ✅ ✅ ✅ ✅ ✅ ❌ Receive assignment notification If assigned If assigned If assigned ✅ ✅ ✅

docs.title: Connected modules
docs.text:
• Configurator: training modules (questions, answers, Fulfilment Level, attachments) are built there.
  • Cockpit: assigned people find their trainings here as tasks.
  • Open Items: Training To-Dos follow the training assignment and close when the person passes.
  • Users: the units, users and user groups you assign to come from here.
  • Reports & downloads: training overview and training detail reports.

docs.title: Open questions
docs.text:
• Qualifications. Users have a Qualifications section in their profile, and the organisation's group builder shows an "Education Group" catalogue meant for the Training module. Passing a training does not update either one today. Should a passed training be recorded as a qualification, and is the Education Group catalogue planned?
  • Pass mark at exactly the Fulfilment Level. The training screen counts a person as passed when the score equals the Fulfilment Level. The stored "completed by" list counts them only when the score is higher. So someone with exactly 80 % on an 80 % training may show as passed in one place and not in another. Which rule is right?
  • Power Users, Management and several units (role table vs feature list). The role table lets every role that can assign a training do so without a unit limit. The feature list says only administrators may assign a training to several units. This page follows the role table. Please confirm.
  • Group Administrator and RiQS Administrator taking trainings (role table vs feature list). The role table says they can complete and view assigned trainings like everyone else. The feature list says they only see other people's answers and cannot start a training. This page follows the role table. Please confirm.
  • Save without submitting. The feature list mentions "save or submit". The app only has Submit, so a half-done attempt cannot be saved. Is a save option still wanted?
  • Default topic. The feature list asks for "Topic 0 Standard" to be pre-selected when assigning, and for a topic filter defaulting to "all". This is not visible in the current assign drawer. Is it still required?
  • Inactive and overdue trainings. Can a person still start a training that has been set to Inactive, or that is past its due date? The app does not clearly block either case.
  • Topic names. Topics show placeholder names such as "Topic 1" to "Topic 10". What are the real on-screen names?
  • File-upload questions. The answer screen can show file-upload questions, but the module builder only offers multiple-choice. File answers are not scored. Is the file-upload question type still in use?

docs.title: Tutorials, Handbook and About
docs.text:
In one sentence: RIQS has built-in help: short videos and a PDF manual for each module, a page where administrators manage that content, and an About page with the version number. Menu: Handbook (managing help content) and About, lower part of the left menu. The help viewer opens from a help button on the module pages. · Status: Live (see Open questions for the start-up introduction)

Handbook: manuals and videos per module and language. Screens show test data.

docs.title: What it is
docs.text:
When users are unsure how a module works, they should not need to leave RIQS or call support. Each module therefore has its own help:

  • a video tutorial (one or more short videos), and
  • a manual (a PDF document, also called the handbook).

Users open this help on the page they are working on. A help panel opens with the videos and the manual for that module, in English or German.

Administrators manage this content in the Handbook menu. Here they upload, replace and delete videos and manuals for each module and language. This admin page is called the Handbook on screen.

The About page shows which version of RIQS you are using. It also shows the copyright and the provider (SELISE).

docs.title: Key terms
docs.text: Term Meaning Help panel The panel that opens from the help button on a module page. It shows Video Tutorial and Documentation. Video tutorial A short video that explains a module. A module can have several videos, each with a title and description. Manual / Handbook A PDF guide for a module. There is one manual per module and language. Tutorial language The language of the help content: English (EN) or German (DE).

docs.title: Who uses it
docs.text: Role What they typically do here RiQS Administrator Uploads and maintains videos and manuals for all modules in the Handbook menu. Group Administrator Watches videos and reads manuals. Administrator Watches videos and reads manuals. May manage content (see Open questions). Power User Watches videos and reads manuals. Management Watches videos and reads manuals. Professional Watches videos and reads manuals.

docs.title: How it works
docs.text:
Admin uploads video / manual per module and language → users open help on the module page → watch or read

  • The help panel knows which module you are in and shows its content.
  • In the panel you can switch to the help of another module, change the Tutorial language, open a video in full screen, or open the manual.
  • If a module has no content yet, the panel shows the general introduction instead.

Modules with their own help content include:

  • Cockpit, Monitoring, Training, Shift Plan, To-Dos, Process Guide, Forms
  • Risk Management, Equipment, RiQS-Pedia, Surveys
  • Incident reports (CIRS, hints, ideas, employee feedback, complaints, faults)
  • Organisations, Units, Users
  • Downloads, Interface Manager, RiQS IT

docs.title: How to open help for a module
docs.text:
Who can do this: all roles 1. Go to the module, for example Equipment. 2. Click the help button. 3. Choose Video Tutorial or Documentation. Change the language if needed.

Result: The video plays, or the manual opens.

docs.title: How to add a video tutorial
docs.text:
Who can do this: users who see the Handbook menu (see Open questions) 1. Click Handbook in the left menu. The Handbook overview lists all modules. For each module it shows which languages already have a manual and videos. 2. Open a module and choose the language tab (English or German). 3. Click Add Video Tutorial. Enter a Title (required) and an optional description. Choose the video file. 4. Click Save.

Result: The video is added to the module's playlist for that language. You can edit it later (Edit video) or delete it (Delete video).

docs.title: How to upload or replace a manual
docs.text:
Who can do this: users who see the Handbook menu 1. Open the module in Handbook and choose the language tab. 2. Click Add Manual (or Re-upload Manual if one exists). Choose a PDF file. 3. Click Save.

Result: The manual is available in the help panel. A re-upload replaces the old manual. Delete manual removes it.

docs.title: How to see the RIQS version
docs.text:
Who can do this: all roles 1. Click About in the left menu.

Result: You see the version number, the copyright and "Technology & Design by SELISE digital platforms".

docs.title: Rules to know
docs.text:
• Manuals: PDF only, maximum 10 MB. One manual per module and language. Uploading again replaces it.
  • Videos: MP4, 3GP, AVI, WEBM, GIF or MPEG-4, maximum 500 MB each. A module can have several videos per language. Each video needs a title.
  • Languages: help content exists in English and German.
  • About is always visible to every user, whatever their role.
  • The help panel's language choice only changes the help content, not the language of RIQS.

docs.title: Who can do what
docs.text: Action RiQS Administrator Group Administrator Administrator Power User Management Professional Open help (videos, manual) on module pages ✅ ✅ ✅ ✅ ✅ ✅ Open About ✅ ✅ ✅ ✅ ✅ ✅ Open the Handbook menu ✅ open question open question open question ❌ ❌ Add, edit, delete videos ✅ open question open question open question ❌ ❌ Upload, replace, delete manuals ✅ open question open question open question ❌ ❌

docs.title: Connected modules
docs.text:
• Every module page can open its help content.
  • Interface Manager, RiQS IT and Reports and downloads have their own help content.

docs.title: Open questions
docs.text:
• Who manages help content? The roles & rights sheets do not cover the Handbook menu. Which roles should manage videos and manuals (RiQS Administrator only, or also Group Administrator, Administrator or Power User)? Can customers upload their own content, or does it apply to all customers?
  • Start-up introduction. The previous app showed an introduction tutorial after login, which users could hide. The new app does not show it yet. Is it still wanted?
  • Other languages. Help content exists only in English and German. Are French, Italian or other languages planned?

docs.title: Users
docs.text:
In one sentence: Invite people to RIQS, give them a role in one or more units, and control whether they can log in. Menu: Users (your own details: your picture or name → Profile) · Status: Live

Users: name, unit, role, last login and date of creation. Screens show test data.

docs.title: What it is
docs.text:
Every person who works with RIQS needs a user account. The account says who the person is (name, email, professional details), which units they work in and which role they have in each unit. The role decides what they can see and do. See Roles & permissions.

Think of it like the staff list and key cabinet of a practice: the list says who works where, and the keys say which doors each person may open. Deactivating a user is like taking back the keys without removing the person from the records.

A user is invited by email. The invited person sets their own password with the link in the email. Only then can they log in. Each unit has a maximum number of active users, set by the subscription. See Subscription & billing.

docs.title: Key terms
docs.text: Term Meaning Role What a user may do: RiQS Administrator, Group Administrator, Administrator, Power User, Management or Professional. Function role An extra job on top of the role, for example CIRS Officer or Equipment Officer. It is given inside the module concerned, not in the user form. Primary unit The user's main unit. RIQS opens it after login. Shown as Primary Unit. Other units Further units the user may work in, each with its own role. Active / Inactive Only active users can log in. Only active users count against the unit's user limit. Activation email The invitation email with a link to set a password. Shown as Send activation E-mail / Resend activation E-mail. Group admin A user who manages several organisations. Set with Assign as group admin. Administrator for all units A user who is Administrator of all units of the chosen organisation(s). Set with the Same for all department tick box. Audit-safe mode A unit setting where data can hardly be deleted. See Organisation & units.

docs.title: Who uses it
docs.text: Role What they typically do here RiQS Administrator Manages any user, including administrators, in any organisation; the only role that deletes activated users in audit-safe units. Group Administrator Manages users of all organisations in the group; can make other users group admins. Administrator Manages users of the own organisation; can give users several units, make users Administrator and delete users; changes email addresses. Power User Invites and maintains users of the own unit, activates and deactivates them, makes users Power User of the own unit. Management Invites and maintains users of the own unit, activates and deactivates them. Professional Looks up colleagues; keeps own profile and password up to date.

docs.title: How it works
docs.text:
Invited (inactive, email not verified)  →  Password set (email verified)  →  Active  ⇄  Inactive  →  (Deleted)
  1. Create. An authorised user fills in the Add User form: personal details, contact details, professional details, organisation, units and roles.
  2. Invite. RIQS sends an activation email to the new user, as long as the unit has a free place.
  3. Activate. The user opens the link and sets a password. The email is now verified and the user is active.
  4. Work. The user logs in and lands in the primary unit.
  5. Change. Admins edit details, add units, change roles or change the email address.
  6. Deactivate. Switch the Status off. The user can no longer log in, but all their records stay. The place in the unit becomes free.
  7. Delete (rare). Removes the user account. In audit-safe units this is restricted (see Rules).

The user list shows Name, Unit (primary and other units), Role, Designation, and for admins also Last Login, Date of Creation and Status. A badge warns when the unit has reached its active user limit, for example "Active user limit reached (10/10)".

docs.title: How to add (invite) a user
docs.text:
Who can do this: RiQS Administrator, Group Administrator, Administrator, Power User, Management 1. Open Users and click Add User. 2. Step 1 (General & professional information): enter first name, last name, display name, email address and date of birth (all required). Add optional details: salutation, gender, nationality, languages, photo, phone, academic title, workload, GLN, ZSR, K and Ku numbers, qualifications and remarks. 3. Click Next. Step 2 (Organisational): choose the organisation, then the Primary Unit and the role in that unit. Add designation, date of joining, business phone and extension if you like. 4. Optional: tick User can create process guide (only for Power User or Management in units that use Process Guide). 5. Optional (admins only): click to add another unit, tick Same for all department or Assign as group admin. 6. Click Save.

Result: "User created successfully". The user appears in the list as inactive and receives the activation email.

docs.title: How to resend the activation email
docs.text:
Who can do this: RiQS Administrator, Group Administrator, Administrator, Power User, Management 1. In Users, find the inactive user. 2. Click Resend activation E-mail in the row.

Result: A new email is sent. The button is disabled if the user has already set a password or if the unit is full.

docs.title: How to set a password for a user
docs.text:
Who can do this: RiQS Administrator, Group Administrator, Administrator (initial activation of another user) 1. Open an inactive user's details. 2. Click Set password, enter the new password twice and save.

Result: The user can log in with this password. Not possible while the unit is full.

docs.title: How to edit a user, add units or change roles
docs.text:
Who can do this: RiQS Administrator, Group Administrator, Administrator, Power User, Management (with limits, see Rules) 1. In Users, open the row's menu and click Edit User. 2. Change the details. On the Organisational step, change the role per unit, or add or remove units. 3. Click Save.

Result: "User updated successfully". If you edited your own account, some changes apply after you log out and in again.

docs.title: How to change a user's email address
docs.text:
Who can do this: RiQS Administrator, Group Administrator, Administrator, Power User, Management (see Open questions) 1. Edit the user and change Email Address. RIQS checks that the address is not already used. 2. Click Save.

Result: The user receives an email at the new address and logs in with the new address and the old password.

docs.title: How to activate or deactivate a user
docs.text:
Who can do this: RiQS Administrator, Group Administrator, Administrator, Power User, Management 1. In Users, find the user. 2. Switch the Status toggle on or off.

Result: The user is active or inactive. You can only switch a user on if they have set their password and the unit has a free place.

docs.title: How to delete a user
docs.text:
Who can do this: RiQS Administrator, Group Administrator, Administrator. In audit-safe units: these three only while the user has never been activated; after activation only the RiQS Administrator. 1. In Users, open the row's menu and click Delete. 2. Confirm Delete User.

Result: The user is removed. If you delete yourself, you are logged out.

docs.title: How to search, filter and download the user list
docs.text:
Who can do this: search and filter: everyone who can open Users; download: everyone except Professional 1. Type in the search box to find by name. 2. Click the filter button and choose organisation, unit, name, role, designation, creation date range or status (All, Active, Inactive). Click Apply Filter. 3. Click the download button (Export report) to create an Excel file of the list.

Result: The list shows only matching users. The report is created in the background and appears in your downloads.

docs.title: How to update your own profile and password
docs.text:
Who can do this: everyone 1. Open your Profile. 2. Overview and Organisation tabs show your details, units and roles. Click edit to change your general and professional information or your photo. 3. Security tab: enter your current password and the new one twice. The screen shows the password rules (at least 8 characters, upper- and lower-case letters, a number and a special character).

Result: "Password updated successfully". Your profile changes are saved.

docs.title: Rules to know
docs.text:
• Required fields: first name, last name (max 25 characters each), display name, email and date of birth. Date of joining is optional and stays empty unless entered.
  • Email must be unique. RIQS checks it while you type.
  • User limit: each unit has a maximum number of active ("authorised") users. Only active users count. A user created in a full unit stays inactive and cannot be activated until a place is free.
  • Several units: only RiQS Administrators, Group Administrators and Administrators can give a user more than one unit. Users of several units who are not admins choose the unit at login. Admins use the Unit Switcher.
  • Primary unit at login: admins always start in their primary unit.
  • Who can give which role:
  • Administrator: only RiQS Administrators, Group Administrators and Administrators. The new Administrator must be a Power User.
  • Power User in one unit: the above and Power Users.
  • Power User with access to several units: only RiQS Administrators, Group Administrators and Administrators.
  • CIRS Officer at organisation level: only RiQS Administrators, Group Administrators and Administrators.
  • Who can edit whom:
  • Only RiQS Administrators can edit RiQS Administrators.
  • Only Administrators and RiQS Administrators can edit an Administrator.
  • A Group Administrator cannot edit another Group Administrator who works in different organisations.
  • Cannot be deleted: the Organisation Admin and Deputy Admin of an organisation (warning "Cannot delete an organization admin user"), and RiQS system administrators.
  • Hidden group admins: Power Users, Management and Professionals do not see Group Administrators in the user list or in downloaded lists.
  • Audit-safe mode: a user who was never activated may be deleted by RiQS Administrator, Group Administrator and Administrator; after activation only the RiQS Administrator may delete. Otherwise deactivate.
  • Emails sent: activation email on create (and on Resend activation E-mail); email to the new address when the email is changed. If the activation link has expired, the user sees a message and an admin must resend the email.
  • Professional replaces the old role "Employee A". The old "Employee B" role no longer exists.

docs.title: CIRS (Critical Incident Reporting)
docs.text: In one sentence: Staff report critical incidents and near misses anonymously, so the organisation can learn from them without blaming anyone. Menu: Reporting module → tab CIRS · Status: Live

docs.title: What it is
docs.text:
CIRS stands for "Critical Incident Reporting System". It is for events where something went wrong or nearly went wrong, for example a mix-up of two patients' samples that was caught just in time.

The goal is learning, not blame. That is why every CIRS report is anonymous: nobody, not even the officer, sees who wrote it.

A CIRS report is first checked by the CIRS Officer in the column To Be Approved. Only after approval does the rest of the unit see it. The officer then plans and tracks measures, and can share the case with the outside network CIRRNET or with an external reporting office.

This page adds the CIRS details to the general Incident Reports page.

docs.title: Key terms
docs.text: Term Meaning Near miss An error that was caught before it caused harm. Also reported in CIRS. To Be Approved First column. Only the officer and a few roles see reports here (see below). Approve Moving a report from To Be Approved to To Do. After that, the unit can see it (depending on the visibility setting). Visibility of CIRS Reports Unit setting: All (all staff of the unit see approved reports) or Management & CIRS officers. Copy Makes a new version of a report. The old version is switched to inactive. CIRRNET An external network where organisations share anonymous incident reports. A unit can forward approved CIRS reports to it. External reporting office An outside contact set up for the organisation who receives approved CIRS reports by email.

docs.title: Who uses it
docs.text: Role What they typically do here Professional, Management Report incidents and read approved reports to learn from them. At Unit without insight level, Management also processes and deactivates reports. Power User Appoints the unit's CIRS Officer (unit levels), processes the CIRS reports of the own unit and, at Unit without insight level, chooses the level and the visibility. To Be Approved) ✅ See approved, active reports of the own unit ✅ Process: edit, approve, move, copy, To-Do, guide, CIRRNET ❌ Deactivate / reactivate ❌ See inactive reports ✅ Download the overview ✅ Delete a report (normal version) ✅ Delete a report (audit-safe mode) ✅

  • Open Items and Process Guide: measures as To-Dos and guides.
  • Organisation & units: reporting level, Visibility of CIRS Reports, CIRRNET, external reporting office.

docs.title: Complaint Management
docs.text: In one sentence: Record complaints from patients, customers, suppliers or partners and follow each one up until it is resolved. Menu: Reporting module → tab Complaint Management · Status: Live

docs.title: What it is
docs.text:
When a patient or customer complains, the complaint must not get lost. Complaint Management lets any staff member write the complaint down, usually on behalf of the person who complained. The Complaint Officer then takes care of it.

Think of it as a complaints book that also tracks the answer. For each complaint you can record who was affected, how it reached you (e.g. phone or letter) and, if the person agrees, their contact details for a reply.

Complaint Management is the first tab: the reporting board always opens here.

This page adds the complaint details to the general Incident Reports page.

docs.title: Key terms
docs.text: Term Meaning Complainant The person who complained. Can be named with contact details, or left out. Affected Party Who the complaint is about or comes from: customer or patient, supplier, business client, or other. Transmitted via / Transmission Type How the complaint reached the unit. Responsible user A person named on the complaint to prepare the response. Complaint only visible to officer A switch on the complaint. When on, only the Complaint Officers, the Power User, the RiQS Administrator (and the writer) see it.

docs.title: Who uses it
docs.text: Role What they typically do here Professional, Management Record complaints they receive. At Unit without insight level, Management also processes complaints. Power User Appoints the unit's Complaint Officer (unit levels); processes complaints of the own unit; can restrict a complaint to officers. Administrator, Group Administrator Set up Complaint Management; appoint the officer (organisation level and unit with insight); process complaints at organisation level. Complaint Officer Reviews, assigns, answers and closes complaints.

docs.title: How it works
docs.text:
New Complaint → In Progress → Complete

Column What it means What moves it on New Complaint Recorded, not yet handled. The officer starts handling it and drags it to In Progress. In Progress Being handled: To-Dos, guides, response being prepared. Responsible users can write their response remarks now. Resolved: drag to Complete. Complete Closed. Can be dragged back to In Progress.

The form asks for: - Send anonymously (optional switch for the person writing the report). - Complaint Reason: Title and Description (both required), and keywords. - Affected Party: customer or patient, supplier, business client, or other. - Transmitted via and Transmission Type: how the complaint came in. - The complainant's contact details, or the choice to leave them out. When included: first name, last name and email are required; company and Phone are optional.

docs.title: How to record a complaint
docs.text:
Who can do this: Everyone except the RiQS Administrator. 1. Open Reporting module. The Complaint Management tab is already selected. 2. Click the create button. 3. Fill in Title and Description. Choose the Affected Party and how the complaint came in. 4. Either include the complainant's contact details or choose to leave them out. 5. Switch on Send anonymously if you do not want your own name shown. 6. Click Report.

Result: The complaint appears in New Complaint. By default the users of the unit can see it (see the table).

docs.title: How to make a complaint visible to everyone (or hide it again)
docs.text:
Who can do this: The Complaint Officer and the Power User. 1. Open the complaint. 2. Switch Complaint only visible to officer off to share it with the unit, or on to keep it with the officers. 3. Save.

Result: The complaint is shown to, or hidden from, the other users of the unit.

docs.title: How to handle a complaint
docs.text:
Who can do this: See "Process" in the table below. 1. Open the complaint and drag it to In Progress. 2. Use Create To Do or Attach Guide for the actions needed. 3. When everything is done, drag it to Complete.

Result: The complaint is closed. It can be reopened by dragging it back to In Progress.

docs.title: Rules to know
docs.text:
• The reporter can stay anonymous with Send anonymously. Separately, the complainant's contact details can be left out.
  • Only the Complaint Officer and the Power User can switch Complaint only visible to officer. When it is on, only the officers, the Power User, the RiQS Administrator and the writer see the complaint.
  • In units without insight, Group Administrators and Administrators do not see the complaints of other units of the organisation.
  • A responsible user can edit the response remarks only while the complaint is In Progress.
  • Complaints cannot be copied or moved to another board.
  • Delete. In audit-safe mode, only the RiQS Administrator can delete a complaint. Outside audit-safe mode, the officer can also delete; at Organizational level also the Group Administrator and Administrator, at unit level also the Power User.

docs.title: Employee Feedback
docs.text: In one sentence: Staff raise personal concerns, wishes or problems at work in confidence, and the Feedback Officer follows them up. Menu: Reporting module → tab Employee Feedback · Status: Live (one change planned, see below)

docs.title: What it is
docs.text:
Not every concern is an incident or an idea. Sometimes a person wants to say "my workload is too high" or "there is a conflict in our team". Employee Feedback is a confidential channel for exactly that.

Feedback is handled by the Feedback Officer. Besides the person who wrote it, only the officers and a few administrative roles can read it; Management and Professionals never see other people's feedback. The writer can limit a feedback to the officers only.

Older screens and documents may call this board "Another message" or "Employee Management".

This page adds the feedback details to the general Incident Reports page.

docs.title: Key terms
docs.text: Term Meaning Feedback A personal concern, wish or problem raised by a staff member. Implementation proposal The writer's own suggestion for how to solve it. Responsible for response The person named to answer the feedback. Feedback only visible to officer Switch on the feedback. On: the officers and the RiQS Administrator (and the writer) only. Off: also the Power User and the administrators who may see the unit's feedback (see the table).

docs.title: Who uses it
docs.text: Role What they typically do here Professional, Management, Power User Raise feedback. Power User Appoints the unit's Feedback Officer; reads and processes feedback at unit level. Management Downloads the overview when the unit uses Unit with insight. Administrator, Group Administrator Set up Employee Feedback; process feedback at organisation level. Feedback Officer Reviews, responds to and closes feedback.

docs.title: How it works
docs.text:
Assignment → In Progress → Completed

Column What it means What moves it on Assignment New feedback, waiting to be assigned. The content can still be updated. The officer assigns it and drags it to In Progress. In Progress Being handled. The responsible person can write response remarks. Resolved: drag to Completed. Completed Closed. Can be dragged back to In Progress.

The form asks for: - Send anonymously (optional). - Title and Short Description (both required). - An implementation proposal, keywords and attachments.

docs.title: How to give feedback
docs.text:
Who can do this: Everyone except the RiQS Administrator. At Unit without insight level, Group Administrators and Administrators cannot. 1. Open Reporting module and click Employee Feedback. 2. Click the create button. 3. Fill in the title and Short Description. Add your proposal if you have one. 4. Switch on Send anonymously if you wish. 5. Click Report.

Result: The feedback appears in Assignment. Only you, the officers and the roles in the table can see it. You receive a confirmation email.

docs.title: How to share feedback with the unit's management
docs.text:
Who can do this: The person who writes the feedback, when creating it (every role that can create feedback). Whether the officer may change it later is open (see Open questions). 1. Open the feedback. 2. Switch Feedback only visible to officer off. Save.

Result: The Power User and the administrators who may see the unit's feedback can now read it. Switch it on again to restrict it.

docs.title: How to handle feedback
docs.text:
Who can do this: See "Process" in the table below. 1. Open the feedback and drag it to In Progress. 2. Use Create To Do or Attach Guide if action is needed. 3. Drag it to Completed when it is resolved.

Result: The feedback is closed.

docs.title: Rules to know
docs.text:
• Feedback is never shown to all staff. Management and Professionals see only their own. The officers, the RiQS Administrator, the Power User (unit levels) and the Group Administrator and Administrator (organisation level and unit with insight) see the unit's feedback, unless it is officer-only.
  • The content of a feedback can only be updated while it is in Assignment.
  • A responsible person can edit response remarks only while it is In Progress.
  • Ideas requalified by the Ideas Officer arrive on this board and are officer-only. Their writer gets an email.
  • Only the RiQS Administrator can delete feedback.
  • Planned: the Feedback only visible to officer switch will move into the creation form, directly below Send anonymously, off by default. Then the writer decides who may read it (e.g. when reporting bullying). Today the switch is still on the feedback details.

docs.title: Fault Management
docs.text: In one sentence: Staff report broken or faulty devices, and the Fault Officer and the people responsible for the device get them fixed. Menu: Reporting module → tab Fault Management · Status: Live

docs.title: What it is
docs.text:
When a blood pressure monitor shows wrong values or a printer stops working, someone has to know about it and fix it. Fault Management is the unit's fault log.

A fault report points to a device from the Equipment module, so the officer immediately sees the device's details: serial number, location and maintenance dates. Faults are sorted into malfunction groups (for example "IT" or "Medical devices"), which the unit sets up in advance.

Faults are handled by the Fault Officer. The people responsible for the device in the Equipment module can also handle its faults.

This page adds the fault details to the general Incident Reports page.

docs.title: Key terms
docs.text: Term Meaning Fault A malfunction of a device or piece of equipment. Malfunction group A category of faults, set up per unit. Older documents call it a "fault group". Urgency Low, Medium, High or Critical. Contact Person Who to ask about the fault. Responsible for the device Users named as responsible for a device in the Equipment module. They can see, process and deactivate its faults and download the overview. Send fault only to officer Switch on the fault. When on, only the Fault Officers, the Power User and the RiQS Administrator (and the writer) see it.

docs.title: Who uses it
docs.text: Role What they typically do here Professional, Management, Power User Report faults. People responsible for a device Process and deactivate the faults of their device; download the overview. Power User Appoints the unit's Fault Officer; sets up malfunction groups; can restrict a fault to officers. Administrator, Group Administrator Set up Fault Management; appoint officers at organisation level; set up malfunction groups. Group Administrators also process and deactivate faults at organisation level; Administrators process them. Fault Officer Reviews, clears and closes faults; sets up malfunction groups.

docs.title: How it works
docs.text:
New Fault → Fault Clearance → Completed

Column What it means What moves it on New Fault Reported, not yet handled. The officer starts the repair and drags it to Fault Clearance. Fault Clearance Being fixed (To-Dos, guides, service partner). Fixed: drag to Completed. Completed Closed. Can be dragged back to Fault Clearance.

The form asks for: - Title and Description (both required). - Urgency, the device (Equipment), Malfunction group, Contact Person and Remarks.

The details also show the device's Serial Number, Internal Number, UDI Number, Location, Exact Location, and the Last Maintenance, Next Maintenance, Last Validation and Next Validation dates.

docs.title: How to report a fault
docs.text:
Who can do this: Everyone except the RiQS Administrator. At Unit without insight level, Group Administrators and Administrators cannot. 1. Open Reporting module and click Fault Management. 2. Click the create button. 3. Fill in Title and Description. Choose the device, the Urgency and the Malfunction group. 4. Click Report.

Result: The fault appears in New Fault. The officer and the people responsible for the device can handle it.

docs.title: How to set up malfunction groups
docs.text:
Who can do this: See "Malfunction groups" in the table below. 1. Open the unit's settings and its reporting configuration. 2. In Malfunction Group, click Add Malfunction group, enter a name and save. 3. Use the edit and active/inactive controls to change or switch off a group. 4. To reuse groups from another unit, use Clone malfunction group.

Result: The groups can be chosen when reporting a fault.

docs.title: How to restrict a fault to officers
docs.text:
Who can do this: The Fault Officer and the Power User. 1. Open the fault. 2. Switch on Send fault only to officer. Save.

Result: Only the officers, the Power User, the RiQS Administrator (and the writer) can see the fault.

docs.title: Rules to know
docs.text:
• Fault reports are never anonymous.
  • The unit setting Report visibility for fault management decides whether new faults are visible to all or restricted.
  • People responsible for the device can see, process and deactivate its faults and download the overview, even without the officer role.
  • Management and Professionals can manage malfunction groups only when they are Fault Officers. Cloning groups to another unit needs the organisation-level Fault Officer role (or an administrator).
  • A malfunction group that is already used in a fault report cannot be deleted; switch it off instead.
  • In units without insight, Group Administrators and Administrators do not see the unit's faults.
  • Only the RiQS Administrator can delete a fault report.

docs.title: Hint Management
docs.text: In one sentence: A safe whistleblowing channel where staff report serious wrongdoing, if they wish anonymously and to an external office. Menu: Reporting module → tab Hint Management · Status: Live

docs.title: What it is
docs.text:
Some problems are too sensitive for the normal channels: suspected fraud, harassment, data protection breaches, or a colleague breaking the rules. Hint Management is the organisation's whistleblowing channel for such "hints".

A hint goes to the Hint Officer of the organisation. The person reporting can stay anonymous. They can also choose to send the hint to an external reporting office, an outside contact the organisation has named (for example a lawyer or ombudsperson).

Unlike the other report types, Hint Management always works for the whole organisation: there is one Hint Officer team for all units.

This page adds the hint details to the general Incident Reports page.

docs.title: Key terms
docs.text: Term Meaning Hint A report of suspected wrongdoing or a serious problem. Type of hint The subject, e.g. Working Conditions, Occupational Safety, Suspected Fraud, Compliance Violation, Data Protection Violation, Discrimination or Harassment, IT Security, Patient Safety, Quality Deficiency. External reporting office An outside contact set up for the organisation. It receives hints by email and opens them through a link, seeing only the hints sent to it. I wish to report The part of the form where the reporter chooses whether the hint also goes to the external reporting office.

docs.title: Who uses it
docs.text: Role What they typically do here All staff Report hints. Administrator Appoints the Hint Officer, sets up the external reporting office, reads all hints of the organisation and downloads the overview. Power User Reads all hints of the organisation and downloads the overview. Group Administrator Appoints the Hint Officer and sets up the external reporting office. Hint Officer The only role that processes hints. Can also set up the external reporting office. External reporting office Receives and reads hints sent to it (outside RIQS, through a link).

docs.title: How it works
docs.text:
New Hint → In Process → Implemented

Column What it means What moves it on New Hint Received, not yet handled. The officer takes it up and drags it to In Process. In Process Being investigated; measures planned. Done: drag to Implemented. Implemented Closed, with the officer's Decision. Can be dragged back to In Process.

The form asks for: - Send anonymously (optional) and I wish to report (whether to include the external reporting office). - Hint Title and Description (both required). - Type of hint, Urgency, Incident date, Location, People involved, Measures taken, keywords and attachments.

In the details the officer records the Decision, next steps and planned measures, and whether the hint was Followed up message or Do not follow up message.

docs.title: How to report a hint
docs.text:
Who can do this: Everyone except the RiQS Administrator. 1. Open Reporting module and click Hint Management. 2. Click the create button. 3. Switch on Send anonymously if you do not want your name shown. 4. Under I wish to report, choose whether the hint should also go to the external reporting office. 5. Fill in Hint Title and Description, and the other fields you can. 6. Click Report.

Result: The hint appears in New Hint. The Hint Officers get an email. You get a confirmation email. If you chose the external office, it gets an email with a link.

docs.title: How to send a hint to the external office later
docs.text:
Who can do this: The Hint Officer. 1. Open the hint. 2. Switch on to the external reporting office. Save.

Result: The external reporting office gets an email with a link to the hint. This happens only once per hint.

docs.title: How to appoint the Hint Officer
docs.text:
Who can do this: RiQS Administrator, Group Administrator, Administrator. 1. Open Reporting module → Hint Management. 2. Click the officer button, pick Administrators, Power Users or Management users in Select user, and click Appoint.

Result: The chosen people are Hint Officers for the whole organisation.

docs.title: Rules to know
docs.text:
• Hint Management can only be set to Organizational.
  • Only the Hint Officer can process, move or deactivate hints. Administrators cannot.
  • Management and Professionals see only the hints they wrote themselves (and hints they got a To-Do on).
  • The external reporting office is set up for the organisation, together with the report types it receives. The RiQS Administrator, Group Administrator, Administrator and Hint Officer can set it up and change it.
  • Only the RiQS Administrator can delete a hint.

docs.title: Idea Management
docs.text: In one sentence: Staff suggest improvements, and the Ideas Officer decides on them and tracks them until they are put into practice. Menu: Reporting module → tab Idea Management · Status: Live

docs.title: What it is
docs.text:
The people doing the work often know best how to do it better. Idea Management is the unit's digital suggestion box. Anyone can post an idea, describe its benefit, and say who it would help.

The Ideas Officer reviews each idea, decides whether it will be implemented, and turns it into work with To-Dos and guides. If an "idea" is really a personal wish or concern, the officer can move it to Employee Feedback instead.

This page adds the idea details to the general Incident Reports page.

docs.title: Key terms
docs.text: Term Meaning Idea A suggestion for improvement. Benefit What the idea would improve. Target Group Who would profit from the idea. Decision The officer's verdict: idea implemented or not implemented. Requalify Moving an idea to the Employee Feedback board because it is really feedback. Done with the Feedback switch on the card.

docs.title: Who uses it
docs.text: Role What they typically do here Professional, Management, Power User Post ideas and read the ideas of the unit. Power User Appoints the unit's Ideas Officer (unit levels); processes and requalifies ideas at unit level; at Unit without insight level can also switch Idea Management on and choose the level. Administrator, Group Administrator Set up Idea Management; appoint officers at organisation level; process ideas at every level. Ideas Officer Reviews, decides, implements or requalifies ideas.

docs.title: How it works
docs.text:
New Idea → In Process → Implemented

Column What it means What moves it on New Idea Posted, not yet reviewed. The officer takes it up and drags it to In Process. In Process Being assessed or implemented (To-Dos, guides). Finished: drag to Implemented. Implemented Closed, with the officer's Decision. Can be dragged back to In Process.

The form asks for: - Send anonymously (optional). - Idea Title and Description (both required). - Benefit, Target Group, feasibility and resource requirements, keywords, attachments.

docs.title: How to post an idea
docs.text:
Who can do this: Everyone except the RiQS Administrator. 1. Open Reporting module and click Idea Management. 2. Click the create button. 3. Fill in Idea Title and Description. Add the benefit and target group if you can. 4. Switch on Send anonymously if you wish. 5. Click Report.

Result: The idea appears in New Idea. Other users of the unit can see it.

docs.title: How to requalify an idea as employee feedback
docs.text:
Who can do this: See "Requalify" in the table below. 1. Find the idea card on the board. 2. Switch on Feedback on the card.

Result: The card moves to the Employee Feedback board, in the matching column. It becomes visible to officers only. The person who posted it gets an email.

docs.title: How to record a decision
docs.text:
Who can do this: See "Process" in the table below. 1. Open the idea and set the Decision (implemented or not implemented). Save. 2. Drag the card to Implemented when it is finished.

Result: The idea is closed with its decision.

docs.title: Rules to know
docs.text:
• Ideas are visible to the whole unit by default (except in units without insight, where Group Administrators and Administrators do not see them).
  • The Feedback switch on the card is the only way to move a report to another board. The app offers no way to move it back.
  • Ideas cannot be copied.
  • Only the Ideas Officer (and, at Organizational level, the Group Administrator and Administrator) can deactivate ideas. The RiQS Administrator cannot process or deactivate ideas.
  • Delete. In audit-safe mode, only the RiQS Administrator can delete an idea. Outside audit-safe mode, at Organizational level the Group Administrator, Administrator and Ideas Officer can also delete.

docs.title: How RIQS is organised
docs.text: In one sentence: RIQS is built in layers: a group can hold several organisations, an organisation holds one or more units, and every user works in at least one unit.

docs.title: The building blocks
docs.text:
Group  (optional)
└── Organisation        e.g. "Medical Centre North Ltd."
    ├── Unit            e.g. "Practice Zurich"
    │   ├── Users
    │   └── Unit data   (documents, shift plans, tasks, equipment, reports …)
    └── Unit            e.g. "Practice Basel"
        └── …
Level What it is Example Group Several organisations that are managed together A chain that owns several companies Organisation The customer company. It holds the subscription, billing and organisation-wide settings "Medical Centre North Ltd." Unit One team, site or practice inside the organisation. Almost all daily work happens at unit level "Practice Zurich" User A person who logs in. Each user has one primary unit and may also have access to other units A nurse working in Zurich who sometimes helps in Basel

In some screens of the app, a unit is called a Client. They mean the same thing.

docs.title: Organisation level vs unit level
docs.text:
Most things in RIQS live inside one unit, for example a shift plan, a task list, a device or an incident report. Only the people of that unit (and admins above them) see it.

Some things can be set up at organisation level so that they apply to all units:

  • documents and folders in RiQS-Pedia that the whole organisation shares
  • officers who act for the whole organisation (for example a CIRS Officer for the organisation)
  • subscription, licences, AI tokens and storage, which the organisation can share out to units

Each module page explains which of its items can live at organisation level.

docs.title: Primary unit and switching units
docs.text:
• When you log in, RIQS opens your primary unit.
  • Administrators (RiQS Administrator, Group Administrator, Administrator) can use the unit switcher at the top of the screen to change to another unit at any time. They don't need to log in again.
  • Other users who belong to more than one unit choose the unit when they log in.
  • What you see (menu, data, buttons) always belongs to the unit you are currently in.

docs.title: Audit-safe mode
docs.text:
Some customers must keep a full, unchangeable record for audits. For them, RIQS can run in audit-safe mode:

  • In the regular version, authorised users can delete records.
  • In audit-safe mode, deleting is blocked for client users. Normally only the RiQS Administrator can delete. Users deactivate items instead, so the history is kept.

The permission tables on every module page show both cases where they differ.

docs.title: What decides what a user can see?
docs.text:
Three things together:

  1. Subscription. Is the module part of the organisation's package? If not, the menu entry is hidden for everyone.
  2. Role. What is the user allowed to do? See Roles & permissions.
  3. Assignment. Some items are only for specific people, for example a restricted document, an assigned task or a training someone was invited to.

docs.title: Roles & permissions
docs.text: In one sentence: Every user has one main role, which sets how much they can do. They can also hold function roles (such as "CIRS Officer"), which add rights for one special area.

docs.title: The six main roles
docs.text:
From most to least powerful:

Role Who is it? Scope In short RiQS Administrator The RIQS platform team All organisations Creates organisations, supports clients, and is the only role that can delete in audit-safe mode Group Administrator Client admin for a group of organisations All organisations in the group and their units Manages several organisations at once Administrator Client admin for one organisation Own organisation and all its units Sets up units, users, subscription and organisation-wide settings Power User Lead of a unit Own unit (or several, if given) Manages the unit: users, content, plans and officers Management Unit management Own unit Mostly reads and runs daily operations. Fewer setup rights than a Power User Professional Regular staff member Own unit Does the daily work: reads, fills in, completes and reports

Older names you may still hear: Professional was called Employee A. The role Employee B has been removed.

docs.title: Simple rule of thumb
docs.text:
• Set up and configure → Administrator / Power User
  • Plan and follow up → Power User / Management
  • Do and report → Professional (and everyone else)

docs.title: Function roles (added on top of a role)
docs.text:
A function role gives one person extra rights for one area without changing their main role. For example, a Professional can be the unit's Fault Officer.

docs.text:

docs.title: What is RIQS?
docs.text: In one sentence: RIQS is a web platform that helps an organisation run its daily quality and risk management in one place: documents, plans, tasks, checks, incident reports, equipment, training and surveys.

docs.title: The problem RIQS solves
docs.text:
Organisations such as medical practices, clinics and care facilities have to prove that they work safely and to a defined quality standard. Without a shared system, this work is usually spread across:

  • Word files and PDFs in personal folders and email
  • paper checklists and wall calendars for shifts and maintenance
  • spreadsheets for training, equipment and complaints
  • conversations that nobody can trace later

People then don't know which document is the official one. Tasks get forgotten, and audits become stressful.

RIQS brings all of this into one system. It has clear roles and permissions, approval steps, reminders and a traceable history.

docs.text:
Who Typical use Staff (Professionals) See their shifts and tasks, read documents, fill in forms and checklists, report incidents, take trainings and surveys Unit leads (Power Users, Management) Plan the unit's work, assign tasks, approve documents, follow up on reports Organisation admins (Administrators, Group Administrators) Set up units and users, manage the subscription, define organisation-wide rules Officers (e.g. CIRS Officer, Equipment Officer) Handle one special area for the unit or organisation RiQS Administrators (platform team) Create organisations, support clients, manage the platform

Read Roles & permissions for the details.

docs.title: Key ideas to remember
docs.text:
1. Everything belongs to a unit. A unit is one team or site, for example one practice. Units belong to an organisation. See How RIQS is organised.
  2. Your role decides what you see. Two people can open the same module and see different buttons.
  3. The subscription decides which modules exist. If a module isn't part of your organisation's subscription, it doesn't appear in the menu.
  4. Modules are connected. For example, a form stored in RiQS-Pedia can be used in a Process Guide, a shift checklist or an equipment check.
